Whether it's data strategy, governance, engineering, analytics, or AI, we work with our clients to turn data into real, impactful results. Our team is made up of friendly, hands-on experts who love solving problems and making a difference. The role
OakNorth's lending business is scaling across the UK and US, and we need a Business Development Representative to join our growing Commercial Strategy team.
Our next good deal should not depend on who happens to find us.
As a Business Development Representative, you own the front end of our lending pipeline. That means two things.

Generating new opportunities. You work hand in hand with Marketing, turning campaign themes, target segments and ideal customer profiles into live outreach: multi-touch sequences across email, phone and LinkedIn, follow-up on the demand our campaigns generate, and the account research that makes it land. The output is qualified meetings with the right people.
Qualifying inbound leads. You own inbound enquiries end to end: researching them, screening them, and routing them, within SLA, to the right Originator.

What you’ll do
Outbound
• Run marketing-led outbound campaigns. Take the segments, messaging and campaign themes Marketing develops and put them into market as multi-touch, multi-channel sequences, run at a consistent cadence.

• Research accounts and personalise. Understand a business and its situation well enough to earn a first conversation.

• Feed back on what is working. You are closest to the response (which messages land, which segments go quiet, which objections keep recurring). Campaign design gets better because you tell Marketing what you are seeing.

Inbound
• Work the demand Marketing generates. Content downloads, webinar and event registrations, website enquiries. You pick these up quickly, research them properly, and convert those that meet our criteria.

• Own the inbound queue. Qualify and route every inbound lead within SLA, with the research already done before it reaches an Originator.

Across both
• Qualify with rigour. Screen against our policies and credit appetite. Saying “this is not a good fit, and here is why” is as valuable here as saying yes.

• Nurture over time. Most businesses worth lending to are not ready today. Keep warm, useful relationships with prospects and referrers until they are.

• Keep the data clean. Accurate CRM records and weekly pipeline reporting. What you build gets reused in outreach across the bank.

• Work shoulder to shoulder with Originators. Take their feedback on lead quality seriously, and adjust how you work.

What this role is not
• It is not a closing role. You will not negotiate or sign facilities. You hand over to an Originator once a prospect is properly qualified.

• It is not a volume-dialling role. Hard-selling outreach damages our standing within the market.

• It is not a role that pays for activity. Booking a meeting is not the finish line.

The Profile
You are likely to be early in your career with some exposure to lending, credit or financial services. How you work matters more than the exact shape of your CV.
You will bring:
• Overall 1-4 years of experience in Sales/Business Development with prior experience working in a banking/fintech industry.

• Enough finance grounding to qualify a lead properly: you can hold a sensible conversation about how a business loan is structured and assessed, or you can learn that quickly and want to.

• Experience working to targets in an outbound role, and the resilience that takes. Outbound means hearing “no” far more often than yes, and we need you as sharp at the end of a campaign as at the start.

• Credibility with senior people. Originators need to take your leads seriously from early on, and prospects and advisers need to find you worth their time.

• Real organisational discipline. You keep records accurate and current without being chased.

• Clear, concise written English. Most of the first impressions you make will be in writing.

job_title: Director, Credit Risk – Cash Flow Lending
job_description:
ABOUT US
At OakNorth, we're on a mission to empower ambitious businesses and the communities they serve.
Since 2015, we've lent over $21 billion across the UK and US, helped create more than 58,000 new homes and 36,000 new jobs, and supported hundreds of thousands of personal savers — all while driving economic growth in the markets we serve.
We're an entrepreneurial, technology-led bank combining deep lending expertise with data, technology and AI to make better decisions and deliver a different experience for our customers.
ABOUT THE TEAM
• Our Credit Risk team plays a critical role in enabling OakNorth to support ambitious businesses while maintaining a high-quality lending portfolio.

• Working closely with Debt Finance Origination, Credit Analytics, Portfolio Management and Legal, the team brings together strong technical expertise, independent judgement and commercial thinking to support lending decisions.

• We're a collaborative, fast-moving team where people are encouraged to challenge, take ownership and find solutions rather than simply follow processes.

• ABOUT THE ROLE

• We're looking for an experienced Director, Credit Risk – Cash flow lending to play a key role in shaping credit decisions across OakNorth's UK lending portfolio.

• This is an opportunity for someone who combines deep technical credit expertise with strong commercial judgement and enjoys being close to the transactions, customers and decisions that matter.

• You'll work across a diverse range of lending opportunities, from established growing businesses to complex, structured and sponsor-backed transactions. Working closely with our Debt Finance, Credit Analytics and Portfolio Management teams, you'll provide independent challenge, help structure transactions and deliver high-quality credit recommendations to Credit Committee.

• Unlike more traditional banking environments, you'll have direct exposure to senior decision-makers, the opportunity to influence deals from an early stage and the ability to make a real impact on how we lend.

• We're looking for someone who is commercially minded, comfortable challenging the status quo and excited by the pace and ownership that comes with working at OakNorth.

WHAT YOU'LL DO
• Shape credit decisions: Lead the independent assessment and challenge of new lending opportunities across UK Trading Businesses, ensuring robust credit recommendations that balance risk and commercial opportunity.

• Influence deal structuring: Partner with Debt Finance Origination and Credit Analytics from an early stage to identify key risks, challenge assumptions and help structure transactions that work for both OakNorth and its customers.

• Drive high-quality Credit Committee discussions: Prepare and present clear, well-reasoned credit recommendations to Credit Committee, providing constructive challenge and supporting informed decision-making.

• Assess complex transactions: Evaluate a broad range of cash-flow lending, acquisition finance, leveraged and sponsor-backed transactions, applying strong financial analysis and credit judgement.

• Engage directly with customers: Work alongside origination teams in customer discussions, providing an early view on credit appetite, transaction structure and potential risks.

• Protect portfolio quality: Work closely with Portfolio Management on existing exposures, including loan increases, extensions, covenant resets, restructurings and emerging risks.

• Support transaction execution: Review term sheets, security structures and key legal documentation, working closely with Legal and Loan Execution teams to ensure appropriate risk protections.

• Provide independent judgement: Bring a balanced, pragmatic approach to credit risk, knowing when to support a transaction, when to challenge and when to recommend declining an opportunity.

• Help shape how we work: Contribute to the continued development of our credit risk capabilities, using data, technology and AI to improve the quality and efficiency of credit assessment and decision-making.

YOU'LL BE A GREAT FIT IF YOU HAVE…
• Minimum 10 years' experience in corporate or commercial credit risk, ideally within a bank, challenger bank or specialist lending institution.

• Strong understanding of UK cash-flow lending, with experience assessing complex corporate transactions, including acquisition finance, leveraged finance, M&A, MBO/MBI and sponsor-backed lending.

• Excellent financial analysis skills, including the ability to assess business models, cash-flow forecasts, debt capacity, covenant structures and downside scenarios.

• A strong track record of exercising independent credit judgement, challenging deal structures and influencing senior credit decisions.

• Experience preparing and presenting complex credit recommendations to senior Credit Committees, with the confidence to challenge proposals and engage with senior stakeholders.

• Strong understanding of credit risk frameworks, including covenant setting, portfolio risk management and key credit risk measures such as RWA, PD and LGD.

• Commercial awareness and the ability to balance disciplined risk management with supporting ambitious businesses.

• Strong communication, negotiation and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build effective relationships across origination, credit and wider business teams.

• A pragmatic, entrepreneurial mindset — someone who can cut through complexity, take ownership and operate effectively in a fast-moving environment.

• An interest in how technology, data and AI can improve credit risk management and lending decisions.

NICE TO HAVE
• Experience across sectors such as healthcare, hospitality and leisure, manufacturing, financial intermediaries or other specialist lending markets.

• Exposure to restructuring, recoveries or managing complex credit situations.

• Experience working directly with business owners, management teams, private equity sponsors or financial advisers.

WHY OAKNORTH?
At OakNorth, you'll have the opportunity to work on meaningful, complex lending transactions without the layers of bureaucracy often associated with larger institutions.
You'll be part of a business that values independent thinking, commercial judgement and people who take ownership. We move quickly, challenge conventional approaches and use technology and AI to continually improve how we work.
As we continue to grow, you'll have the opportunity to influence not just individual transactions, but how we approach lending and risk management more broadly.
If you're an experienced credit professional looking for greater ownership, exposure to senior decision-makers and the opportunity to make a real impact, we'd love to hear from you.

WHAT WE OFFER
• Equity — we want everyone to have a stake in the business so our interests are aligned

• 25 days holiday plus personalised benefits — opt in to what matters to you

• Subsidised private medical insurance with Bupa

• Enhanced maternity and paternity leave

• Wellbeing and social events, plus in-house Barista Bar in the London office

• Volunteering time off to support causes that matter to you

• Salary sacrifice schemes — cycle to work, nursery, gym, and electric car scheme

ABOUT US
At OakNorth, we’re on a mission to empower ambitious businesses and the communities they serve. Since 2015, we’ve lent over $21 billion across the UK and US, helped create more than 58,000 new homes and 36,000 new jobs, and supported hundreds of thousands of personal savers — all while driving economic growth in the markets we serve.
We’re an entrepreneurial, technology-led bank, combining deep lending expertise with data, technology and AI to make better decisions and deliver a different experience for our customers.
THE ROLE
Working directly with OakNorth's Chief Lending Officer and the broader lending team, you will be the driver for how we scale our UK and US lending businesses.
You’ll operate across every lending function and work directly with senior leadership - the connective tissue between the lending team and the rest of the business - with a seat at the table on strategy and board-level planning.
You will identify the biggest opportunities and constraints, turn strategy into clear plans and both lead and support delivery across key initiatives.
This is a broad, hands-on mandate for someone who owns problems, builds solutions and gets things done.

WHAT YOU'LL DO
Drive the lending roadmap
• Translate our lending priorities and strategy into an executable roadmap across the UK and US in support of our scaling mandate
• Partner with lending leadership to set and align OKRs, dovetailing into the Monthly Business Reviews, Quarterly Business Reviews, and strategic planning operating rhythm

• Own the roadmap for our highest priority strategy and operational initiatives - including growth bets into new sectors and geographies

Build the commercial engine
• Own and strengthen the commercial engine and our sales operation processes across the funnel, with the overall goal of widening top of funnel and improving conversion rates
• Own the commercial operating model, including the agenda on recruitment, org design, capability, and our capacity model

• Improve the end-to-end lending journey and build scalable, efficient processes, with an emphasis on where we need human touchpoints versus technology, automation and AI

• Manage a small team across marketing, revenue operations and sales enablement

THE PROFILE
We are open on background. You may have worked as an Operating Partner, Chief of Staff, Strategy & Operations leader, business builder or general manager. How you think and operate matters most.
You will bring:
• A track record of leading complex, cross-functional initiatives from idea to outcome.

• A strong systems thinker with sound commercial judgement and analytical ability.

• Enough commercial and credit fluency to earn credibility with senior dealmakers and engage seriously with how deals are originated, structured and underwritten.

• The ability to move comfortably between strategy and operational detail.

• An entrepreneurial approach and confidence building without a playbook.

• High energy, low ego and a bias for action.

• Comfort with ambiguity, pace and accountability.

• Strong preference for experience in financial services - banking, private equity, a credit fund or similar

Written by Nicole Treacy

Location: Peterborough I Salary: Dependant on experience

We are looking for an experienced Automation Engineer to join our Technology team in Peterborough.

This is a hands-on engineering role where you’ll design, develop, test and commission the control software behind our robotic and automated machinery solutions.

You’ll work primarily with Beckhoff TwinCAT 3 and Structured Text, developing robust, maintainable machine-control software and integrating PLCs with robotics, drives, vision systems, sensors, safety systems and other industrial equipment.

You won’t be working in isolation. You’ll be part of a multi-disciplined engineering environment, working alongside Project, Electrical, Mechanical, Robotics, Vision and Software Engineers to take automation solutions from development and testing through to commissioning on customer sites.

As OAL continues to grow, there will also be the opportunity to take increasing ownership of automation delivery and develop your capability through collaboration and knowledge sharing across the engineering team.

What you’ll be doing

Your role will include:

- Developing, maintaining and testing PLC and machine-control software using Beckhoff TwinCAT 3

- Programming using IEC 61131-3 Structured Text and structured/object-oriented programming principles

- Developing reusable, readable and maintainable automation software

- Integrating PLCs, robots, drives, vision systems, sensors, safety systems and other industrial equipment

- Developing and supporting HMI and Web Visualisation solutions

- Taking part in factory acceptance testing, system integration and validation

- Commissioning, troubleshooting and optimising systems at customer sites

- Working collaboratively on design reviews, software reviews and technical problem solving

- Contributing to reusable software libraries, code reviews and automation standards

- Producing clear technical, testing and commissioning documentation

- Supporting continuous improvement and knowledge sharing across OAL’s automation capability

The role includes travel to customer sites for installation, commissioning and support when required.

What we’re looking for

We’re looking for someone with a strong industrial automation background who is comfortable getting involved across the full lifecycle of an automation project.

You’ll ideally have:

- Proven experience developing automation software using Beckhoff TwinCAT 3

- Strong IEC 61131-3 Structured Text programming capability

- Experience using structured and object-oriented programming techniques

- Practical experience working with robotics and/or automated machinery

- Experience integrating PLC control with drives, sensors, actuators and other field equipment

- HMI and/or Web Visualisation development experience

- Strong commissioning, fault-finding and problem-solving skills

- Experience working within multi-disciplined engineering teams

- Good communication skills and the confidence to work with colleagues, suppliers and customers

- A willingness to travel to customer sites when required

- A full UK driving licence

Experience with KUKA robotics, Beckhoff TwinSAFE, EtherCAT, PROFINET, EtherNet/IP, OPC UA, Azure DevOps or Git would be an advantage, as would experience within food, beverage, packaging, palletising or other high-throughput automated production environments.

Why OAL?

At OAL, you’ll be working on real-world automation projects where the software you develop directly controls complex robotic and automated machinery.

We’re continuing to grow our engineering capability, which means this is an opportunity to join a business where you can contribute technically, share ideas and help shape how we develop and standardise our automation platforms.

We’re looking for engineers who enjoy solving problems, working collaboratively and taking ownership – people who want to build automation that works reliably in the real world, not just on a test bench.

Interested? Apply now to join the OAL team in Peterborough.

Important information

- This is an office-based role so applicants must be able to commute to our offices in Peterborough.

- Applicants must have the right to work in the UK without requiring employer sponsorship. Unfortunately, OAL is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position.

OAL is an equal opportunities employer and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified candidates.

📍 Location: Peterborough, PE2 6YN | Up to £45k (Subject to Experience) | Full-Time, Permanent

The software you build this month might prevent a product recall. Next month it might run a robotic cell.

OAL's software engineers work across compliance, vision, robotics and traceability systems for UK food manufacturers. One project might be a label verification system for a major retailer. The next might be software for a robotic palletising cell, a vision inspection system catching defects on apples, or a traceability platform tracking every ingredient for your favourite loaf of bread from intake to dispatch. You develop them at OAL's Peterborough base, deploy them at customer sites and support them once they are running.

This is not a pure desk role. You will write code, but you will also travel to factories to commission what you have built, support field engineers remotely, and pick up customer support tickets to SLA targets. Expect a mix of development, deployment and support throughout the year.

Develop software to control advanced robotic food manufacturing systems

Your skills probably already fit

- Languages and frameworks: .NET, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Entity Framework, VB6
- Platforms: Inductive Automation's Ignition (SCADA/MES), Azure DevOps
- Databases: MSSQL, SQL Server
- Industrial awareness: familiarity with PLCs (Rockwell or Beckhoff), machine vision systems, or robotic system integration
- Ways of working: Agile methodologies, version control, structured documentation

You do not need all of these, and you do not need food manufacturing experience. If you are strong in some areas and willing to learn the rest, that works. What matters is clean code and taking responsibility for what you deliver.

What we expect, and what you get

You own the quality of what you deliver. The work is structured: defined processes, technical reviews, proper version control. You will travel to customer sites for deployments. Support is part of the role, and you need to be comfortable switching between planned development and reactive tickets.

In return: software running on real production lines, a broad technical stack spanning SCADA, databases, PLC integration, machine vision and robotics, variety across customers and sites, and progression based on what you deliver.

What we are looking for

- At least 3 years of experience in software development
- Degree in Computer Science, IT or a related field
- Experience with at least some of: .NET, JavaScript, MSSQL, Ignition, PLC integration
- Full UK driving licence and willing to travel to customer sites across the UK

We are on a mission to become the leading international force in residential property management. What we do matters to millions of people in their everyday lives.
Residential real estate is the world’s largest asset class, and for most families, buying a home is the single biggest financial decision they will ever make. For too long, residential property management has fallen short of homeowners' and residents' expectations, and the industry is ready for change. Odevo was formed to make that change happen.
In just six years, Odevo has grown more than 70-fold, establishing us as the leading international player. We are more than 14,000 people across the US, the UK, the Nordics, Germany, Spain, Portugal, Mexico, and Italy building Odevo. Together, we aspire to break new ground through innovation and cultivate a workplace where we help each other succeed, where ideas matter more than titles, and where kindness is a strength.
By combining the power of people and technology, we set a new standard for how homes are managed. Our technology-enabled services simplify living for residents and create a better experience for property owners and boards.
Our ambition is to continue our fast-growing journey through new customers, service expansion, and by partnering with great companies that share our mindset and ambition, both in existing and new markets.
As we continue to grow, we stay true to who we are, challenge unnecessary bureaucracy, and keep decision-making close to our customers.
If you share our mindset and ambition, we’d love you to join us and help accelerate our mission together.
About the role
We’re seeking a UX Designer to shape the future of proptech for the UK market. This is a unique opportunity to join an industry still in an early stage of digital maturity, where you can have a significant impact. We see customer experience as a critical differentiator and an important part of our ambition to transform the global property management industry. You’ll join a global design team led by the Head of Design in Sweden, primarily supporting UK product teams. You’ll work closely with product managers, subject matter experts, stakeholders, and engineers, mainly in the UK. You will also collaborate with the global design team to strengthen design operations, evolve design systems, raise CX maturity, and support knowledge sharing across all our markets (UK, Europe, US and Mexico). As part of this role, you will shape both intuitive customer-facing experiences and complex internal property management employee workflows.
We are actively exploring how AI can improve both the products we build and the way we build them. We are looking for someone with practical experience applying AI who sees AI fluency as a way of working across all aspects of design—using it responsibly to work faster, accelerate learning, improve quality, and strengthen communication and influence, while applying strong human judgement throughout.
Core responsibilities
Alongside the core design responsibilities below, help define and implement AI-driven ways of working across design and product development. Partner with product managers and engineers to establish how designers, developers, and AI agents collaborate throughout the development lifecycle, using design artefacts, specifications, and workflows to guide and validate AI-driven development.
• User Research and Discovery — Plan and lead interviews, observations, and usability testing to uncover user needs, behaviours, pain points, and opportunities.

• Service Design — Create journey maps, service blueprints, personas, and other artefacts to build a shared understanding of users and the end-to-end service experience.

• Interaction & Visual Design — Translate insights into user flows, wireframes, prototypes, and high-quality design solutions. Apply and evolve visual identities where needed.

• Design Systems, Accessibility & Implementation Guidance — Collaborate with front-end developers to maintain design libraries, components, and patterns. Define component rules, accessibility requirements, and interaction principles to support consistent, high-quality implementation by AI agents.

• Design Validation — Communicate design rationale and evaluate solutions through usability testing, user feedback, behavioural data, and outcome metrics.

• Cross-functional Collaboration — Work with product managers, engineers, business analysts, and stakeholders to align solutions with user needs, business goals, technical feasibility, and product strategy.

• Design for Multiple User Groups — Create intuitive customer-facing services for clients and residents, and efficient internal tools tailored to expert users, including property managers, accountants, and on-site staff.

Who you are
You are genuinely interested in understanding people’s needs, behaviours, and motivations, and use that insight to shape services that deliver real value. You combine strong design craft with systems thinking and can move comfortably between user needs, business outcomes, service journeys, and detailed interaction design. You strive for quality, value collaboration over prestige, and enjoy contributing to a strong team culture. You turn research insights and design rationale into shared understanding, helping teams and stakeholders translate that understanding into action. You are curious about emerging technologies and excited by how AI is changing both digital products and product development. You combine strong design judgement with a willingness to experiment with new ways of working, while ensuring that user needs, trust, usability, and quality remain at the center of every decision.
You are also comfortable working in ambiguity and in an organisation where design and UX practices are not yet fully established—helping teams build user-centred ways of working and shape solutions where user needs, technology, and business opportunities are still emerging.
Experience and qualifications
• 3-5 years’ experience as a UX Designer, Product Designer, or in a similar role, working on complex digital products.

• Strong experience designing web and mobile experiences, including complex workflows and efficiency-focused tools, with solid grounding in UX research, service design, and interaction design.

• Experience working in agile, cross-functional product teams.

• Practical experience using Figma and code for design, prototyping, and design systems. Ability to translate design intent into clear specifications and reusable guidance for AI agents.

• Hands-on experience applying AI across product development, from research and ideation to prototyping, specification, validation, and AI-agent implementation.

• Design principles for AI-supported experiences, including transparency, trust, explainability, error handling, and human oversight.

• A bachelor’s degree in design, HCI, behavioural science, or related field.

OEG Job Advert - Commercial Manager
 Company Overview
 OEG is a leading energy solutions business, providing mission-critical infrastructure assets and services to the global offshore energy industry. Through our specialist divisions - topside, marine, subsea, logistics and industrials, we are a pivotal link in the global offshore energy project chain, ensuring our customers’ projects are delivered safely, reliably and efficiently.
 Location
 • United Kingdom.
 • Open to candidates across the United Kingdom, with a preference for those based in Liverpool.
 Core Purpose
 • Support the growth of the Subsea Division by identifying new opportunities, engaging with prospective and existing clients, and contributing to the execution of the divisional business development strategy.
 • Operating under the Commercial Director, this role is accountable for managing client relationships, developing commercial opportunities, defining win strategies and leading commercial discussions from tender submission through to contract award, in close collaboration with Tendering and Contract Management.
 Key Responsibilities and Accountabilities
 • Identify and develop new business opportunities in existing and emerging markets within the subsea and offshore energy sectors.
 • Build and maintain strong client relationships, acting as a point of contact and promoting the company’s capabilities.
 • Collaborate closely with commercial and operational teams to implement strategic initiatives and meet commercial targets.
 • Conduct market research and competitor analysis to identify trends, gaps, and potential areas of growth.
 • Prepare and deliver client presentations, proposals, and capability statements tailored to specific customer needs.
 • Maintain and update CRM systems with opportunity and contact information, ensuring accuracy in pipeline reporting.
 • Lead the development of opportunity-specific win strategies and commercial positioning, working closely with Tendering and relevant internal stakeholders.
 • Act as the commercial opportunity owner, ensuring effective coordination with Tendering throughout the bid process and alignment between client requirements, commercial strategy and proposed solutions.
 • Take ownership of post-submission client engagement, including proposal follow-up, commercial clarifications and negotiations, through to contract award.
 • Coordinate and support client negotiations in close collaboration with the Contract Specialist, who leads contractual negotiations and ensures alignment with approved contractual positions.
 • Retain overall commercial ownership of opportunities throughout the negotiation process, ensuring alignment between client expectations, commercial objectives and contractual outcomes.
 • Drive opportunities towards successful contract award, ensuring timely resolution of outstanding commercial matters and alignment with divisional revenue and profitability objectives.
 • Support Bid/No-Bid decisions and tender reviews by providing client intelligence, commercial positioning and recommendations.
 • Support the formal contract handover to Project Management, ensuring agreed commercial commitments and client expectations are clearly communicated.
 • Attend relevant industry events, trade shows, and conferences to represent the Subsea Division and build networks.
 • Contribute to marketing and promotional activities in partnership with the central marketing team.
 • Provide regular performance and market updates to the Commercial Director.
 • Uphold and promote OEG’s QHSE policies and business values.
 QHSE Responsibilities 
 To have a general understanding of the areas of our QHSE Management System and OEG’s QHSE aims and objectives that are relevant to the role.
 Comply with the requirements of OEG Energy Group Policies and the responsibilities within the wider QHSE Management System.
 Promoting:

Take a customer's sensor and make it work on Scout: mounted, wired, powered, coded and proven at sea.

Onodrim is building Europe's largest defence and industrial platform. We acquire specialist manufacturers in critical defence and dual-use supply chains, then invest behind their growth with capital, technology and operating know-how.
The companies we buy are usually excellent at what they make and under-invested in selling it. They have a handful of long-standing customers, a reputation inside a narrow circle, but no clear focus on finding the next programme. The Business Development Lead for Aerospace and Defence changes that. You'll own top-line growth for our portfolio companies in aerospace and defence, starting with the acquisitions we have already made in that space: work out where the demand is, get in front of the people who control it, and bring back signed business.
This is a sales role, and a self-directed one. You'll come with your own view on how to grow the business and the drive to go and test it – with ministries and procurement agencies, armed forces, primes and tier-one integrators, and the partners who can open doors. You'll represent Onodrim and its companies externally, at a level where what you say carries weight, and you'll be measured on what you close.
What you'll do
Build the growth plan. For each portfolio company in your area, work out where the addressable demand is – programmes, platforms, customers, geographies – and write a plan with targets, priorities and a pipeline to get there.
Open doors. Build and work relationships with ministries of defence, procurement agencies, armed-forces users, primes, tier-one integrators and partners across Europe; get the company into the conversations and tenders it is currently missing.
Own the pipeline. Qualify opportunities hard, run them through the sales cycle – capture plan, proposal, negotiation, contract – and keep an honest, current forecast.
Close. Bring in signed business and be accountable for bookings against the plan.
Represent the company. Speak for Onodrim and its portfolio companies at conferences, industry bodies, customer briefings and in the press where appropriate, with the discretion the sector requires.
Shape the offer. Take what you hear from customers back into product, pricing and positioning decisions with the company's leadership and our operators; make sure what is sold can be delivered.
Run proposals. Lead or coordinate responses to RFIs, RFPs and framework tenders, including the teaming, pricing and compliance work behind them.
Work the partner channel. Build teaming and distribution arrangements with primes and complementary suppliers where they get us to customers faster than going direct.
Inform what we buy next. Feed market, customer and competitor intelligence to the deal team and the leadership: where demand is going, which capabilities customers are missing, which companies they wish existed.
Build the function. Put the basics in place – CRM, pipeline reviews, capture process – at companies that have never had them, and help their own teams sell.

About the role
Onodrim is building Europe's largest defence and industrial platform. We acquire specialist manufacturers in critical defence and dual-use supply chains, then invest behind their growth with capital, technology and operating know-how.
A company that is buying manufacturers, launching products, entering new countries and growing its own team at the same time generates problems faster than any function can own them. The Business Operations and Strategy Lead is the person who takes those problems. You'll work across the whole business – with the leadership team, the deal team, engineering, finance, legal and the people running our portfolio companies – to get things done: design how something new should work, stand it up, unblock what is stuck, and use the company's own data to decide how it should run.
The work changes every few months. Examples of what you might take on:
Designing the operating model for a new market or region launch
Building workforce and capacity models to keep pace with rapid growth
Negotiating a first-of-its-kind partnership
Standing up an operational team for a new product line
Using internal data to inform key decisions about how the company runs

Take the problem nobody owns. Pick up the cross-functional questions that fall between teams – a new entity, a new process, a decision that has stalled – and drive them to a result.
Design how new things work. Define the operating model for a new region, product line, function or partnership: who does what, how it is governed, what it costs, what has to be true for it to work.

Unblock the organisation. Find where decisions, approvals, handoffs and tools slow the company down; fix them, and remove process rather than add it wherever possible.
Build the models. Workforce and capacity plans, scenario models for growth and integration, unit economics for a new line – built from the company's own data and used to make real decisions.

Run the operating rhythm. Support the leadership team's planning and review cycle – objectives, metrics, business reviews – so the company knows how it is doing and decides quickly.
Bring data to decisions. Pull together internal data from finance, operations, people and the portfolio companies into analyses the leadership team can act on, and make the data easier to get next time.
Support integration. Take cross-functional workstreams in the integration of acquired companies – entity set-up, shared services, reporting – where no single function owns them.

5+ years in roles where you made things happen across an organisation: business operations, chief of staff, strategy and operations at a scale-up, management consulting with real implementation, or operations leadership inside a growing company.
A track record of standing something up from nothing – a team, a function, a process, an entity – and leaving it running.

Comfort with ambiguity: you have been handed a one-line brief and turned it into a plan and a result, more than once.

Exposure to manufacturing, defence or another industrial sector where operations are physical and regulated.

Time in a start-up or small team where you did whatever the company needed.

About the role
Onodrim is building Europe's largest defence and industrial platform. We acquire specialist manufacturers in critical defence and dual-use supply chains, then invest behind their growth with capital, technology and operating know-how.
Forward Deployed Operators are Onodrim's people on the ground. You'll embed inside the companies we acquire – plants, lines and the offices that run them – and own one part of making them grow. For this role, that part is the finance.
The manufacturers we buy are often decades old and owner-run, with a bookkeeper, an external accountant, a chart of accounts that has grown by accretion, limited cash management and product costs recalculations. The Forward Deployed Operator for Finance walks in after an acquisition and builds the real picture: what each product actually costs, where cash is tied up in inventory and receivables, what the plant's numbers look like against budget and prior years, and what it would take to close the books in days rather than weeks. This is not a head-office finance job. One week you'll be rebuilding the costing model with the production planner; the next, setting up a monthly close with the bookkeeper and mapping the ledger to the group chart of accounts; the next, building the business case for a capex decision with the Production Engineering Operator and the plant director. It is what a finance lead does for a company, done repeatedly across our portfolio.
What you'll do
Diagnose the finance function. In the first weeks on site, rebuild the P&L, balance sheet and cash position from the ledger, assess the people, processes and tools, and find where the numbers are wrong, late or missing.
Get product costs right. Build or rebuild product and process costing with production – materials, labour, overhead, scrap, capacity – so the company knows what it makes money on and prices accordingly.
Release working capital. Analyse inventory, receivables and payables; set targets with the plant and procurement; put the routines in place to hold them.
Stand up the close. Design and run a fast, reliable month-end close – reconciliations, accruals, inventory valuation, intercompany – and get it to the group's cadence within the first quarter.
Build the reporting. Set up monthly management reporting and KPIs for the company's leadership; analyse results against budget and prior periods and explain the variances in plain terms.
Forecast cash and results. Build and maintain rolling cash and P&L forecasts and the scenarios behind capacity, hiring and capex decisions.
Connect to the group. Map the ledger to the group chart of accounts, apply group accounting policies and IFRS adjustments locally.
Upgrade the systems. Assess the ERP, accounting and reporting tools in use; fix configuration, replace spreadsheets where it pays, and work with the Software Engineering Operator on the data behind the numbers.

About the role
Onodrim is building Europe's largest defence and industrial platform. We acquire specialist manufacturers in critical defence and dual-use supply chains, then invest behind their growth with capital, technology and operating know-how.
Forward Deployed Operators are Onodrim's people on the ground. You'll embed inside the companies we acquire – plants, lines and the offices that run them – and own one part of making them grow. For this role, that part is the people.

Experience hiring for industrial and technical roles – operators, technicians, engineers, plant management – in tight labour markets.

Clear, direct communication in English, written and spoken.

About the role

You'll work alongside our Forward Deployed Operators, who diagnose where a plant loses value on the floor and in the back office. Build what's missing. Write custom code – services, integrations, internal tools, data models – where off-the-shelf products fall short, and ship it into live production environments.
Integrate the stack. Connect ERP, MES, SCADA, PLM, quality and finance systems so data flows end to end; replace the spreadsheets and manual handoffs that bridge them today.

Ship for Onodrim itself. Build and run the internal tooling the platform needs – across finance, operations, security and portfolio reporting – with the same standards as sub-co work.

A degree in computer science, software engineering or a closely related technical discipline – or an equivalent track record of shipped software.
At least 2–4 years' experience as a software engineer, with at least some of it spent deploying software to real users: forward deployed, solutions or implementation engineering, or product engineering with direct customer contact.
A builder at heart: you'd rather ship something imperfect this week and improve it than design the perfect system for next quarter.
Strong general-purpose engineering skills – you're fluent in at least one of Python, TypeScript or Java, write SQL without thinking about it, and can pick up a new language, API or platform in days.
Comfort with data: ingesting messy exports from ERP, MES and quality systems, modelling them and producing something people trust.
Good judgement on build vs. buy vs. configure – and the willingness to use an existing tool when it does the job.
Credibility with non-engineers: you can sit with a shift supervisor or a controller, understand their world, and explain what you're building in their terms.
Clear, direct communication in English, written and spoken.
Willingness to travel extensively and spend extended periods at portfolio companies across Europe.
Right to work in the UK, Switzerland or the EU.
Nice to have
We operate our business in English but fluency in one or more additional European languages is hugely helpful – German or Italian especially valuable.
Experience in or around manufacturing, defence, logistics or another industrial environment where the software meets physical operations.
Prior forward deployed, solutions or consulting-style engineering where you owned the outcome at the client, not just the code.
Familiarity with industrial data and protocols: OPC UA, PLC exports, machine logs, time-series data.
Experience building LLM-backed tools on top of enterprise data, and a view on where they help and where they don't.
An entrepreneurial streak: a start-up you ran, a product you shipped on the side, or a stint in a small team where you did whatever the problem needed.

job_title: Head of Information and Cyber Security
job_description:
About the role
Onodrim is building Europe's largest defence and industrial platform. We acquire specialist manufacturers in critical defence and dual-use supply chains, then invest behind their growth with capital, technology and operating know-how.
The Head of Information Security owns security across the whole platform: Onodrim itself and every company we acquire. A defence platform with investor backing is a target for state actors, criminal groups and everyone in between. Our acquired companies arrive with their own networks, their own IT people and their own history – and they build things that must not leak. You'll set the standard, make it real at each site, and be the person who picks up the phone when something goes wrong.
This is a hands-on role. Onodrim itself is a small, young company. You'll take over its security from the CTO on day one and run it yourself, then extend it to sub-cos that look nothing like it: on-premise ERP, shop-floor networks, machine controllers, and a plant IT administrator who has done everything alone for fifteen years.
Alongside security you'll own the basics of corporate IT for Onodrim – identity and access, devices, SaaS administration, onboarding and offboarding – and set the model for how sub-co IT is run and, where it makes sense, consolidated.
What you'll do
Own the security programme. Set Onodrim's security strategy, standards and risk appetite.
Run Onodrim's own estate. Operate and harden identity and access, endpoint management, the productivity suite and the rest of the SaaS stack.
Secure the sub-cos. Within the first weeks after each acquisition, assess the company's security posture, fix what is urgent, and bring it onto the platform standard over time – without disrupting production.
Support the deal team. Run security and IT due diligence on acquisition targets: what they run, what has happened to them, what it will cost to fix, and what could kill the deal.
Protect the shop floor. Bring OT and industrial control systems into scope: network segmentation, machine access, vendor remote access, and the gap between the IT and OT teams.
Lead incident response. Own detection, response and recovery across the platform; run tabletop exercises; be the escalation point when something happens at 02:00 at a sub-co.
Get and keep the certifications that unlock business. Drive ISO 27001, NIS2 readiness and the national defence-industry and classified-information requirements (e.g. BSI, Facility Security Clearance equivalents) that our customers and partners demand, and support export-control compliance (ITAR/EAR, EU dual-use) on the technical side.

Run corporate IT for the Top-Co. Own device procurement and lifecycle, joiner/mover/leaver, SaaS licensing and administration, and first-line support – either directly or through a managed provider you select and manage.
Set the sub-co IT model. Decide what gets consolidated (identity, email, endpoint, backup), what stays local, and how plant IT teams plug into the platform.
Build the function. Hire and manage security and IT staff as the platform grows; select and manage MSSPs, MDR providers and auditors in the meantime.
Make security usable. Write policies people can follow, train staff, and design controls that a 20-person company and a 500-person manufacturer can both live with.
What you'll bring
5+ years in information security, with at least 2 in a role where you owned the programme – Head of Security, CISO or deputy at a company of similar or larger scale, or equivalent responsibility in government, military or a defence contractor.
Deep hands-on experience with a modern cloud-native stack: an enterprise identity provider, Apple and Windows endpoint management, cloud productivity-suite administration, and SaaS security.
Experience securing on-premise and industrial environments – Windows domains, legacy ERP, shop-floor networks, OT/ICS – not only cloud.
A track record of leading incident response, including at least one serious incident you can talk through end to end.
Working knowledge of the European regulatory landscape for defence and critical industry: NIS2, ISO 27001, GDPR, export control (EU dual-use, ITAR/EAR) and national classified-information regimes.
Experience taking a company through ISO 27001 or an equivalent certification from scratch.
Comfort with corporate IT: you have run or managed device fleets, SaaS administration and onboarding, and are willing to do it yourself at a small company.
Strong judgement on build vs. buy vs. outsource – you know when to run it yourself and when to bring in an MSSP, MDR provider or auditor.
Clear, direct communication in English, written and spoken, with the ability to present risk to a board and explain controls to a plant administrator.
Willingness to travel regularly to across Europe, with extended time on site after each acquisition.
Right to work in the UK, Switzerland or the EU, and eligibility for a national security clearance in at least one of our operating countries.
Nice to have
We operate our business in English but fluency in one or more additional European languages is beneficial.
An existing national security clearance (UK SC/DV, German Ü2/Ü3, NATO Secret or equivalent).
Experience in a defence contractor, a government security agency, or a company handling classified or export-controlled material.
Experience with M&A security: diligence, day-one integration playbooks, and consolidating IT across acquired companies.
Hands-on OT security experience (IEC 62443, Purdue model, vendor remote access) in manufacturing.
Security engineering background – you can read code, review an architecture, and have opinions about how software should be built securely.
Certifications such as CISSP, CISM, ISO 27001 Lead Implementer or GIAC – or strong opinions about why they don't matter.
Experience in a scale-up or PE-backed platform where you built the function from one person up.

About the role
Onodrim is building Europe's largest defence and industrial platform. We acquire specialist manufacturers in critical defence and dual-use supply chains, then invest behind their growth with capital, technology and operating know-how.
Onodrim is growing through acquisition, and every deal we do is ultimately a people decision. As Head of People Operations, you'll make sure we understand the people, leadership and culture of a business before we buy it – and that its team is set up to thrive once we integrate.
About 70% of your time goes on our deal pipeline: people due diligence on targets, integration planning, and leading the people workstream through close and the first 100 days. The other 30% is spent building Onodrim's own people function – hiring, policies, processes and culture that every acquired team will join.
The two halves feed each other. What you build internally is the landing zone foreach acquisition; what you learn in each deal shapes how Onodrim's people model needs to grow.

Lead people due diligence. Assess each target's leadership, organisation design, key-person dependencies, culture, compensation and benefits, contracts, pensions, employee relations and HR compliance across jurisdictions.

Shape the deal. Work with corporate development, finance and legal on deal structure, retention and incentive packages for founders and key staff, and the people terms of the SPA.

Support hiring. Partner with leaders on workforce planning and recruitment, including roles like our Forward Deployed Operators.
Develop leaders. Put in place performance management, feedback and development practices that suit a hands-on, results-driven team.
Look after culture. Advise the leadership team on engagement, employee relations and culture, and act as a trusted adviser on sensitive people matters.
What you'll bring
At least 5 years' of experience working with people operations in complex environments.
Hands-on M&A experience: you've led people due diligence and integration on multiple acquisitions, ideally in a buy-and-build, private equity-backed or serial-acquirer setting.
Strong working knowledge of employment law and practice across continental Europe and UK, including TUPE, information and consultation, and works councils.
Commercial and financial fluency: you can model the cost of harmonising terms, size a retention pool and explain people risk in deal-value terms.
Experience building or scaling a people function in a growing business, not just running an established one.
Credibility with founders, CEOs and deal teams, and the empathy to support employees through uncertain change.
Clear, direct communication in English, written and spoken.
Willingness to travel regularly to target and acquired companies across Europe.
Right to work in the UK, Switzerland or the EU.
Nice to have
We operate our business in English but fluency in one or more additional European languages – German, Dutch, Italian, Polish or French – especially helps when working with local teams and works councils. 
Experience integrating acquisitions in manufacturing, industrial or operations-heavy businesses, with frontline and unionised workforces.
Background in M&A advisory, a Big Four people-transactions team, or a private equity portfolio operations role. 
Clearance in at least one of our operating countries.

## Introduction

We are looking for an experienced Adaptive Planning specialist to own the administration, architecture and ongoing optimisation of our Adaptive Planning environment. 

The role will be responsible for ensuring that our forecasting and planning model is well structured, scalable, controlled and fit for purpose, including ownership of dimensions, hierarchies, versions, forecast structures, assumptions, data flows and user access. 

The successful candidate will partner closely with FP&A, FBPs, Data Services and Technology teams to improve the quality, efficiency and governance of our forecasting data and flows. 

## Job Responsibilities

**Adaptive Planning Model & Management** 

- Own and maintain the overall Adaptive Planning model structure and architecture. 

- Manage dimensions, hierarchies, levels, accounts, attributes, mappings and reporting structures. 

- Ensure the model supports evolving business requirements, including organisational, product, customer, geographic and AI-related reporting.  

- Review and optimise the existing models to improve scalability, usability and performance. 

- Establish clear version naming, ownership, roll-forward and locking processes. 

- Manage forecast calendars and ensure appropriate controls around version creation and changes. 

- Translate FP&A requirements into effective Adaptive model solutions. 

- Support FP&A in developing scenario and what-if modelling capabilities. 

**System Administration** 

- Manage users, roles, permissions and access. 

- Maintain sheets, formulas, assumptions, business rules and model logic. 

- Manage data imports, exports and integrations. 

- Investigate and resolve data/model issues. 

- Maintain appropriate system documentation and change controls. 

**Data & Reporting** 

- Work with Data Service teams to ensure reliable data flows between Adaptive and other systems. 

- Manage Adaptive integrations with other systems. 

- Perform data validation and reconciliation between Adaptive, actuals and other systems. Help establish a robust single source of truth for forecasting and management reporting. 

- Identify opportunities to use AI and automate manual forecasting and reporting processes.  

- Simplify and standardise planning processes and reporting across Finance. 

- Support new reporting and modelling requirements while maintaining appropriate model governance. 

- Develop documentation and train FP&A users to ensure sustainable ownership. 

## Knowledge and Experience

**Essential** 

- 3–5+ years of hands-on Workday Adaptive Planning / Adaptive Insights experience. 

- Strong experience as an Adaptive administrator and model builder, rather than solely an end user. 

- Demonstrable experience managing dimensions, hierarchies, versions, sheets, formulas and business rules. 

- Good understanding of management accounting, budgeting, forecasting and FP&A processes. 

- Strong practical data analysis skills, including SQL and/or Python, ability to work confidently with structured data, datasets and reporting outputs. 

- Multi-entity and multi-currency planning experience. 

- Experience managing Adaptive integrations and data loads. 

- Ability to understand complex models, translate and build in Adaptive  

- Strong stakeholder management and communication skills. 

**Desirable** 

- Experience with Snowflake, NetSuite, Salesforce and Success Factor. 

- SaaS / technology /AI industry experience. 

- Familiar with ARR, revenue, headcount and cost forecasting. 

- Experience designing scenario and driver-based planning models in Adaptive. 
- Data Science or machine-learning expertise is preferred but not required.

• SQL Server ETL Development 

• Develop and maintain T-SQL based ETL pipelines running on SQL Server 2019. 

• Data Processing & Data Quality 

• Investigate and resolve data integrity and quality issues across multiple research databases. 

• Write historic correction scripts to fix data anomalies across large datasets. 

• Implement validation and consistency checks during data ingestion and transformation. 

• Performance & Database Engineering 

• Optimise ETL queries and batch processes running against very large tables (billions of rows). 

• Analyse and tune query execution plans, indexing strategies, and partitioned tables. 

• Improve performance of data loads and batch ETL processing. 

• Operational Database Work 

• Support operational SQL Server tasks including: 

• monitoring ETL jobs 

• backup verification 

• integrity checks 

• troubleshooting failed imports 

• Manage file-based data ingestion, including large CSV imports and server directory management. 

• Maintain and improve SSIS packages and SQL-driven import scripts. 

• Manage ~700 automated data imports per month from multiple GP clinical systems. 

• Maintain and extend 150+ ETL scripts responsible for data ingestion, transformation, and validation. 

• Adapt ETL pipelines as data formats and source system specifications evolve. 

Key Requirements: 
• This role requires strong practical experience with SQL Server ETL development. Applicants should have: 

• Strong commercial experience working with Microsoft SQL Server (2016–2019+) 

• Extensive T-SQL development experience, including: 

• stored procedures 

• complex joins and transformations 

• large batch processing scripts 

• error handling and logging 

• Hands-on experience building or maintaining ETL pipelines using SSIS 

• Experience working with large datasets (hundreds of millions to billions of rows) 

• Experience with query optimisation and performance tuning, including: 

• index design 

• execution plan analysis 

• partitioned tables 

• Experience working in script-driven ETL environments 

• Comfortable working directly with database servers and file-based data imports 

• Typical candidates will have approximately 3–6 years experience in SQL Server ETL, BI development, or database engineering roles.

• Experience working with clinical, healthcare, or research datasets

• Development of OMOP-compatible data pipelines to strengthen interoperability and support advanced research workflows.

• National GP clinical datasets used in medical and population health research

• Very large datasets containing billions of clinical records

Overview

The SAP Business One System Specialist will help transform Orphalan’s use of SAP Business One into an integrated ERP and operational control system. The role will work across Finance, Supply Chain, Commercial, Legal, Quality and Technology to design, configure, integrate and embed end-to-end business processes in SAP B1.

This is a hands-on specialist role combining SAP B1 functional expertise, systems configuration, process analysis, integration coordination, data governance, reporting and user enablement. The successful candidate will translate business requirements into controlled, supportable solutions and ensure that SAP B1 becomes the reliable system of record for purchasing, inventory, order-to-cash, payments, close and management reporting.

Role Purpose

• Own the functional evolution, configuration and continuous improvement of SAP B1 across Orphalan.

• Convert approved future-state processes and controls into practical SAP B1 workflows, authorisations, master data, integrations, reports and operating procedures.

• Coordinate delivery across business owners, Finance, external SAP partners and integrated-system providers while protecting data quality, auditability and segregation of duties.

• Drive adoption so users follow standard ERP processes rather than parallel email, spreadsheet or manual workarounds.

Key Responsibilities

SAP B1 Functional Ownership and Solution Design

• Act as Orphalan’s internal SAP B1 functional specialist and primary point of coordination for ERP configuration, enhancement, support and roadmap delivery.

• Lead discovery workshops, document requirements, map end-to-end processes and translate business needs into fit-for-purpose SAP B1 designs.

• Assess when to use SAP B1 native capabilities, approved add-ons, Microsoft Power Platform or integrated solutions, balancing control, usability, maintainability and cost.

• Maintain the system design, configuration documentation, process maps, decision log, change backlog and release plan.

Request-to-Pay and Supplier Management

• Implement structured purchase requests, budget checks, contract references, approval workflows and purchase-order creation in SAP B1.

• Configure vendor onboarding controls, mandatory fields, duplicate detection and governed vendor master-data changes, including independent verification of bank details.

• Enable goods receipt and service-confirmation processes linked to purchase orders and contracts.

Inventory, Batch Management and 3PL Integration

• Configure SAP B1 as the financial inventory system of record, including products, warehouses, batches, expiry dates, quarantine, release and ownership status.

• Coordinate transaction-level integration with 3PL providers for receipts, releases, transfers, shipments, returns and adjustments.

• Implement interface control totals, exception reporting and reconciliation for inventory movements.

• Support accurate cut-off and accounting for goods in transit, consignment stock, distributor stock and third-party-held inventory.

Order-to-Cash, Shipment and Revenue Processes

• Implement controlled sales-order processing with product, price, quantity, delivery terms, credit status and required shipment date.

• Configure approvals for price, discount, credit and exceptional delivery terms.

• Integrate approved sales orders with 3PL shipment confirmation, delivery transactions and subsequent invoicing.

• Enable traceable document flows from sales order to delivery to invoice, with controls supporting revenue cut-off, credit notes, returns and distributor arrangements.

Payments, Banking and Cash Management

• Complete deployment of the SAP B1 Payment Wizard across relevant legal entities and support secure bank-file integration.

• Implement payment proposals based on approved, due and unblocked liabilities, with appropriate separation of preparation and approval.

• Link payment batches, approvals and bank confirmations back to SAP B1 to maintain a complete audit trail.

• Implement daily bank-statement imports, automated matching rules, cash application and aged ownership of unmatched items.

Financial Close, Accounting and Controls

• Configure reporting and controlled workflows for accrual candidates arising from POs, receipts, service confirmations, contracts, recurring commitments and unprocessed invoices.

• Enable auto-reversing accruals, controlled prepayment schedules, fixed-asset integration, intercompany postings and foreign-exchange revaluation.

• Support a single close calendar, standard balance-sheet reconciliations, preparer/reviewer sign-off and evidence retention.

• Partner with Finance to support a controlled working-day 5 close and the longer-term move towards a working-day 3–4 core accounting close.

Reporting, Data and Exception Management

• Build reliable SAP B1 queries, alerts and operational reports for budget, commitments, inventory, sales, cash, close and exceptions.

• Help establish a controlled finance data layer over SAP B1 and integrate it with Power BI once transactional processes and master data are stable.

• Ensure management reports reconcile to the SAP B1 general ledger before distribution.

• Design exception-led monitoring for unmatched invoices, late receipts, unusual price movements, negative inventory, overdue approvals and unresolved interface items.

Master Data, Security and Governance

• Implement governance for customers, vendors, products, accounts, projects, cost centres and other critical master data.

• Configure role-based authorisations for requesters, approvers, procurement, warehouse, AP, Finance, administrators and payment users.

• Support periodic access recertification, prompt leaver and role-change updates, and controls preventing incompatible combinations of duties.

• Ensure system changes, configuration decisions and control exceptions follow formal ERP governance and change control.

Training, Adoption and Operational Support

• Create concise procedures, workflow guides, approval rules, release notes and role-based training using real Orphalan scenarios.

• Provide second-line functional support, triage incidents, coordinate vendor escalation and identify root causes and preventive improvements.

• Monitor adoption, system usage, workflow ageing and exception rates; work with process owners to retire unauthorised spreadsheets and manual workarounds when processes are stable.

• Build a network of process owners and super-users to sustain knowledge, adoption and continuous improvement.

Required Profile

• Demonstrable hands-on experience implementing, configuring, supporting and improving SAP Business One in a multi-process business environment.

• Strong functional knowledge of SAP B1 across purchasing, sales, inventory, financials, banking, approvals, authorisations, master data and reporting.

• Experience translating business processes and internal controls into system configuration and practical workflows.

• Experience with SAP B1 integration approaches and coordinating interfaces with third-party platforms, 3PLs, banks or invoice-processing systems.

• Working knowledge of SQL-based queries and reporting for SAP B1; ability to diagnose data and transaction issues logically.

• Understanding of finance and accounting processes, including AP, AR, general ledger, accruals, prepayments, fixed assets, intercompany, FX, bank reconciliation and period close.

• Good understanding of role-based access, segregation of duties, audit trails, change control and master-data governance.

• Strong stakeholder engagement, workshop facilitation, documentation and training skills.

• Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities and coordinate effectively with external implementation partners.

Desirable Experience

• Experience in pharmaceutical, life-sciences, healthcare or another regulated environment.

• Experience with batch-managed and expiry-controlled inventory, third-party logistics and multi-entity operations.

• Exposure to SAP Concur, Power BI, Microsoft Power Platform

• Knowledge of SAP B1 Service Layer, integration framework, APIs or common SAP B1 add-ons.

• Relevant SAP Business One certification or equivalent evidence of implementation expertise.

• Experience supporting ERP transformation`, process standardisation and business adoption beyond Finance.

job_description:
Oxford Data Plan is an alternative data company serving institutional investors, primarily hedge funds, with real time daily KPI and revenue tracking products. We work with around 100 funds across fundamental long/short, multi-manager and systematic strategies. Post Series B, scaling fast.
We are hiring a senior leader to own the link between what clients buy and what we build. Reporting to the CRO, you will analyse win and deal rates at product level, size our target market, rank coverage gaps by the revenue attached to them, and turn that into roadmap recommendations and clear go to market messaging for the revenue team. The role needs both data science skills and commercial judgment. The goal is to maximise ARR by building the right products in the right order and selling them well.
Responsibilities:
• Win and deal rate analysis. Own the product level view of commercial performance: win/loss themes, conversion rates by product, segment and sector, and where deals stall for product reasons.
• Target market and TAM. Define and maintain our target market and TAM analysis by client segment, sector and KPI coverage area, so roadmap decisions are sized against addressable revenue. This becomes the reference map for where we grow next.
• Roadmap prioritisation. Recommend which products, segments, sectors and KPIs to prioritise, ranked by ARR impact, drawing on client interactions, pipeline evidence and your own analysis.
• Gap identification. Keep a live, ranked view of gaps in the current offering versus client demand, each with the revenue attached. Coverage gap closure is the company-level metric this role owns; Tech and Partnerships execute the closures.
• Product and Data Strategy Working Group. Take a leading role in the working group, holding the Revenue seat and bringing win/loss evidence and client demand ranked by ARR into every cycle.
• GTM messaging and timing. Create the messaging Sales and Account Management take to market for each product and launch: positioning, proof points, competitive counters and launch timing.
• Cross-department collaboration. Work closely with the CRO, CTO and Head of Data Partnerships so commercial signal reaches product and partnership decisions, and new capability reaches the sales floor.
• Market intelligence. Track competitor coverage, pricing and product moves, and keep our differentiation and Series B product narrative current.
Success Measures: 
• ARR from products launched through the working group, and improved win rates on deals where a roadmap gap had been cited.
• Coverage gaps closed per quarter, weighted by revenue attached.
• Shorter time from commercial signal to roadmap decision, with one ranked list.
• Sales and AM teams working from consistent, current messaging on every priority product.
Requirements:
• Buy side experience at a leading hedge fund or asset manager, ideally in a market intelligence or alternative data function, evaluating datasets the way our clients do.
• Strong quantitative background, with working Python and SQL. You go to the data yourself.
• Experience sizing markets and making prioritisation calls with capital or revenue at stake, for example in an investing or strategy seat.
• Experience leading a data function or workstream, and able to translate between technical and commercial teams.
• Clear communicator who can turn analysis into a short recommendation and defend it with leadership and with the sales team.

We are looking for a Principal Software Architect to join our Compute Software organisation at IonQ. In this role, you will be responsible for developing and maintaining the architecture of the software that enables a quantum computer, from low level hardware control up to developer programming interfaces, contributing to the team’s mission of delivering a complete software product for a quantum computer.

You’ll play an important part in shaping the software and tools that support our work in building the world’s most advanced quantum systems. Our architecture now needs to evolve to support the next generation of our systems, and you will lead that work.

Responsibilities:

In this position, you will develop the software architecture covering real-time and non-real-time hardware management, low level orchestration and user interfaces for the current product and the future roadmap of products. You will also work with the technical leads from the development teams to support the effective development and delivery of a scalable solution that supports internal experimental scientists and external customers.

You’ll have the opportunity to develop an evolving software architecture to support a family of products, contributing directly to the success of the system software team in delivering a world leading quantum computer. You will coach and train technical leads in good architectural principles, and work closely with the infrastructure, firmware and compiler teams across the UK and the US.

Key responsibilities include:

• Development and documentation of the system software architecture

• Managing the evolving architecture across a family of products

• Coordination with other architects across the whole of software and the wider system

• Research and analysis to support future requirements elucidation

• Coordination with technical leads to ensure that the design and implementation meets the intention of the architecture

Requirements:

To be successful, you will need prior experience of developing a large and scalable software architecture covering real-time requirements and distributed processing. We’re looking for someone who can think strategically at the architecture level, solve challenging technical issues, track the latest industry good practice and tools, and communicate those ideas and technologies to the wider software team.

You will work at the level of the whole system, describing each component, what it does and its constraints, and then handing the detailed design and implementation to the development teams rather than designing through code. A grounding in formal architecture methods and principles such as cohesion, coupling and encapsulation will help you succeed, as will experience of evolving an architecture that has to grow with the product. Our immediate focus is system software and lower level control; experience further up the software stack is an advantage.

• More than 10 years of software development experience, with more than 5 as a software architect

• A clear understanding of software architecture principles

Job Summary Your Career Are you passionate about driving customer success in the cybersecurity industry? We are looking for a dynamic and proactive Technical Support Engineer to join our team. Your strong ability to articulate intricate technical issues to both technical and non-technical audiences will enable you to collaborate seamlessly with stakeholders beyond your immediate domain of expertise.

In this role, you will serve as a designated customer advocate, delivering tailored support that includes weekly reviews, root cause analysis for critical issues, release assessments, upgrade planning, and quarterly business reviews. Your Impact 
• Deliver expert-level technical assistance to top-tier customers, ensuring timely resolution of complex security issues through in-depth troubleshooting, configuration guidance, and best practice implementation.

• Act as a trusted advisor, effectively communicating technical solutions to both technical and executive stakeholders to foster trust and credibility.
• Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams—including Account, Sales, and Marketing—to drive a seamless and positive customer experience while proactively addressing critical challenges.
• Drive continuous customer engagement through Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) and Account Case Reviews, providing tailored recommendations, release planning, and proactive risk mitigation strategies to enhance security posture.
• Serve as a subject matter expert on Palo Alto Networks' core technologies, identifying product defects through lab replication, network simulation, and performance testing.
• Work with Engineering and QA teams to file bug reports, develop test plans, and improve software and hardware quality with each release cycle.
• Facilitate hiring and onboarding by conducting technical screenings, training new hires on technical and soft skills, and ensuring readiness through process and tools training.
• Contribute to the organization’s knowledge base by authoring Technical Support Bulletins, training materials, and troubleshooting guides to enhance internal and customer-facing resources.
• Provide rapid, high-quality support in high-pressure situations, traveling to customer sites to expedite critical issue resolution.
• Engage in technical discussions with cross-functional teams to drive transparency, optimize security posture, and enhance cybersecurity resilience
Qualifications Your Experience 
• Minimum of 7 years of network security experience
• Expertise in TCP/IP and advanced knowledge of LAN/WAN technologies, expertise with general routing/switching, Routing protocols (e.g, BGP, OSPF, EIGRP), branch, and center architectures
• Extensive experience with troubleshooting Remote Access VPN solutions including IPSEC, PKI & SSL technologies
• Ability to independently debug complex networks with mixed media and protocols with an advanced understanding of packet flow across multiple OSI layers
• In-depth knowledge of networking operations - TCP and UDP, SNMP, IPv6, VLSM, CIDR, and NAT - Static, Dynamic, and PAT
• Proficiency with network troubleshooting tools - Wireshark, GNS3
• Strong grasp authentication protocols - LDAP, TACACS+, Radius
• The below skills are a plus:• Virtualization experience (AWS, Azure, VMWare, OpenStack)
• Experience with Windows, MAC OS, and Linux (Debugging, Editing Registries, Plist, etc.)
• Experience with Python or Shell scripting a plus
• Multi-Vendor Exposure - Cisco Advanced Security Appliances, Palo Alto Next-Generation Firewalls, Prisma Access, Cisco Firepower, Checkpoint Firewalls, Cisco Switches, and Intrusion Detection/ Intrusion Prevention Systems

• Skilled in engaging executive-level stakeholders with clear technical communication.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills - the ability to clearly articulate technical issues to both technical and non-technical audiences and to explain the impact in business terms
