You will ensure that every initiative we launch is audited for impact, aligned with global standards, and executed with operational excellence.

Your Impact

• End-to-End Program Operational Governance: Own the full operational lifecycle of all EMEA enablement initiatives, leading strategic project intake, resource orchestration, and cross-functional project management to ensure every program is delivered on time and at a high standard. You will serve as the operational engine for EMEA Sales Enablement, ensuring key revenue-driving initiatives are executed seamlessly to maximize field productivity and reduce rep ramp time. You will manage the execution roadmap, event logistics and post-program success validation to ensure initiatives achieve their defined KPIs, while explicitly delegating content design and facilitation to the respective Subject Matter Experts.

You will translate the high-level FY27 Blueprint into actionable operational plans; orchestrating timelines, managing risks, and ensuring stakeholder alignment across regional and global teams. Your focus is on maintaining a high standard of project integrity, ensuring that every initiative is delivered on schedule and is directly mapped to the team’s strategic KPIs and ROI.
• Program Management: Support the development and manage the execution of flagship enablement programs that help to drive revenue across EMEA, including FLIGHT Sales Onboarding, Brilliant at the Basics and EBC Excellence.
• Global Liaison & Best Practice Synthesis: Serve as the primary point of connection between EMEA and the Global Enablement organization. You will ensure regional alignment with global vision while proactively "exporting" EMEA best practices to influence the global roadmap, ensuring our theater has a seat at the table for worldwide strategy.
• Strategic Event Ownership (SKO & DSM Summit): Executing revenue-critical regional enablement milestones (SKO/DSM Summit) to accelerate pipeline velocity and Q1/Q2 deal execution. This is not a logistical support role; you own the end-to-end strategic framework, budget ROI, and the alignment of event content with EMEA’s specific sales objectives.

Your Experience

• Operational Leadership: Proven experience in a Sales Operations leadership or Strategic Enablement leadership role where you have managed complex portfolios.
• Process Engineering: A track record of identifying operational bottlenecks and implementing scalable solutions that improve team productivity.
• Stakeholder Influence: Experience acting as a liaison between regional and global teams, with the ability to negotiate priorities and share best practices across borders.
• Program Ownership: Experience owning large-scale, high-visibility projects (like SKO) from a strategic and budgetary perspective, rather than just a logistical one.
• Data & Executive Synthesis: Ability to navigate CRM data and translate it into a compelling "so-what" narrative for executive-level stakeholders, including detailed strategic data analysis showing correlation between enablement efforts and results.

About The Role:
Reporting to the Treasury Technology Lead, this is a senior, hands-on role within Treasury, operating at the centre of how Paysend prices and controls FX across 170+ countries. You will own the FX pricing platform end to end, covering how rates are sourced, controlled and delivered to every product. You will also own the automated treasury reconciliation that confirms every treasury movement is accounted for.
You will be the go-to person for FX configuration, rate integrity and reconciliation breaks, and the product owner taking these systems from manual processes to automated, production-grade infrastructure. The role requires someone who understands FX markets, is comfortable working directly with data, and has delivered systems into production rather than only specifying them.
This is not a pure operations or business analysis role. We are looking for someone who can run a live FX system with financial impact every day, while designing and implementing what replaces the manual parts of it.

What You'll Do (Responsibilities):
FX Pricing & Rate Management
• Own the configuration of the FX pricing engine, including instruments, currency pairs, rate sources, quote objects, contracts, tariffs and trade modes.

• Onboard and maintain rate sources across market data providers, liquidity providers, card schemes, central banks and partner rates, ensuring uninterrupted quote delivery.

• Set and adjust treasury spreads in line with market conditions and pricing policy, and maintain the treasury rate methodology used by all products.

• Configure FX pricing for new partners, products and corridors, including stablecoin pairs, with the Enterprise, Consumer and Network teams.

FX Risk & Control
• Run and continuously improve the daily FX rate control process: identifying off-market and invalid quotes, investigating deviations against market and partner rates, and escalating where required.

• Own FX alerting and monitoring, including deviation thresholds, exception lists and source freshness, replacing manual checks with automation.

• Manage user roles and access rights in the FX system, maintaining segregation of duties across Treasury, Product, Enterprise and Finance.

• Provide FX evidence for audits, risk reviews and pricing governance, and supply data for gross margin analysis and the pricing committee.

Treasury Reconciliation
• Own the automated reconciliation of internal treasury transactions (FX deals and transfers) against bank and partner data, including matching logic, exception handling and the manual correction process.

• Extend reconciliation coverage to new banking and liquidity partners, defining data mappings and transformation rules for each.

• Maintain the logic that converts reconciled data into NetSuite journals, partnering with Finance and the Settlement and Reconciliation team on accuracy and audit trail.

• Investigate and resolve reconciliation breaks independently, and report on status and recurring issues.

Business Analysis & Implementation
• Act as the business analyst and product owner for all treasury technology initiatives. Gather, structure and validate requirements with stakeholders, and translate them into functional specifications, data models and acceptance criteria.

• Lead delivery with Engineering through prioritisation, testing, release validation, user training and production cutover.

• Drive the roadmap towards an automated treasury FX platform covering price aggregation, FX deal execution with liquidity providers, real-time currency position monitoring, limits and FX booking.

• Analyse data in SQL and build Python tooling for monitoring, bulk configuration and reporting, using AI-assisted development where it accelerates delivery.

• Act as the escalation point for FX configuration, access and data requests through the Treasury Helpdesk, and define and enforce Treasury acceptance standards for functionality delivered by other teams.

• Work independently on ambiguous problems, bringing structured solutions, and document processes, controls and configuration so that the platform does not depend on a single person.

What You’ll Need To Be Successful In This Role:
Essential:
• 5+ years in FX within a fintech, payments company, bank or broker, in FX operations, pricing, treasury systems or FX product.

• Strong understanding of FX market mechanics, including bid/ask/mid, spreads and markups, cross rates, liquidity sources and FX risk drivers.

• Strong SQL, with the ability to query, validate and reconcile large transactional datasets independently.

• Working Python, with the ability to build, read, test and maintain data logic, whether written by hand or with AI tools, and take accountability for the results.

• Proven experience taking FX, treasury or reconciliation functionality from requirements through UAT into production.

• Hands-on reconciliation experience, including matching logic, break investigation and the link to accounting entries.

• Familiarity with APIs and integration concepts (REST, authentication, webhooks, JSON/XML).

Competencies:
• Strong attention to detail where configuration errors have direct financial impact, combined with the ability to see the bigger picture.

• Sound judgement and confidence acting on non-routine market events.

• Clear written communication of processes, controls and requirements to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Proactive, self-starting approach with a track record of automating manual work.

Desirable:
• Experience with market data providers (e.g. Refinitiv/LSEG) or trading and RFQ platforms (e.g. 360T); familiarity with the FIX protocol.

• Exposure to FX execution, position management or treasury management systems.

• Experience with Databricks, NetSuite, or BI tools such as Superset or Metabase.

• Knowledge of payment rails, card scheme FX, or stablecoin FX.

• Experience in a regulated environment (FCA/EMI), including safeguarding.

Why Join Paysend?
• Make a Global Impact:

WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS NOW

Pencil has grown fast, one feature at a time. Much of the UI has been designed and built with AI tools. The product works, but it does not yet feel like one product: components are duplicated, the same task works differently in different places, and there is no shared foundation.

Our designers sit inside product squads, and design has no single owner above them. Priorities are set squad by squad. This role closes that gap.

You will not start from a blank page. Pencil already has a design system, but it has not been fully reviewed or implemented across the product. Your first job is to own it: review it, close the gaps, and make it the way Pencil gets built.

The team also needs a leader. Someone who inspires people, builds a culture designers want to be part of, and brings creative ambition to a product that has mostly been built to work, not to delight.




WHAT YOU WILL OWN

 - One design function. Bring product design and UX into a single team with one quality bar. Designers report to design and work inside squads. Squads own priority and delivery; design owns craft and sign-off.

 - Team culture. Inspire a team that has worked without a design leader. Build the critique, rituals and shared ambition that make designers proud of what they ship.

 - Shipping, with magic. Get features out the door with product and engineering, on time and on-system. Then add what people remember: ideas, craft and moments of delight that go beyond the brief.

 - Design for AI-built UI. Much of Pencil's UI is built with AI coding tools, and that will continue. Make the system the source those tools build from, with written guidelines that keep generated UI on-system.

 - How people work with agents. Define how users brief, run, supervise, review and approve work done by agents. This is Pencil's core interaction model, and no one has solved it yet.

 - Two users in the same screens. Enterprise buyers judge Pencil on governance, control and trust. Practitioners judge it on speed and creative range. The product has to serve both.

 - How design works with product and engineering. Design review, who approves new patterns, and the rituals the three disciplines share.

job_description:
# About Performix Media

Performix Media is a performance marketing company running high-volume paid social campaigns, primarily in the igaming, sportsbetting and crypto verticals. We move fast, spend meaningfully, and hold ourselves to hard CPA targets – every pound of ad spend has a job to do.

# The Role

We’re looking for an exceptional Meta media buyer who operates the way the best marketers will operate in 2026: with AI in the loop at every step. You’ll own high-volume Facebook and Instagram campaigns end to end – strategy, creative production, launch, and optimisation – with aggressive CPA targets and real budget authority.

This is not a role for someone who dabbles with ChatGPT for ad copy. We want someone who has rebuilt their entire workflow around AI: driving campaign optimisation programmatically through the Meta Ads API and MCP-connected agents, generating and iterating video creative with AI tools in hours rather than weeks, and letting data decide what runs.

# What You’ll Do

- Own high-volume campaigns — plan, launch, and scale Meta campaigns across multiple ad accounts, owning performance against tight CPA and ROAS targets.
- Optimise with AI in the loop — build and run agentic workflows (MCP servers, Meta Ads API, custom scripts, or tools like Claude) that monitor spend, surface anomalies, rotate creative, and execute budget and bid changes at a pace no manual buyer can match.
- Create video at speed — produce ad videos on the fly using AI video generation and editing tools (e.g. Runway, Veo, Sora, Kling, HeyGen, CapCut and similar), turning a creative brief into live test variants same-day.
- Handle editing and banner design — cut, caption, resize, and version video for placements; design static banners and image ads to a standard good enough to ship without a designer in the loop.
- Run a rigorous testing programme — structure high-tempo creative testing — hooks, formats, angles, audiences — and feed the results back into both the creative pipeline and the account structure.
- Stay on top of the data — own tracking, attribution (Pixel, CAPI, post-back), reporting, and the numbers behind every decision. You should be able to explain any account’s performance from memory.
- Build the playbook — document what works, systematise it, and raise the bar for how the whole company buys media.

# What We’re Looking For

- Proven track record — managing high-volume Meta campaigns to tight CPA targets, with numbers you can walk us through.
- Genuinely AI-native — AI is not a tool you tried, it’s how you work. You use LLMs and agents daily for analysis, automation, and creative, and you can show us real examples.
- Hands-on with MCP / API automation — comfortable connecting AI agents to ad platforms via MCP or the Meta Ads API, or scripting your own automation (Python/JS a plus, not required if you get there with no-code/agent tooling).
- AI video generation skills — you can take a product and, within a day, have multiple AI-generated video ads live and testing.
- Video editing and design — practical ability in video editing (CapCut, Premiere, Descript or similar) and banner/static design (Figma, Canva, Photoshop) — good taste, fast hands.
- Meta platform mastery — deep, current knowledge of Meta’s ecosystem — Advantage+, Andromeda-era ranking, creative-led account structures, CAPI, and how to keep learning phases stable at scale.
- Ownership mentality — you treat spend like it’s your own money, communicate clearly and proactively, and don’t need managing.

# Nice to Have

- Experience across other paid channels (TikTok, Google, native, programmatic).
- Experience in leadgen, igaming or sportsbetting.
- Built or contributed to internal marketing tools, MCP servers, or automation stacks.

# How to Apply

Send the following to mb@performixmedia.com:

- A short note (or 2-minute Loom) on the best Meta account you’ve run: spend level, CPA target, and what you did to hit it.
- One concrete example of an AI/automation workflow you built into your media buying — what it does and what it replaced.
- 2–3 ad creatives you made yourself (video or static), ideally AI-assisted, with a line on how each performed.

About the Role:
Perk is going through a period of significant growth, and we're using AI and automation to make our sales teams more productive and to take manual work out of our reps' day-to-day, in our tools and in the CRM. Nowhere is that more visible than in our SDR organisation, where we are rolling out AI-driven outbound prospecting with tools like Clay.

We're hiring a Revenue Operations Manager in Barcelona to support our SDR organisation globally. This is a senior individual contributor role: a strategic business partner to SDR leadership on process, systems, and operating cadences, and the business owner of the SDR tech stack, from Sales Engagement tooling to LinkedIn Sales Navigator and enrichment. You'll own how SDRs prospect, engage, and hand off pipeline, from the data and signals that tell them who to contact, to the sequences and automations that help them do it at scale, to the reporting that shows what is working.

We're looking for a true owner who understands what good looks like, has rolled out AI and automation for outbound at scale elsewhere, and is curious about where AI can take outbound next.

What You'll Do:
Be the strategic partner to SDR leadership
• Partner with global SDR leaders to define and run the operating model: processes, territories and handoffs, and the weekly, monthly, and quarterly cadences that keep the team on track.

• Work with Sales Leadership, Marketing, Sales Enablement, and Finance to keep lead management and pipeline definitions aligned end to end.

Own the SDR process
• Own the end-to-end SDR process, from prospecting and outreach to qualification and handoff to Account Executives, and keep it documented in clear playbooks that are consistent across regions.

• Own the prospecting process: ICP and account prioritisation, signal-based targeting, and outbound cadences.

• Own the qualification methodology: lead and opportunity definitions, qualification criteria, stage and disqualification logic, and acceptance standards for handoffs, and evolve them as our go-to-market changes.

• Own the inbound lead process: capture, routing, speed-to-lead standards, follow-up expectations, ownership rules, and the handoff between Marketing and SDRs.

• Roll out process changes with SDR leaders and Enablement, and make sure they are adopted and followed.

• Own the Rules of Engagement for outbound and inbound, including account ownership between regional and global accounts, so SDRs, Account Executives, and Marketing know who works which accounts and leads, and conflicts are resolved quickly and fairly.

Own the SDR tech stack
• Act as the business owner of every tool our SDR organisation uses in its prospecting efforts globally, including Sales Engagement platforms, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, and data enrichment tools, owning the roadmap, configuration, licences and cost, adoption, data quality, and vendor relationships.

• Make sure the tools, the CRM, and the data around them work as one system, so reps spend their time selling, not updating records.

• Evaluate, pilot, and roll out new tools and features, with clear business cases and success metrics.

• Partner closely with the Revenue Systems team, who are the technical owners of these tools and manage configuration, syncs, and integrations, by setting priorities and requirements as the business owner, and with Enablement on training and change management.

Drive AI and automation for outbound and inbound
• Partner with the GTM Engineering team, who own Clay and the AI automation for SDRs, and act as the business owner of the SDR automation roadmap, defining the use cases and priorities for AI-driven outbound: signal-based targeting, account and contact research, enrichment, personalisation, and sequencing.

• Reduce manual work for SDRs by automating CRM updates, lead and account research, routing, and follow-up, and measure the time saved and the pipeline impact.

• Design and refine lead routing, scoring, and inbound handling so the right leads reach the right reps quickly.

• Test and pilot emerging AI capabilities for SDR and inbound use cases, and scale what works with clear guardrails on data quality, compliance, and brand.

Protect data and quality
• Set the standards for data hygiene, outreach governance, and deliverability across SDR tools, and make sure they are followed.

• Build the dashboards and reporting that give SDR leaders and reps a single source of truth on activity, funnel, and outcomes.

• Document processes and playbooks so they are repeatable across regions.

What We're Looking For:
• Significant experience (typically 5+ years) in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, or SDR/Pipeline Operations in B2B SaaS, with a focus on SDR or outbound productivity.

• Proven experience supporting the roll out of AI and automation for outbound prospecting from a process point of view

• Deep hands-on knowledge of Salesforce and of Sales Engagement platforms (such as Outreach, Salesloft, or Gong), including sequencing, enrichment, routing, and scoring.

• Strong analytical skills: you can find the story in funnel and rep-activity data and turn it into decisions that SDR leaders act on.

• A true owner: you take responsibility for a tool, a process, or an outcome end to end, and you don't wait to be asked.

• Credibility as a strategic partner to senior sales leaders, comfortable challenging and influencing across Sales, Marketing, Enablement, Finance, and Systems.

• Strong project and change management skills, with a track record of driving adoption across global teams.

• Curiosity about AI and where it can take SDR, outbound, and inbound operations next.

• Comfortable in a fast-growing, fast-changing environment where processes are still being built.

What we offer: 
• Receive competitive compensation and equity ownership in Perk

• Rest and recharge with 25 days of annual leave plus bank holidays

• Take control of your physical health with private medical cover and voluntary dental insurance from Bupa, and discounted gym memberships with GymFlex

• Plan for your future with our qualifying earnings company pension plan with Aviva

• Know that your loved ones are protected financially through your Life Insurance if the worst were to happen

• Rest assured that you’re covered by income protection in case you experience a long-term sickness or absence

• Leverage tax-efficient cycle and electric car schemes with Cycle2Work & Octopus

• Join our unforgettable Perk events, including our spectacular annual summer party

• Always feel supported with Spring Health, our market-leading wellbeing partner, providing fast, comprehensive access to 12x therapy and 12x coaching sessions for you and your loved ones

• Focus on your family with 12-16 weeks’ paid parental leave

• Contribute to your community with 16 paid hours per year to spend volunteering for your dearest charitable causes

• Broaden your horizons with up to 20 "Work from Anywhere" days per year

• Stay savvy with access to a wide variety of discounts and rewards

• Follow your passions and take a four-week, fully paid sabbatical once you reach 5 years

• Let us help you move to one of our hubs with relocation support

Hiring Process
• 30 min online call with Talent Acquisition 

• Online 45min call with the hiring manager 

• IRL Assessment with the Hiring manager + another senior person from the Rev Ops team

• 30 min online panel interview with the SDR Manager 

• 30 min Online Culture interview with SE Manager 

AI at Perk
AI is embedded in how we work across every function. The tools you'll use day-to-day are AI-enabled so you can move faster and spend more time on the work that matters. In practice, that means using AI to research and prioritise accounts, draft and refine outreach, handle customer interactions more effectively, synthesise information, and cut through shadow work - the invisible tasks that pull people away from the work only they can do - so you can focus on relationships and outcomes.

How We Work
At Perk, we take an IRL-first approach to work, where our team works together in-person 3 days a week. As such, this role requires you to be based within commuting distance of our hubs. We fundamentally believe in the value of meeting in real life to improve connectivity, productivity, creativity and ultimately making us a great place to work.

Perk is a global company with a diverse customer base, and we want to make sure the people behind our product reflect that. We’re an equal opportunity employer, which means you’re welcome at Perk regardless of how you look, where you’re from, or anything else that makes you, well, you.

Protect Yourself from Recruitment Scams
All official communication from Perk will always come from email addresses ending in @perk.com or @externalperk.com, our verified social media channels, or recruiters listed on our official LinkedIn page. We will never ask you to pay for equipment, training, or fees, request sensitive personal information such as bank details early in the process, or communicate through unofficial apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, or Signal. If you receive a message claiming to be from Perk that seems suspicious, please do not respond. Forward it to security [at] perk .com, and we will confirm whether it is legitimate.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Enterprise Trust & Governance team builds the control plane that lets the world’s largest organizations deploy Perplexity broadly and with confidence. Computer and our agents work across a growing share of our customers’ environments, tools, and models. For administrators, that makes precise, enforceable control essential: who can do what, with which data, through which agents, and within what usage limits. This team makes those controls easy to manage, reliable and consistent across every product, and transparent to the people accountable for them.

This is a product and platform engineering role with end-to-end ownership, from shaping the architecture and policy models to shipping the experiences our customers’ administrators and security teams use every day. You’ll work across product and infrastructure teams to turn complex enterprise requirements into reusable primitives and intuitive controls. The scope spans identity and provisioning, fine-grained role-based access across connectors, tool actions, and models, customer-managed encryption keys, admin APIs, audit logs, and policy and usage controls. Strong governance helps enterprises move from pilots to company-wide rollouts and gives them the confidence to entrust agents with greater responsibility over time.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own enterprise identity and provisioning, including SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM, WorkOS integrations, and support for identity providers such as Okta and Microsoft Entra ID.

 - Build the permissions platform, with fine-grained roles and permissions for connectors, tool actions, models, and model effort levels, enforced consistently across products and agent workflows.

 - Design and ship secure, well-documented admin APIs for audit logs, members, groups, roles, and settings.

 - Build policy controls for model and feature availability, staged rollouts, model deprecations, usage and spend limits, alerts, and cost-center allocation.

 - Build admin-facing analytics for adoption, usage, spend, and policy enforcement, helping organizations measure value and manage their deployments.

 - Deliver audit logs and change notifications that help administrators investigate activity, track configuration changes, and support compliance.

 - Set the technical bar for authorization correctness and reliability, with fast, consistent, explainable permission checks, well-defined failure behavior, and strong tenant isolation.

 - Partner with Product, Design, Security, Sales, and Customer Success to translate complex enterprise requirements into reusable platform capabilities and intuitive admin experiences.
   
   


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 4+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of owning complex backend systems from design through production operation.

 - Strong system design skills, including building reliable, scalable, multi-tenant SaaS platforms with clear security and isolation boundaries.

 - Strong proficiency in a backend language such as Python, Go, or Rust, and hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure such as AWS and Kubernetes.

 - Deep expertise in at least one of the following:
   
   - Enterprise identity and provisioning, including OAuth, OIDC, SAML, and SCIM.
   
   - Permissions platforms, fine-grained authorization, and policy enforcement.
   
   - Encryption, customer-managed keys, and key lifecycle management.
   
   - Enterprise admin platforms, audit infrastructure, or usage and spend analytics.

 - Experience building or integrating enterprise identity and access systems, including platforms such as WorkOS, Okta, or Microsoft Entra ID.

 - Sound technical judgment in security-sensitive systems, balancing threat models, authorization correctness, and failure behavior with usability and delivery speed.

 - A track record of leading ambiguous, cross-team initiatives from architecture through adoption, setting technical direction for shared platforms, and raising engineering quality through mentorship.

If you’re excited about this role, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every qualification. We value demonstrated impact, deep ownership, and the initiative to turn ambiguity into results.

Purpose

Turn the build decision from the Investment Committee into a MVP that is real enough to judge, and make sure that when an initiative fails it fails on its hypothesis rather than on an avoidable product weakness. This role owns the vision of what gets built, at what pace, and whether intended users adopt it during the MVP stages.

Key accountabilities

·       Sets the vision for the build, if it scales. Write the target product profile, product requirements and acceptance criteria for every initiative funded by the pillar.

·       Work directly with scrum masters, product teams and engineering teams in the Build pillar so approved work is sequenced, built correctly and delivered at pace.

·       Work with users as closely as with engineers: take each increment back to the target market, convert feedback into backlog decisions and ensure the specification reflects the features that matter.

·       Own product adoption during MVP stage. A portfolio failure should come from a disproven hypothesis, not a solution users could not or would not use because of preventable product choices.

·       Bring product, user and technical evidence to the stage gate discussion for transitioning a MVP into a product to scale.

·       Provide build estimates for externally sourced opportunities, including internal cost, capacity, time and principal delivery risks, as the counterweight to rent-or-partner proposals.

·       Own end-to-end programme and project management for each funded MVP: establish the integrated plan, milestones, dependencies and decision points; manage scope, risks and change; escalate delivery constraints; and close or transition work cleanly at each gate.

Decision rights

Owns the product specification, acceptance criteria and backlog prioritisation within an approved initiative. Determines whether product and user evidence is sufficient to present at a stage gate; the Investment Committee decides whether the initiative progresses.

Required experience and capabilities

·       Proven relevant experience in digital product management, product development, technology-enabled transformation or a related field; (further experience required for candidates without an advanced degree).

·       Demonstrated end-to-end accountability for digital products from discovery and business case through build, launch, and adoption, preferably across multiple markets.

·       Has shipped digital products. Able to write and defend specifications, make trade-offs and change direction when evidence requires it.

·       Credible with engineers and architects: understands technical capability, development timelines, dependencies and what is realistic to promise.

·       Equally credible with commercial leaders, initiative sponsors and users. The role requires translation in both directions and the authority to hold each side to agreed outcomes.

·       Highly structured, with rigorous control of scope, timeline, product quality and decision records.

·       Able to estimate build cost and effort sufficiently for a meaningful rent-versus-build comparison.

·       Experienced in influencing delivery teams and senior sponsors without owning the engineering resource.

Job Title
Advertising Effectiveness Lead
Job Description
We’re looking for a measurement leader to show brands the impact of advertising on our app. You’ll build a clear, credible approach to measuring campaign performance across our inventory, turn results into useful recommendations, and help our commercial team demonstrate the value of partnering with us.
You’ll work across Sales, Ad Operations, Product, Data and external research partners. The role combines hands-on campaign analysis with building the measurement products and processes that can scale as the business grows.

What you’ll do
• Define the measurement strategy for brand campaigns across our app and any associated channels.
• Establish practical measurement frameworks for reach, frequency, engagement, brand lift and other relevant outcomes.
• Lead campaign studies, including survey-based brand lift, conversion measurement and advertiser-specific research where appropriate.
• Translate campaign and audience data into clear reporting, case studies and recommendations for brands.
• Build repeatable measurement packages that the sales team can explain and sell.
• Partner with Ad Operations and Product to improve campaign tagging, data quality, reporting and measurement readiness.
• Work with Data and Analytics teams to develop dashboards and reliable ways to assess campaign performance.
• Manage relationships with research vendors, measurement platforms and other external partners.
• Set standards for study design, methodology, privacy and responsible use of data.
• Train and support commercial teams so they can confidently discuss measurement with clients.
• Track market developments and bring forward new approaches that improve the value of our advertising offer.

What you’ll bring
• Experience in advertising measurement, media research, marketing science, analytics or a related field.
• A track record of measuring campaigns for publishers, platforms, agencies or brands.
• Familiarity with brand lift studies, survey research, attribution and campaign effectiveness methods.
• Strong analytical skills and the ability to explain findings clearly to non-technical audiences.
• Experience turning measurement into commercial tools, client recommendations or sales enablement.
• Confidence working across Sales, Product, Data and Operations teams.
• Good judgement around research quality, privacy and the limits of what campaign data can show.
• Clear written and verbal communication skills, including presenting results to senior clients.

What success looks like
• Brands understand what our campaigns delivered and what they learned.
• Measurement is included in more proposals and is straightforward to activate.
• Campaign reporting is timely, consistent and trusted by clients.
• Insights lead to useful recommendations, repeat investment and stronger case studies.
• Our measurement offer grows without compromising research quality or user privacy.

Compensation & benefits
Doing meaningful work should come with fair, transparent rewards. 
The base salary range for this role is between 39,300.00£ - 61,800.00£.
We determine pay within the range using objective factors, like the skills the role requires, your relevant experience and the responsibility you'll have in this role, alongside internal equity and local market considerations. This role is eligible for an annual incentive with your rewards linked to key performance indicators and company results. 

Benefits include a generous pension contribution, private healthcare, along with a range of flexible benefits and family friendly policies - be sure to speak to your recruiter about all the benefits on offer. We also have plenty of learning opportunities to support your development at Philips.

How we work together
We believe that we are better together than apart. For our office-based teams, this means working in-person at least 3 days per week.

Job Description
Be part of a team connecting patients with hospitals, helping to make a difference and improving lives every day.

In this role, you have the opportunity to:
Lead customer-facing programs for Radiology Informatics (RI) — including PACS, RIS, and enterprise imaging solutions — to meet project objectives, stakeholders’ expectations, and create lasting customer value.
Your role:

As a Philips Customer Program Manager for Radiology Informatics, you will be at the leading edge of healthcare innovation, improving customer satisfaction (NPS) by delivering software solutions that meet our healthcare customers’ needs. You will use project methodologies such as PMP/PRINCE2 to manage complex software implementation projects through their full lifecycle, from customer order signature to revenue recognition, go-live, and handover to Support Services.

Using a structured approach, you will provide timely and regular stakeholder communication (internal and external) supported by clear documentation, effective risk management, and rigorous management of the customer acceptance process.

This is a field-based role, predominantly covering customers across the UK, Ireland, and the Nordics (Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Finland), with responsibility to support other areas within Northern Europe as needed. You will work from home with regular travel to customer sites.

You are responsible for:
• Overseeing and managing large-scale, cross-functional projects (typically >€/£1M budget), ensuring delivery across scope, timeline, budget, quality, resources, and risk.
• Gaining agreement on and achieving project goals and objectives; balancing and managing the project scope (including requirements), schedule, budget, quality, resources, and risks.
• Driving decision-making, appropriately balancing risk-taking and issue escalation, and setting up detailed progress/escalation reports with clear corrective actions.
• Building strong relationships with customers and external partners within the region up to senior leadership level.
• Representing projects in steering committees and governance forums.
• Leading and empowering diverse project teams, enabling team members to become efficient and effective.
• Ensuring adherence to standardized solution delivery processes (e.g., SOLiD/Gearshift framework) and providing a flawless customer experience.
• Ensuring that RI solutions are delivered according to agreed scope, quality, budget, and time targets.
• Managing external parties such as subcontractors and partners, including complex or customized contract environments.
• Ensuring cost performance and optimization by driving KPIs such as utilization rate by role/skill level and project costing/recalculation.
• Controlling project budgets and project progress; evaluating all change requests for feasibility, cost/benefit, and added value; taking corrective actions.
• Supporting the revenue and cost forecast process for projects and ensuring changes to the forecast are reported and flagged promptly.
• Managing workforce planning and resource allocation across projects to ensure seamless delivery and flawless customer experience.
• Developing proposals to improve processes and procedures proactively in the interest of continuous improvement.

You are part of:
Enterprise Informatics RI S&SD Implementation Northern Europe. You will report to the EI RI S&SD Implementation Project Management Leader in Northern Europe. You will be part of an inspiring team that has the goal to strengthen and drive performance of EI RI S&SD Implementation within Northern Europe.

To succeed in this role, you should have the following skills and experience:
• 5+ years of work experience in software professional services and project management, ideally across different countries/markets.
• A degree/qualification in Software Engineering, Business Engineering, or equivalent.
• Must have related healthcare domain experience.
• PMP (PMI) certified or equivalent (mandatory).
• Professional knowledge of project management methodologies and estimation techniques (resources, cost, time, and risks).
• Proven experience delivering healthcare IT/software projects, ideally including Radiology Informatics and PACS.
• Functional knowledge of applied products and systems, and their interaction with third-party systems.
• Financial acumen to influence margin in the pre-sales phase and to improve margin during delivery execution.
• Communication skills to manage relationships with executive/management representatives of customers.
• Experience managing teams, subcontractors, and complex contract negotiations.
• Relevant experience with improvement projects for software delivery, meeting time, budget, and quality targets.
• Experience in analyzing process performance, identifying improvement opportunities, and driving change.
• Knowledge of quality and compliance requirements.
• Knowledge of Health & Safety standards; ideally in-depth experience in the Health Systems industry.
• Comprehensive understanding of "people business" — managing key skills in project, solutions, and services business, and driving continuous professionalization.
• Quality-first mindset.
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

• Acts as a role model for our Philips Leadership Asks: Customers first; Patient Safety, Quality and Integrity always; Team up to win; Take ownership to deliver fast; Eager to improve and inspire.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Risk and Controls Manager to join our Risk & Controls team, part of Pleo's Second Line of Defence. You'll report to our Head of Risk and Controls, helping build and run our enterprise risk management framework, from risk appetite linkage through to the risk reporting our senior leaders and committees rely on. Alongside that full ERM remit, you'll own second line oversight of security, technology and operational resilience risk, giving our technology and security teams informed, credible challenge. It's a rare mix: a broad enterprise risk role with a technology risk specialism, in a FinTech that's still shaping how it manages risk as it scales. We value people from a range of risk backgrounds, so if you match most of what's below, we'd love to hear from you.




WHO YOU'LL BE WORKING WITH AND REPORTING TO

 - Shape our GRC tooling: Run GRC tools and help decide how we bring more structure and automation to how we manage risk.

 - Be a trusted risk partner: Advise First Line teams on risk, regulatory change and the control environment, and support our engagement with regulators.

Right now we're broadening what the team covers. We already have strong financial and credit risk skills in the team. This hire closes our gap in technology risk and gives us a second person who can run enterprise risk management end to end. You'll work across a risk universe that spans technology, information security, privacy and operational resilience, alongside product, operational and financial risk.




WHAT YOU BRING

You could step in for the Head of Risk and Control when needed.

 - Technology risk know-how: Hands-on experience applying security, technology and operational resilience risk methodology and standards, with enough depth to challenge technology and security teams credibly. You don't need to be an engineer.

 - Controls testing experience: A track record of ITGC testing or similar control testing and assurance work.

 - The ability to influence: Confidence engaging stakeholders on complex or sensitive risk topics, challenging constructively and being heard.

We're committed to helping you grow here, whether that means deepening your technical expertise, expanding your regulatory knowledge, or stepping into broader leadership responsibilities as the team develops.



WHY IS THIS ROLE A GOOD FIT FOR YOU

This role is a good fit for you if:

HOW YOU'LL DEVELOP IN THIS ROLE

### Cheif Architect

We are seeking a Chief Architect to lead the end-to-end architecture of our next-generation analog chips focused on processing raw sensor data from various 1-D signal sources. You will be the technical center of gravity for new products, owning the spec, driving cross-discipline trade-offs, and guiding the team through the design to align architecture and specifications.

#### Key Responsibilities

**System Architecture & Definition**

- Total System Architecture: Define the end-to-end architecture spanning the IC, its signal chain, sensor interfaces, and the companion MCU and host software interfaces, including the partitioning of functionality between the IC and the customer-side MCU.
- Companion IC Strategy: Specify the IC’s role within a customer system built around an external MCU — defining interfaces (I²S, TDM, SPI, I²C, etc.), control and data flows, latency budgets, and integration guidelines.
-  Trade-off Analysis: Drive architectural trade-offs across power, performance, area, cost, latency, and time-to-market, and clearly document the reasoning behind those decisions.

**IC Development & Release**

- IC Development: Lead system-level specification, design reviews, and interface definition for new ICs, working closely with analog, digital, layout, and verification teams.
- Product Release: Involve the IC release cycle as spec owner
- Cross-functional coordination: Partner with IC design, firmware, applications, and product teams to translate customer requirements into a coherent, executable specification.

#### Requirements

- Education: BS/MS/PhD in Electrical/Radio Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
- Experience: 10+ years in mixed-signal IC or SoC development. Demonstrated experience in defining total system architecture spanning IC, embedded firmware, host software interfaces, and the surrounding MCU, not just a single layer of the stack. MCU & Embedded Knowledge.
- Communication: Ability to write a clean architecture spec, defend it in a room of opinionated specialists, and translate between engineering, product, and customer audiences.

- Global Team: Collaborate with industry experts worldwide.

- Our expertise in building and scaling world-class products.

Who we are.
Precica (precica.ai) is a deep-tech spinout of the University of Manchester, backed by Northern Gritstone and Deeptech Labs. Our product, pdata, compresses data by orders of magnitude whilst keeping it directly queryable — with applications in analytics, ML, querying, and forecasting. We're running live pilots in electricity markets and expanding into unstructured data (video, logs, sensor streams). Precica is an early-stage company with a small founding team, tackling one of the defining infrastructure problems of the coming decade: the cost, energy, and carbon footprint of dark data.

The Role
What you'll do.
We're seeking a Machine Learning Engineer with a focus on neural and learned data compression. The role involves designing, implementing, and optimising compression models that underpin pdata's core engine.
Responsibilities include developing and benchmarking compression pipelines for structured and unstructured data, performing statistical evaluation of rate–distortion and query-accuracy trade-offs, and deploying models into production and pilot environments.
You will work directly with the founding team to translate research advances into scalable product capability, maintain code quality and reproducibility, and contribute to technical documentation and white papers.
As one of the first technical hires, you will have unusual scope to shape the company's technical direction. Responsibility at Precica grows with contribution and with the company itself — those who build the core of the product will be well placed to lead as we scale.

Requirements
What we're looking for.
Essential
• Strong foundation in Computer Science: data structures, algorithms, and software engineering principles.
• Applied expertise in machine learning, with hands-on experience building and tuning models on real-world data.
• In-depth understanding of neural architectures relevant to compression and representation learning.
• Proficiency in statistics, probability, and experimental design for rigorous model evaluation.
• Fluency in Python and modern ML frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn) and adaptability to work across frameworks.
• Experience with large datasets, data pipelines, and version control (Git).
• Ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly and document work thoroughly.
• Degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related field.

Desirable
• Direct experience with neural or learned compression: quantisation-aware training, rate–distortion optimisation, or learned transforms.
• Postgraduate degree or research experience in machine learning, information theory, signal processing, or data compression.
• Background in low-rank or structured representations (e.g. tensor decompositions, sketching, dimensionality reduction).
• Experience with time-series modelling and forecasting, particularly in energy or industrial settings.
• Familiarity with embedding-based retrieval and video/image representation learning (e.g. CLIP-style models, vector search).
• Performance engineering skills: C++, CUDA, or optimisation of inference pipelines for throughput and memory.
• Experience deploying models to production (MLOps, containerisation, CI/CD) and with cloud or HPC environments.
• Publications, open-source contributions, or patents in a relevant area.

Logistics
A few practical details.
• Minimum education: Bachelor's degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience.
• Required field of study: Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related field relevant to the role.
• Minimum years of experience: This is an entry-level role — we weigh demonstrated ability and relevant project or research experience over years on paper.
• Location-based hybrid policy: Precica is based in Manchester, UK. This role is hybrid — specific in-office expectations will be confirmed during the interview process.
• Visa sponsorship: We do not currently sponsor visas — we don't hold a sponsorship licence. You must already have the right to work in the UK to apply for this role.
We encourage you to apply even if you don't believe you meet every single qualification listed. Not all strong candidates tick every box, and research shows that people from underrepresented groups are especially prone to underestimating their own fit — so please don't rule yourself out prematurely. Problems like the one we're solving benefit from a wide range of perspectives, and we're building Precica with that in mind.
Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Precica recruiters only contact you from @precica.ai email addresses — be cautious of emails from other domains claiming to represent us. Legitimate Precica recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links — get in touch with us directly at contact@precica.ai to confirm.

How We're Different
Small team, big infrastructure problem.
We believe infrastructure problems with real cost, energy, and carbon footprint attached deserve first-principles engineering, not incremental fixes. At Precica we work as a small, tightly-knit founding team rather than siloed subteams, and we value shipping real capability into live pilots over polishing research for its own sake. We treat compression as a systems problem as much as a modelling one — we're already running pilots in electricity markets while expanding into unstructured data. As one of our first technical hires, you won't be handed a narrow ticket queue — you'll help define how the core product works.

Preply is one of the largest advertisers in the Education Tech space. Our marketing operations span dozens of languages, thousands of creatives, and multiple acquisition channels. To keep growing at this scale, we need world-class products that take marketing channels to levels of performance impossible to reach manually.

As the Senior Product Manager for MarTech Scale, you'll own the products that scale Preply's marketing channels far beyond what manual effort allows - across Paid Search, SEO, AI Search, Display (Meta, TikTok, etc.), Affiliates, and the next wave of channels yet to emerge.

You'll partner with engineering, data, and marketing teams to build products that efficiently drive new subscribers to Preply at unprecedented scale.

 - Scale paid acquisition channels through Product

   - Shape Preply's positioning in AI Search as discovery shifts from blue links to LLM answers - defining the content, structure, and signals that win on this new surface.
   
   - Continuously evolve the page-creation engine to stay ahead of evolving search behaviour, ranking systems, and AI search tools.

job_description:
Locations: Prague / Brno / London / Dublin
At Productboard, we're building the first agentic product management system. We're rethinking how product management is done in a world full of AI agents, and how we help our customers build what matters for their audience.
For Spark, our AI agent for product teams, to do real work inside an enterprise organization, it has to earn the right to operate there: what it's allowed to do, on whose behalf, with which model, at what cost, how anyone can tell afterwards, and how far it can go on its own. We're looking for a Staff Product Manager to own the Enterprise AI stack that answers those questions: a hands-on senior IC from an AI-first product company who sets the direction for it, drives the initiatives that cut across teams, and personally carries the hardest product problems at the edge of enterprise AI.
You'll own the enterprise AI harness around Spark: the layer that lets an enterprise put agents to work at scale and trust them with more over time. Permissioning, audit, and limits so agents act within the organization's policies. Bring-your-own-model and model routing so every task runs on the right model at the right cost. Agentic automation so agents run on triggers and schedules across a product organization, not only when asked. And the control plane that lets a customer see every agent running, what it costs, how well it performs, and how far it's allowed to go on its own. You'll spend real time with enterprise customers, translate what they need into product, and make sure they get value at scale with the governance they require. The rules for how agents operate inside a company are being written right now, and you'll write them into the product. Our customers are product organizations inside large companies. They need support in how agents are deployed across their organization, and someone to remove the obstacles along the way.
Your responsibilities
• Own the Enterprise AI stack. Set the strategy, roadmap, and outcomes for permissioning, audit, limits, BYOM, model routing, and agentic automation, the layer every agent runs on and every enterprise customer depends on, and give the teams around you a clear view of where it's going and why.
• Turn enterprise needs into product. Spend real time with enterprise customers, from CPOs and product operations to IT, security, and procurement. Understand what it takes to roll agents out to thousands of users, and turn it into capabilities that serve every customer rather than a custom build for one.
• Drive key initiatives across teams. Take on the problems bigger than any one squad: agents that respect a customer's permission model in every action, agents running unattended on schedules and triggers, agents delegating to other agents inside a customer's policies, and autonomy that expands as trust is earned. Frame them, align the org, ship, and measure whether it worked.
• Shape how we measure success. Define the metrics that show governance is enabling value rather than blocking it: adoption depth across an organization, time from contract to agents doing real work, cost per outcome. Use them to close debates.
• Prototype in code by default. When words aren't settling a debate, build the control or the routing policy with AI coding tools and put it in front of customers.
• Raise the bar. Be the first user of Spark for your own work, give sales and customer success a crisp articulation of how Spark's agents are governed, and mentor other PMs through pairing and example.
About you
• 8+ years in product management, all of it hands-on. A senior individual contributor on complex products, with meaningful time in enterprise B2B SaaS, and an AI product used inside large organizations that is visibly better because you owned it.
• Expertise in the enterprise AI stack. You've shipped permissioning, audit, admin controls, usage and cost limits, model choice and routing, or agentic automation for an AI product in production. You understand how permissions flow from people to agents, what an auditable agent action looks like, and why rollouts stall at security review, and you have a view on how an enterprise should expand agent autonomy over time.
• Enterprise customers are your home turf. You're highly skilled at user research, comfortable in the room with enterprise buyers and their security and IT teams, and you've taken a product through security reviews and multi-thousand-seat rollouts. You know how product organizations really work inside large companies, including the messy parts.
• Systems thinker with technical depth. You reason comfortably about identity, permission models, data models, APIs, and model gateways, you understand how LLMs behave in practice, including context, tool use, latency, cost, and non-determinism, and you can hold the whole system in your head while deciding about one part of it.
• Agentic products experience. You've shipped products where an agent does real work on the user's behalf, wrestled with trust, control, and quality evaluation, and have real opinions on how agents should be governed inside structured enterprise software, because you use the newest ones the week they ship.
• AI-first in how you work. AI agents are how you research, synthesize, analyze, and prototype every day. When a debate needs settling, you build it with Claude Code, Cursor, or whatever fits.
• Excellent product instincts. You translate complex systems and governance requirements into simple concepts and elegant experiences, you know that controls people actually use beat controls that merely exist, and you know which parts of the traditional enterprise stack are worth rebuilding for an agentic world.
• Founder mentality, low ego. You own outcomes end to end, turn ambiguity into clear decisions, stand up for what's right with challenging stakeholders, and work in the open with designers and engineers as peers.
• Strategic communicator. You can turn a finding from a customer's security review into a clear decision for an executive, an engineer, and a GTM team, and each leaves clearer than they arrived.
What's in it for you?

Jobs

 Quality Assurance Lead (Lex Academic)

 Posted on: 20th October, 2026. Closing date: 15th November, 2026

 Apply by 15 November for this full-time remote role.

Lex Academic purveys white-glove editing, indexing, and translation services to academics, doctoral candidates, and university presses worldwide, with particular strength in philosophy, classics, and history. Lex Academic seek to appoint a full-time Quality Assurance Lead to take responsibility for the standard of every edited manuscript that leaves the company.

This role reports directly to the Editorial Project Manager and CEO. The role is fully remote.

About the role

This is a full-time remote role for a Quality Assurance Lead. Lex Academic’s editing is carried out by PhD-educated freelance editors working remotely, and no manuscript is returned to a client until it has passed a second, independent check. The Quality Assurance Lead performs that check: a secondary copy-edit of each manuscript (articles, theses, and monographs, predominantly in the humanities and social sciences) once the freelancer has returned it. This involves correcting residual errors of grammar, syntax, punctuation, and spelling; ensuring consistency of style and formatting; verifying that citations and references conform to the required style; and making sure that the editor’s comments and queries to the author are clear, correct, and appropriately phrased. Where a freelancer’s work has fallen short, the Quality Assurance Lead corrects the work (e.g., correctly applying the style guide; improving the mark-up on the text, etc.) and itemizes the shortfalls so that the freelancer can learn and improve.

Each week, the Editorial Project Manager will provide the list of jobs to be quality-controlled. The Quality Assurance Lead works through that list, quality-controlling each project, and reporting back on each manuscript.

Lex Academic are a boutique editorial outfit, so the focus is not on high volumes of work, but exceptionally high quality across around 50 projects per month. The work is deadline-led and spans many citation styles and publishers’ house styles; the Quality Assurance Lead must therefore be able to move between conventions without loss of accuracy and to work to fixed delivery dates. All editorial work is carried out by human experts, without recourse to AI.

Skills and qualities required

• Right to work in the UK (UK passport required)

• At least ten years’ professional experience in proofreading and copy-editing, ideally of academic work (required for shortlisting)

• Native-level command of written English: work arrives in English and demands the highest proficiency in the language

• Proficiency in all major citation styles, including Chicago (notes–bibliography and author–date), MHRA, MLA, APA, Harvard, and OSCOLA

• Outstanding attention to detail, together with the judgement to distinguish an error from an authorial choice

• The ability to assess another editor’s work rigorously and fairly, and to correct its shortcomings precisely

• Impeccable time management and the ability to work to fixed delivery dates across several manuscripts at once

• High degree of competence in Microsoft Word (Track Changes and comments) and Office 365

• A PhD, preferably in the humanities or social sciences (anthropology, philosophy, classics, and history are Lex Academic’s core fields), is strongly preferred

• One or more foreign languages are preferred (most desirable: French, German, Italian, Arabic)

• Proficiency in Adobe Acrobat (for PDF proofreading) and InDesign (for typeset proofs) is very desirable

• When quality-assurance tasks are lighter, you will be required to perform copy-editing tasks, proofreading, and other tasks that fit your experience

Applicants should have at least a very good first degree in the humanities or social sciences, an impeccable command of the English language, and the temperament to check the work of other experts with rigour and tact. Ten years’ professional experience in proofreading and editing will be required for shortlisting. Their preference is for an applicant with higher research degrees and considerable in-house or freelance copy-editing experience. Proficiency in foreign languages is highly desirable. Career development would involve learning how to procure image and textual permissions for monograph publications.

This fully remote role requires exceptional concentration, exactness, and a commitment to delivering editorial work of the highest quality. Lex Academic’s motto is that they never let an academic client down.

Salary: £32,000–42,000 depending on experience (plus pension).

Contract: full-time, remote role.

For more information and to apply, see the Lex Academic website.

 Posted on: 28th October, 2026. Closing date: 6th November, 2026

 Apply by 6 November for this full-time, permanent role based in Edinburgh, Bristol, London or Sheffield.

Who Hachette Learning are and what they do

At Hachette Learning (formerly Hodder Education), there’s one thing they’re certain about. No two students learn the same way. That’s why Hachette Learning’s approach to teaching begins by recognising the needs of individuals first. Their mission is to enable every learner to fulfil their unique potential by empowering those who teach them. From their expert teaching and learning resources to their digital educational tools that make learning easier and more accessible for all, they provide solutions designed to maximise the impact of learning for every teacher, parent and student.

Aligned with their parent company, Hachette Livre, founded in 1826, Hachette Learning are proud to deliver high-quality learning solutions on a global scale. Hachette Learning make it easier for everyone to unlock a new world of learning.

Hachette Learning is a division of Hachette, one of the largest publishing groups in the UK, with 10 publishing divisions and over 60 imprints. Everyone there is proud to be in the business of opening doors and minds.

What you’ll be doing

The successful candidate will lead the strategy, development and commercial performance for a portfolio of Science educational products for UK and International Secondary schools (print and digital). Working at the intersection of customer insight, pedagogy and market opportunity, they will shape the future product roadmap, identifying new opportunities for growth while ensuring products continue to meet the evolving needs of educators and learners.

They will act as a market expert for the Secondary Science portfolio, maintaining a detailed understanding of the competitive landscape across educational publishing and educational technology. They will use customer research, sales data, market analysis and competitor intelligence to identify opportunities that inform product strategy and investment priorities, making evidence-based decisions that maximise both educational impact and commercial success.

Working collaboratively across product, platform, editorial, technology, data, sales and marketing teams, they will oversee the full product lifecycle, from concept and business case development through to launch, optimisation and ongoing portfolio management. They will champion the voice of the customer, build strong relationships with authors and external partners, and drive innovation through inclusive, accessible and high-quality learning experiences that deliver value for customers and help to position the organisation as a trusted leader in Secondary Science education.

Who they are looking for

Hachette Learning are looking for an experienced product professional with a strong track record of conceptualising, developing and launching commercially successful educational products and resources for UK and/or International schools, within the Science subject area. You will have experience evaluating market opportunities, analysing commercial performance and using evidence to inform strategic product and investment decisions. You bring a deep understanding of how effective teaching and learning happens in the classroom, how students learn, the impact of curriculum and assessment developments, and the strengths and weaknesses of the print and digital products currently used in schools. You will be skilled at translating customer insight, educational best practice, emerging market trends and opportunities into high-quality products that deliver meaningful outcomes for both educators and learners.

The ideal candidate will have a strong understanding of the Secondary Science market, including knowledge of market trends, print and digital resources used, and challenges faced by teachers and students in schools, and a proven ability to engage with the teaching community to identify and respond to their needs. You will be an excellent collaborator and communicator, comfortable working across cross-functional teams, engaging with customers and educators, and building relationships with authors and external partners. Connections within Science education networks, subject associations or professional organisations would be highly advantageous, helping you to stay close to curriculum developments, emerging trends and the evolving needs of the Science education community.

Location: Bristol, Edinburgh, London, Sheffield

Salary: £50,000-£60,000 dependent on experience and location

Contact: Full time, permanent

Machine Learning Engineer / AI Research Engineer
We're looking for a Machine Learning Engineer / AI Research Engineer to join our small core team. This is a hands-on role sitting at the intersection of modern machine learning and quantum computing — with two complementary directions.
Two directions
• ML for quantum — using neural networks and learning-based methods to accelerate quantum computation (e.g. circuit optimisation and compilation, error mitigation, calibration, variational-parameter optimisation, and surrogate modelling of quantum processes).
• ML on/with quantum — building and adapting classical AI methods, including neural networks and large language models, so they can benefit from quantum hardware and algorithms.
You don't need to be a world expert in either quantum or LLMs — but you should be genuinely comfortable with neural networks and excited to grow into the rest.

What the role looks like
• You'll work across the full lifecycle — research, design, coding, evaluation, and iteration.
• You'll design, train, and evaluate neural networks for both of the directions above.
• You'll help train, fine-tune, host, and serve models — including LLMs. Some of this you'll already know; parts you'll pick up on the job.
• You'll turn recent papers into working code, and working code into product.
• You'll collaborate closely with our quantum scientists, our CTO, and leading researchers at the University of Cambridge.
• You'll take real ownership of projects in a fast-moving, high-impact field.
This is a small, highly motivated team in central Cambridge. The environment is collaborative, relaxed, and academic — freedom to think creatively and work independently. Innovation gets celebrated. Achievements get rewarded.

What we're looking for
Essential
• Strong Python, with good software-engineering habits (Git, testing, reproducible experiments).
• Solid grounding in machine learning / deep-learning fundamentals — you can build, train, and debug neural networks from scratch in a modern framework (PyTorch, JAX, or similar).
• Demonstrable hands-on experience: research projects, publications, internships, open-source, or production work.
• Comfortable reading ML papers and reimplementing them.
• A fast learner who's happy with ambiguity and wants ownership.
Desirable (or willing to learn)
• Experience with LLMs: fine-tuning (LoRA / PEFT / full), serving and hosting (e.g. vLLM, TGI, Ollama), and distributed or multi-GPU training.
• Familiarity with GPUs, cloud, and containers (Docker, etc.).
• Background in optimisation, Bayesian methods, reinforcement learning, or time-series modelling.
• Exposure to quantum computing or quantum frameworks (Qiskit, Cirq, PennyLane) — not required, we'll happily teach it.

Send your CV and cover letter to recruitment@qubitera.io.

**A bit about the work**

Good backend development turns lines of code into something that actually works — an app, an integration, a website that quietly does clever things in the background. In e-commerce, that background work is where a lot of the value (and the revenue) lives.

Most retailers don’t have the skills to make their systems talk to each other — they can’t wire up the third party that runs their warehouse, their subscriptions, their ERP or their loyalty programme, and the data ends up stranded where it’s no use to anyone. That’s where we come in — and increasingly, it’s the kind of work we want to do more of.

So this time we’re after a backend developer: someone who’s comfortable in the server-side, cares about a well-structured database, and enjoys the challenge of making two systems that were never designed to talk to each other work together.

**Who are we?**

We’re Quickfire Digital — an award-winning e-commerce development agency and Shopify Platinum Partner, based in Norwich. We work with scale-hungry DTC and retail brands, from traditional retailers who want the whole thing managed for them, through to some genuinely weird and wonderful businesses who just want a seamless way to get people to buy their products.

We’re busy, we’ve got ambitious growth plans, and alongside our Shopify build work we’re diversifying into application development and a few other fun areas when the project’s right for the studio. That’s exactly the kind of work this role leans into.

**What is the job?**

You’ll report to our Head of Development and our Senior Backend Developer, working as part of the dev team. This is a hands-on build role — focused on writing great backend code, not managing people. As a Shopify Platinum Partner, much of your work will centre on the Shopify ecosystem: building the integrations and backend services that sit in and around our clients’ stores. You’ll be the person we point at the harder server-side problems. In a nutshell, your duties and responsibilities will be…

- Building and maintaining backend systems in PHP and Laravel — custom functionality, internal tools, application work and the bits of client projects that go beyond the theme.
- Designing and building third party API integrations — connecting Shopify and our clients’ wider tech stacks (ERPs, PIMs, subscription platforms, warehouses, loyalty, payment providers and the rest).
- Database design and management — sensible table structures, migrations, and data that’s modelled to last.
- Handling data transposition, migration and integration work as part of build and replatforming projects.
- Assisting the development team with software design, code and problem-solving across projects.
- Writing clean, documented, testable code — documentation comes as standard with your work here.
- Working on bug fixes and helping keep the codebase healthy.
- Attending and contributing to development meetings, and giving the Head of Development / PM team honest estimations and milestone updates.
- Engaging with clients where needed — explaining the technical side in human language and telling us what we need from them to move a project forward.
- Occasionally rolling up your sleeves and getting stuck into our internal projects (we build our own tools too).

**Who are we looking for?**

We’re after a solid, effective mid-level developer who can hit the ground running and add real value — this is a growth role off the back of some recent project wins and expanding accounts. It’s not a junior position, so we do need to see demonstrable commercial experience — ideally two to four years working with PHP — but you don’t need to be at senior level. This is a great step for someone ready to take on meatier backend and integration work.

If you’ve been an in-house backend dev seeking more variety in your projects and fancy trying agency life? Brilliant — this could be a great match.

**The essentials:**

- Solid, demonstrable experience with PHP and Laravel — this is the core of the role.
- Strong MySQL and relational database skills: table design, infrastructure and implementation best practice.
- Experience with background jobs and queues (Laravel Horizon) — a lot of our integration work runs on these.
- A habit of writing automated tests (PHPUnit or Pest).
- Confident with Git-based version control and a clean branching / pull-request workflow.
- Working knowledge of the front-end fundamentals — HTML, CSS and JavaScript — enough to work across the stack when a job calls for it.
- Experience with data transposition, migration and integration processes.
- Comfortable using AI tooling as part of your everyday development workflow — it’s a normal part of how we work here, not a novelty.
- The ability to write clean, maintainable, well-documented code and manage your own workload across multiple projects at varying stages.
- Comfortable in a collaborative, sprint-based team working to tight deadlines — someone who can help clear a backlog effectively.
- Au fait with the usual kit: wikis, Slack, G-Suite and time-tracking software.

**The bonuses (these are what’ll make you stand out):**

- Shopify experience — a big plus for us. As a Shopify Platinum Partner, most of what we build lives in and around the Shopify ecosystem, so hands-on experience with the Shopify Admin API, app development, or headless / integration work will put you right at home.
- Third party API integration experience — REST and GraphQL. If you’ve built and maintained integrations between commerce platforms and external systems, we really want to hear from you.
- Node.js and Cloudflare Workers — we use these across recent projects and our own internal tooling, so experience here is a real plus.
- Deployment and server management, ideally with Laravel Forge.
- Experience with CI/CD pipelines and Docker.
- Familiarity with Vue.js or React.
- Previous agency experience, or experience in a **fast-paced multi-project dev setting**.

**What’s in it for you?**

Let’s be upfront — we’re not Meta or Google, and we can’t match those salaries. But nor do you get the relentless pressure that tends to come with them. What we can offer…

- A genuinely competitive salary for the Norfolk tech scene. We did the research.
- Hybrid working — 3 days in the office, 2 at home, negotiable once you’ve passed probation. We’d love you to be Norfolk or Suffolk based for a comfortable commute (this isn’t a remote-only role — much of the team’s in most days and the office atmosphere is a big part of who we are).
- Free parking on site, in a spot that’s convenient for commuting.
- A non-corporate environment — jeans and a t-shirt far more likely than a shirt and chinos.
- A competitive holiday allowance.
- Private medical cover — even as a small business, we’ve got benefits.
- Company pension scheme.
- Half-yearly salary reviews, with regular reward and incentives, plus a financial bonus at Christmas if we’ve had a good year.
- A bustling social calendar and an office rammed with treats — we get a lot of swag sent to us and you’ll benefit from it.
- The best biscuit drawer in Norfolk. We’re quietly confident on this one.

**What’s the interview process?**

Nice and simple — no endless multi-stage process here.

1. A chat with our Head of Development — your chance to ask everything you need, talk through your experience, and decide if we’re the place for you. Usually a call or video call.
2. A technical task, so we can see how you think and work. Nothing designed to trip you up — just a fair look at how you approach a real-world problem.
3. A final interview with one of our co-founders and the Head of Development, in person — so you can see the office, meet the team and get a proper feel for the place.
4. Then we make you an offer, and hopefully you say yes.
