The Opportunity
Rackspace Technology has a strategic partnership with one of the world’s largest enterprise go to market partners. Through it, our cloud services & AI solutions are sold to that partner’s enterprise customer base by the partner’s own sales organisation. This is a rare chance to build a new route to market at scale.
As Enterprise Account Manager, you will be the face of Rackspace inside the partner’s sales organisation. You won’t be working a named list of end customers. Your customer is the partner’s sellers, and your job is to make sure Rackspace is the first name they think of when a client needs cloud, data, security or AI. You’ll build relationships across their account teams, equip them to position us with confidence, and get Rackspace pulled into the right customer opportunities early.

What you will do
Build and grow relationships across the partner’s sales organisation
• Establish yourself as a trusted, visible figure with the partner’s sellers, account directors, sales leaders and specialists across industries and regions.
• Run a structured engagement plan: regular account reviews, one-to-ones, team meetings and joint events, so Rackspace stays front of mind.
• Gain access to the partner’s wider sales community, and open doors for Rackspace’s own executives and technical teams.
Drive pipeline through the partner
• Identify the partner accounts and opportunities where Rackspace’s cloud, managed services, data, security and AI offerings add value, and shape joint opportunity plans around them.
• Get Rackspace pulled into customer deals at the right stage, working alongside partner sellers from first conversation through to close.
• Take ownership of opportunity registration, qualification and pipeline progression, keeping forecasts accurate and visible.
• Work with partner sellers and Rackspace Solutions Architects on discovery, solution design and proposals, including RFI and RFP responses and commercial negotiation.
Enable and promote
• Educate and inspire the partner’s sellers on the full Rackspace portfolio, including our AI solutions and compute, through briefings, workshops, use-case stories and joint customer wins.
• Create simple, credible messaging that makes it easy for a seller who isn’t a Rackspace product portfollio specialist to spot an opportunity and bring us in.
• Partner with Rackspace marketing on joint campaigns, events, case studies and customer references.
Own the partnership commercially
• Build and run a joint business plan, with clear targets, priorities and cadence, and report on progress to Rackspace leadership and the partner.
• Understand how the partner’s sellers are measured and rewarded and use that to make selling Rackspace the easy choice for them.
• Act as the voice of the partner inside Rackspace, bringing back feedback to product, pre-sales, legal and commercial teams, and resolving issues quickly.

What you will bring
Essential
• Proven track record of selling technology services through a large partner, systems integrator, carrier, distributor or alliance, or of selling alongside a partner’s sales team in a co-sell model.
• A sales-focused account management background, with a history of meeting or exceeding quota in enterprise IT, cloud, managed services or a comparable sector.
• Outstanding networking and relationship-building skills. You are comfortable earning credibility with people you don’t manage and who have no obligation to sell for you.
• Ability to influence without authority, from frontline sellers to senior leaders.
• Strong commercial acumen: you can qualify, structure and negotiate complex, multi-party deals, and handle RFIs and RFPs.
• Excellent communication and presentation skills, in writing and in person.
• Self-starter who is organised enough to manage a broad network and a long-cycle pipeline, while still delivering in-year numbers.
Desirable
• Knowledge of the cloud landscape (public, private and hybrid cloud, managed services, FinOps and migration), and an appetite for AI, data and compute.
• Experience in regulated or public sector markets, or with sovereignty and data-residency requirements.
• Familiarity with partner programmes, deal registration, joint business planning and partner-led marketing.
• CRM experience (we use [Salesforce]) and disciplined pipeline management.
• Professional sales training and a recognised sales methodology.

What success looks like
First 90 days: You’ve met and built early relationships with the key partner sellers and leaders, and you understand how the partner sells, is organised and is rewarded. You have a joint plan agreed and your first opportunities in the pipeline.
First year: Rackspace is a known, trusted name across the partner’s sales force. You have a healthy, partner-influenced and partner-sourced pipeline, repeatable enablement and a growing list of joint wins. You will have built strong relationships with our partners GTM sellers and fully positioned Rackspace’s capabilities with that community.

 Job summary

 Make a Real Impact in Cancer Care as a Band 7 Engineer at The Christie NHS Foundation Trust

If you are motivated by work that truly matters this is your opportunity to play a vital role in supporting cancer patients throughout their treatment journey by ensuring the reliability and performance of essential medical imaging and radiotherapy equipment. We are seeking a dedicated and skilled engineer to join our team.

You will be a key contributor to the safe and effective delivery of our services, taking responsibility for both planned and corrective maintenance across a diverse portfolio of advanced medical imaging and radiotherapy equipment. Helping to ensure that our clinical teams can deliver world class care every day.

We are looking for an enthusiastic, adaptable professional with engineering knowledge to at least HND level. You will bring strong problem solving abilities, excellent communication skills, and the confidence to work under pressure on complex technical challenges.

Experience with medical devices or quality management systems such as ISO 9001, ISO 13485, or ISO 14971 is highly desirable, though not essential for the right candidate.

If you are driven by purpose, thrive in a collaborative environment, and want to contribute to life changing patient care, we would be delighted to hear from you.

 Main duties of the job

 This role is critical in ensuring the safety, reliability and performance of specialist medical technology used in cancer diagnosis and treatment. Core responsibilities typically include:

Radiology equipment maintenance -- Acting as a primary engineering lead for the Radiology department, delivering planned preventative maintenance & timely corrective repairs across a wide range of imaging systems to minimise downtime & support uninterrupted clinical services.

Technical fault investigation -- Diagnosing complex equipment issues under time pressure, applying advanced engineering principles to restore functionality & ensure devices remain safe & compliant.

Quality and safety compliance -- Working within existing quality frameworks, contributing to documentation, risk assessments & adherence to ISO standards.

Cross departmental support -- Providing secondary engineering support to the Radiotherapy department, assisting with maintenance activities on high precision treatment equipment.

Collaborative service delivery -- Working closely with clinical, technical & managerial teams to ensure equipment availability, communicate technical findings clearly, & contribute to a responsive, patient centred service.

Continuous improvement -- Identifying opportunities to enhance equipment performance, maintenance processes & service efficiency through proactive monitoring & professional development.

 About us

 The Christie is one of Europe's leading cancer centres, looking after more than 64,000 patients a year. We are based in Manchester and serve a population of 3.2 million across Greater Manchester & Cheshire, but as a national specialist around 25% patients are referred to us from other parts of the country.

We are the largest radiotherapy provider in the NHS with one in 20 treatments delivered at The Christie. We have up to 15 linear accelerators operating across our network of sites. We operate the largest chemotherapy unit in the UK on our main site and treatments are also provided at 13 other networked sites, and in patients homes. And as a specialist tertiary surgical centre, we focus on rare cancers, complex procedures, and multidisciplinary approaches to cancer surgery, specialising in colorectal, peritoneal, gynaecological, urological and plastic surgery.

We are also an international leader in research, with world first breakthroughs for over 100 years. We have been named by the UK's National Institute for Health Research (NIHR), as one of the best hospitals providing opportunities for patients to participate in clinical research studies, with more than 800 studies open at any time, caring for over 3,000 patients.

About the role

A hands-on analyst for a consumer energy business: pay-as-you-go cooking gas (LPG) delivered to hundreds of thousands of households in fast-growing emerging markets. You own the analysis end to end — framing the question, getting the data, building the numbers and defending them in front of the people who will act on them. You work directly with commercial, operations, finance and management, and with our founders — no account manager in between.

You join our energy data team, alongside a senior data scientist and a data & BI engineer. A meaningful part of the work starts in raw tables, meter logs, payment exports and field-operations files rather than in a tidy warehouse.

We do not require you to come from oil & gas. The business model is much closer to a prepaid mobile operator than to a fuel station: customers top up credit with mobile money, consume in small amounts, and every unit used is recorded by a smart meter. Experience at mobile network operators, telecoms, mobile money or fintech, utilities with prepaid metering, pay-as-you-go solar, and similar high-volume B2C businesses is directly relevant.

What the work looks like

Each customer home has a stove, a smart meter and a gas cylinder owned and maintained by the company. Customers pay only for the gas they use, topping up as little as a single meal’s worth through mobile money, and local technicians replace cylinders before they run out. That produces rich data — consumption, top-ups, cylinder swaps, deliveries, meter events — and commercial questions to match: which customers stay and why, what a customer is worth, where the network makes or loses money, and what to do about it.

Scope

• Customer analytics — acquisition, activation, retention and churn, cohort behaviour, revenue and margin per household, lifetime value against the cost of installation

• Consumption and top-up behaviour — frequency and size of top-ups, usage patterns, seasonality, early signs that a customer is about to go dormant

• Pricing and promotion analysis — the effect of price, top-up incentives and campaigns on usage and margin, measured against proper baselines and control groups

• Field operations and unit economics — cylinder swap and delivery efficiency, depot and area performance, technician productivity, cost to serve per household

• Forecasting gas demand, cylinder logistics and revenue by area, to support supply, stock and expansion decisions

• Anomaly and fraud detection — meter tampering, consumption that does not match cylinder swaps, payment irregularities, unusual field activity

• Reporting with single agreed definitions where commercial, operations and finance count customers, revenue or volume differently

• Messy data as the normal case: meter connectivity gaps, delayed payment records, re-assigned devices, data from more than one country and system

Requirements

• 4+ years as a data analyst or in a comparable analytical role, owning your own analyses from question to recommendation

• Experience with high-volume B2C transactional data — prepaid mobile or telecoms, mobile money, utilities, pay-as-you-go energy, retail or similar. You know what subscriber-, account- or transaction-level data looks like and where it lies

• Commercial analytics in practice: churn and retention, cohort and lifetime-value analysis, segmentation, pricing or campaign evaluation

• Strong SQL and Python (pandas or similar), and readiness to work in raw data yourself: unfamiliar schemas, undocumented tables, exports never meant for analysis

• Sound statistics for business questions — baselines, control groups, seasonality, telling a real effect from noise

• Working with coding agents, seriously. Agents write most of the code here. Bad agent output in analysis fails silently: a join fans out rows, a filter drops half the active customers, a top-up is attributed to the wrong month. We hire for verification habits, not speed — row-count and population checks, reconciliation against a number someone already trusts, a traceable path from raw data to any figure a decision-maker sees

• Experience with a BI tool (Power BI, Tableau, Metabase, Superset or similar)

• Clear communication: you can explain a result, its limits and what to do about it to a non-technical manager

• English sufficient to present findings and defend methodology

• Professional proficiency in Russian

Nice to have

• Experience in emerging markets or with mobile money data

• Experience with IoT, smart-meter or device data

• Field operations or logistics analytics — routing, depots, delivery efficiency

• Experience with experimentation or A/B testing at scale

What we offer

• Ownership of customer and commercial analytics, and room to shape how it is done

• Direct access to founders and decision-makers; short feedback loops

• Generous AI tooling budget — frontier models are a working expense, not a perk

• Hybrid working from our London office

• Competitive compensation, discussed individually

How to apply

Share your CV and an answer to any of the questions below, at your choice. Applications without answers are not reviewed.

• After a top-up bonus campaign in one city, the number of top-ups rose 20%, but gas consumed per household barely changed and revenue per household fell. Marketing calls it a success, finance calls it a loss. How would you work out what actually happened, what data would you need, and what would you deliver?

• Give a real case where two teams or two systems reported different numbers for the same customers, subscribers, revenue or churn. What were the figures, why did they differ, which one did the business treat as truth, and what did you change?

• Show a real prompt or task brief you gave an agent for an analysis, and what it produced. Then one case where agent output looked right and was numerically wrong: what was wrong, how you caught it, what check you added.

• Which transactional or customer systems have you personally pulled data from — billing or CRM at a telecom operator, mobile money or payment platforms, smart-meter or IoT data, POS, ERP? Pick one and tell us something about its data that only someone who has used it would know.

**About Reversec** 

At Reversec, we deliver research-led cyber security services that help organisations defend against real-world threats and build long-term resilience. Our consultants are a diverse team of highly skilled technical experts, researchers, and creative problem-solvers who are passionate about advancing the cyber security industry.  

We believe great consultants are empowered consultants. Our people take ownership of their professional development, contribute to meaningful research, and have the freedom to shape the way we work. If you're driven by curiosity, enjoy solving complex technical challenges, and thrive in an environment that values innovation and continuous learning, we'd love to hear from you. 

**The Role** 

Reversec is a specialist security consultancy built on deep technical expertise, research, and real-world security engineering. Our consultants regularly analyse highly obfuscated software, reverse engineer complex applications, develop custom tooling, and contribute to open-source security projects used throughout the industry. Reversec maintains Android security tooling such as Drozer and invests heavily in research-led capability development.   

We are seeking Android reverse engineers and malware analysts across all experience levels (from those building their skills to seasoned experts) to join a specialist team supporting one of the world's largest technology platforms.  

As an Android Malware Reverse Engineering Analyst, you will investigate complex and evasive Android applications, identify malicious functionality, conduct detailed reverse engineering, and support automated detection development.  

You will work as part of a specialist malware analysis team responsible for investigating applications that fall outside standard analysis processes and require advanced technical expertise. This includes malware research, incident investigations, escalation handling, detection engineering, and quality assurance activities.  

We're recruiting analysts across multiple career stages, from aspiring reverse engineers to experienced malware researchers. Your responsibilities and the expectations placed on you will depend directly on the experience you bring. Experienced analysts will take on complex samples and investigations with a high degree of independence, provide mentorship to junior team members, and assist in developing internal tooling and processes. Analysts earlier in their careers will carry out similar categories of work, with closer support and a remit that grows as their skills develop. Wherever you start, training will be available to bring you up to the standard the team works to. 

**Key Responsibilities** 

All analysts contribute across the areas below. The complexity of the cases assigned to you, the degree of independence expected of you, and any additional oversight and reporting duties will reflect your experience. 

**Malware Reverse Engineering** 

- Perform detailed static and dynamic analysis of Android applications and SDKs. 

- Analyse heavily obfuscated Java/Kotlin applications, native code, and framework applications (e.g., Flutter, .NET MAUI, React Native). 

- Investigate packers, in-memory loading techniques, encrypted payloads and anti-analysis mechanisms. 

- Determine application behaviour and identify potentially harmful functionality.  

**Investigation & Incident Response** 

- Conduct complex investigations into suspicious applications and malware campaigns. 

- Support escalations and urgent high-priority investigations. 

- Analyse internal and external malware leads. 

- Identify indicators, behaviours, attack techniques and attacker objectives.  

**Detection Engineering** 

- Develop and validate detection logic and automated rules. 

- Support improvements to malware detection capabilities. 

- Work with analysts and engineering teams to improve investigative efficiency.  

**Quality & Peer Review** 

- Review analysis performed by other analysts. 

- Validate technical findings and enforcement decisions. 

- Ensure consistent technical standards and reporting quality.  

**Research & Tool Development** 

- Develop one-off tools, scripts and automation to support investigations. 

- Contribute to internal research initiatives. 

- Stay current with evolving Android threats, malware techniques and analysis methodologies. 

**Experience and Expectations** 

We do not require a fixed profile. Instead, we will calibrate expectations to the experience you bring. 

\*\*In all cases, you will need:\*\* 

- Strong programming fundamentals in at least one object-oriented language. 

- A genuine interest in Android internals and how malicious software works. 

- An investigative mindset – curiosity, persistence, and attention to detail. 

- Clear written and spoken communication in English. 

If you are an experienced analyst, we expect proven experience in one or more of: Android malware analysis, Android application security testing, mobile application reverse engineering, malware research, threat research, or mobile threat intelligence. You should be able to demonstrate skills across Java and Android internals, Smali and DEX analysis, Android application architecture, static and dynamic analysis techniques, analysis of obfuscated code, native Android libraries (C/C), and scripting or tool development (e.g. Python). In return, you will be trusted to work independently on complex cases from an early stage, lead urgent escalations, review the work of others and mentor colleagues. 

If you are earlier in your career, we do not expect the above on day one. Show us evidence that you enjoy understanding how software works and are actively developing technical security skills - CTFs, crackmes, personal reverse engineering projects, relevant coursework or published write-ups. You will receive structured training and mentoring to bring you up to the team's standard, and your responsibilities will expand as your capability does. 

Candidates anywhere between these two points are equally welcome: tell us what you can already do, and we will shape both expectations and training around it. 

Work is allocated according to capability and experience. All analysts receive structured mentoring, peer review and continuous technical development 

**Technical Skills** 

An ideal candidate will demonstrate experience with some of the following: 

- Reverse engineering and static analysis – use of decompilers and disassemblers, particularly to tackle heavily obfuscated code, native libraries, and custom cryptography 

- Dynamic analysis – frameworks like Frida and LSPosed particularly welcome 

- Malware analysis – detection development, behavioural analysis - Software development – Kotlin, Java, Python, C/C 

**Why Join Reversec?**

Because the work here is hard, and that’s the point. We are a research-led organisation with expertise recognized across the industry, and the problems we take on rarely come with cookie-cutter answers. You’ll solve them alongside some of the strongest security specialists in the field. 

We’ll invest in you too – through internal training, mentoring, and room to develop. What you build here won’t stay internal: our tooling, research, and methodologies are used throughout the security community. 

**Advice for Candidates** 

We expect this role to attract a significant number of applications. If you want yours to stand out, focus on helping us understand what is genuinely relevant about you. 

We Read Covering Letters 

We genuinely read covering letters, and they often make the difference between two otherwise similar applications. 

A covering letter is your opportunity to explain: 

- Why this area of security interests you. 

- What relevant experience, projects, research, or personal work you've completed. 

- What you've been learning recently. 

- Why you believe your skills are relevant to the role. 

Don't tell us what you think we want to hear. Tell us what genuinely interests you. 

A candidate who can clearly explain why they enjoy reverse engineering Android applications, analysing malware, writing tooling, researching software internals, or investigating complex technical problems will stand out far more than a generic application submitted to dozens of employers. 

**Tell Us What Excites You About the Subject** 

We're much more interested in why you're interested in the work than why you're interested in Reversec. 

We're looking for people who are excited by questions such as: 

- How does this application actually work? 

- What is this code trying to hide? 

- Why is this behaviour occurring? 

- How can this analysis be automated? 

- How can software be understood more deeply? 

Genuine curiosity and enthusiasm for the subject are often stronger indicators of success than a particular certification or job title. 

Differentiate Yourself 

Help us understand: 

- What you've built. 

- What you've researched. 

- What you've reverse engineered. 

- What you've learned outside of formal education or employment. 

- What areas of Android security or malware analysis genuinely interest you. 

Relevant personal projects, technical write-ups, open-source contributions, tooling, university work, challenge participation, and research are all valuable evidence of interest and capability. 

**What to Expect from the Recruitment Process** 

Our recruitment process is designed to help both sides determine whether this is the right fit. 

Step One - CV Review 

Our team will review your application to understand your background, technical skills, experience, aptitude, and overall suitability for the role. 

We are not looking for a perfect checklist match. We're looking for evidence of capability, potential, curiosity, and genuine interest in the subject matter.

Step Two - Initial Interview 

You'll meet with a member of our team to discuss the role, your background, and your experience. 

This conversation is as much for you as it is for us. We're assessing whether the role is a good fit for your skills and aspirations, while giving you the opportunity to understand the work we do, the team you'll be joining, and whether Reversec is the right fit for you. 

Step Three - Technical Challenge 

Candidates who successfully complete the initial interview will be invited to complete a technical challenge. 

The challenge will be representative of the type of work performed by the team and may include activities such as reverse engineering, malware analysis, software investigation, tooling development, or technical problem solving. 

You'll be provided with instructions, any required files or supporting material, and a defined timeframe in which to complete the exercise. We expect candidates to work independently and document their findings as they go. 

Your output should explain: 

- Your approach to the problem. 

- The analysis you performed. 

- Any findings or conclusions you reached. 

- Any limitations, assumptions, or questions that remain unanswered. 

There is rarely a single "correct" answer. We are interested not only in whether you reach the right conclusion, but also in how you think, how you investigate technical problems, and how clearly you communicate your findings. 

This challenge will be time bound; however we understand applicants may have work and personal commitments, and we are happy to discuss reasonable adjustments where required. 

Completed challenges should be returned to the hiring manager within the specified timeframe. 

Step Four - Technical Interview 

You'll meet with members of the technical team for a deeper discussion around your technical background, problem-solving approach, and relevant experience. 

The goal is not to catch you out or test obscure facts. We want to understand how you think, how you approach technical challenges, and how your skills align with the work we perform. 

For experienced candidates, this may involve detailed discussions around reverse engineering, malware analysis, security research, development, or tooling. For less experienced candidates, we're often just as interested in your reasoning, curiosity, and willingness to learn.

Rivan Industries (Rivan.com) is a synthetic fuel company designed to decarbonise heavy industry. We aim to make synthetic fuel cheaper than fossil fuels and sustain life on earth by keeping the CO2 locked underground.

We design and manufacture modular synthetic fuel plants consisting of a DAC system, an Alkaline Electrolyser, and a Sabatier Reactor, whilst vertically integrating with off-grid DC solar and the European gas-grid. We’ve recently deployed the UK’s largest synthetic fuel plant and are planning to 1000x this scale in the next 2 years.

You take our sites from design through construction and commissioning to a working asset exporting gas to the grid, on programme and on budget. You start with Rivan’s first commercial project and move quickly to 50 MW and 100 MW sites, each deployed faster than the last. You lead the project engineers, construction and commissioning teams, own the critical path, and run the relationships that keep the programme moving.

The role

• Navigate the project from site design through construction and commissioning to a working asset exporting gas to the grid.

• Collect and manage all project requirements, from the gas network, planning conditions, lenders, offtaker and our own systems, and hold the team and contractors to them.

• Own the programme and its critical path. Know what is on it, protect it and pull it forward.

• Own the budget and risk register and act early when either moves.

• Integrate the site engineering packages with the Rivan systems delivered by our R&D and Manufacturing teams.

• Run the relationships that drive the programme, including the gas network, landowners, planning and highway authorities, suppliers and lenders’ advisers.

• Prepare the gate decision packs and the handover to operations.

• Work from the factory HQ and be on site most weeks once construction starts.

• Capture learnings from every project into the project delivery framework so the next site deploys faster.

Core skills

• You have delivered a large, complex project end to end, ideally a process plant or energy project, and know what it takes to get from drawings to a working asset.

• You have an engineering background and read structural, electrical and process drawings well enough to ask the right questions where you’re not the expert.

• You reason from first principles. When told that’s how it’s always done, you work out the real requirement and whether there is a better way.

• You are commercially sharp. You have reasoned a price down on evidence and kept scopes tight to avoid creep.

• You align incentives so external parties stay on our timeline and budget.

• You run design, procurement, construction, commissioning and stakeholder workstreams at the same time and keep each moving against the critical path without losing the detail.

• You stay calm under pressure and write clearly.

• Experience in both the UK and Europe is valuable.

Specifics

• £75 - 100k Salary depending on experience

• Share options as part of the early team

• Extensive relocation support, including £6000 per year extra to live close to our HQ

• In-person work at our HQ in Bermondsey, South-East London – flexibility considered based on personal circumstances

• Private health insurance

• Visa sponsorship available

• Unlimited time off

We encourage exceptional applicants from all backgrounds to apply for this role, even if they do not meet all the requirements listed.

About the role

As we scale and strengthen our financial control environment, we are transforming our finance and business systems — including a NetSuite implementation delivered to PCAOB and SOX 404(a) standards, alongside the wider platform landscape (including CRM, stock administration, AP, treasury, FP&A and BI) and their integrations.

Reporting to the Group Financial Controller, the Finance Systems Accountant is the finance-side expert who makes this happen. This is a hands-on, delivery-focused role for a qualified accountant who will spend all of their time on our finance business systems. Your job is to do the analysis and legwork that facilitates good decisions from key stakeholders, and then to execute those decisions into the platforms. A key part of the role is enabling successful implementations through high-quality data set-up, including data migration, and strong stakeholder management throughout.

What you will do

• Gather and document business-platform requirements from across the organisation, so decisions are well-informed

• Develop business-platform architecture options and evaluate the technology stack against Riverlane’s objectives, presenting clear recommendations for stakeholders to decide

• Build implementation plans and a sequenced systems roadmap for stakeholder agreement, balancing priorities, bandwidth and the external audit timetable

• Run the process to identify and evaluate third-party implementation partners, and make recommendations — the appointment decision sits with stakeholders

• Lead the internal finance work on implementations — requirements, chart-of-accounts and data-model design, master data, data migration, configuration input, testing and acceptance — coordinating the chosen implementation partners

• Set up and migrate high-quality data — a key enabler of every implementation. Own the finance-side data workstream: defining data requirements and standards, cleansing and validating source data, mapping and reconciling it, and planning and running data migration and post-migration checks, so each system goes live on complete, accurate, well-structured data.

• Deliver the NetSuite implementation to PCAOB and SOX 404(a) standards, ensuring the platforms produce auditable, well-controlled outputs; work closely with our internal-controls specialist, who designs the controls, to execute those designs into the systems

• Own systems change management — documenting process and configuration changes, securing the appropriate approvals, and maintaining a clear audit trail (a requirement of our external auditors)

• Support the wider platform landscape — CRM, stock administration, AP, treasury, FP&A and BI — and the integrations into NetSuite, helping keep change across systems coordinated

• Document business processes and systems as they are built, feeding audit-readiness and the finance team’s process documentation

• Manage stakeholders across finance, IT and the wider business — keeping the CFO, Group Financial Controller, Head of IT and function owners informed and aligned, and acting as the connective tissue between them and the implementation partners

• Plan the handover of each system into business-as-usual, working with the ERP Administrator and Head of IT

What we need

• Qualified accountant (ACA, ACMA/CIMA or ACCA)

• Proven, hands-on experience implementing and configuring finance systems, ideally NetSuite (OneWorld / multi-entity, multi-currency)

• Experience across several finance-system implementations, including requirements, testing and go-live

• Strong data-migration and data-quality experience — cleansing, mapping, reconciliation and validation — with the rigour to land implementations on accurate, well-structured data

• Strong understanding of core finance processes (GL, AP, AR, fixed assets, intercompany, month-end close, revenue recognition) — you speak finance, not just systems

• Experience designing chart-of-accounts / data models and setting up master data in a multi-entity environment

• Awareness of building systems for control and auditability — access, change management, segregation of duties and data integrity (IT general controls)

• Excellent stakeholder management and communication — able to influence and align senior decision-makers without owning the decision

• Organised, delivery-focused and comfortable prioritising and working to tight deadlines

• Highly motivated and hardworking, with the energy and enthusiasm to achieve ambitious targets

Even better if you have…

• Experience implementing finance systems to PCAOB / SOX 404(a) or comparable public-company control standards

• Experience in a company operating to US public-company reporting and control standards

• Experience with the wider platform stack — CRM (e.g. Salesforce), AP automation, treasury, FP&A and BI tools — and integrating them with an ERP

• Inventory / stock and hardware-tracking module experience

• Experience in deep tech, R&D-focused or high-growth start-up environments

• International finance experience across multiple jurisdictions

• Data and reporting skills (SQL, Power BI, SuiteAnalytics or similar)

What can you expect from us

• A comprehensive benefits package that includes an annual bonus plan, private medical insurance, life insurance, and a contributory pension scheme

• Equity, so that our team can share in the long-term success of Riverlane

• 28 days annual leave, plus bank holidays and enhanced family leave

• A diverse work environment that brings together experts in many fields (including software and hardware development, quantum information theory, physics and maths) and over 20 different nationalities

• A learning environment that encourages individual, team and company growth and development, including a regular programme of learning events and training and conference budgets

About the role
• You'll develop models that are accurate, trusted and predictive. 
• You are not just doing a job, you are growing a business.
About you
• In addition to direct experience, you'll be excited to join a lean start-up working with small fast teams where your ideas get built rather than queued. 
• You will be excited to have broad company involvement, autonomy and impact. You'll be a Big fish in a small pond developing amazing models.
• You'll be a self-starter, clever and innovative

In this role, you will
• Every second, our vehicles and sensors produce a torrent of data. Your job is to turn it into decisions that keep drivers (and other road users) safe, cut insurance losses and save fleets real money. 
You’ll own the full journey from raw signal to shipped product:

Create the risk score the industry relies on. You’ll model accident frequency and severity from real driving behaviour and distil it into a single score that insurers will price on and fleet managers will act on. This is the model that changes behaviour and premiums.

Predict what’s next. Fuel burn, maintenance failures, customer lifetime value and other high-impact use cases are all on the table. You’ll take each one from first prototype to production, with no hand-off to another team and no model left gathering dust in a notebook.

• You are able to combine rigorous statistical and machine learning thinking with a pragmatic focus on models that perform reliably in the real world, and you can explain your work clearly to technical and non-technical audiences alike.
• 4+ years relevant experience
• Fluent English, written and spoken.

• Ideally you will have knowledge and experience of motor insurance and claims analytics.

You’ll lead Rooya’s move into new UK mid-market sectors. You’ll take the sectors and channels where we have early proof and turn them into repeatable business. You’ll sit in the UK Commercial Team with an SDR booking meetings into your accounts, and you’ll work closely with Customer Success, Product, Sales Engineering and Analytics, with direct access to leadership.
You’ll be measured on new ARR from the sectors and partnerships you own, on the quality of the pipeline you build, and on clean records in Pipedrive. You’ll also be judged on the playbook you leave behind for the team to run. You’ll report to and be coached by our Senior Director of Sales and Marketing. As the sectors you open grow, the role can grow into leading a sector or channel team, with a direct say in where Rooya goes next.
About you
You’re a hunter. You get a buzz from winning a new logo, and you’d rather build pipeline than wait for it. Give you a blank sheet and a sector and you’ll find the first ten conversations and the first customer. You care about the outcome too: safer drivers, safer roads and fewer collisions matter to you.
Day to day, you’re curious and organised. You go deep on how a business really runs: its routes, claims, compliance and where the real costs hide. You plan your week around pipeline, keep Pipedrive clean, and write things down so what you learn becomes messaging, a proof point or a play the team can use.
With customers, you sell on value, not features. Fleet operators have been burnt by point solutions, so you earn their trust by understanding their world and keeping your word. You build the business case, model the deal and know when to walk away. With colleagues, you’re a team player who shares what works and celebrates the team’s wins as much as your own. Under pressure, you stay calm and keep going. A lost deal or a quiet month makes you sharper, not slower.
You take feedback well and act on it. You ask for it after calls and deals, look at your own numbers honestly, and keep improving how you prospect, run discovery and close.In this role, you will
• Own two or three target sectors or channels from our focus list, end to end: research, messaging, pipeline and close
• Deliver your quota of new ARR from the sectors and partnerships you own
• Build your own pipeline through account mapping, cold calling and outbound, with an SDR booking meetings into your accounts
• Run complex deals from first conversation with operators and executives through to signature, working with operations, finance and the board on the client side
• Open partnerships with insurers, brokers, resellers and installers that bring in new fleets
• Work with Customer Success, Product, Sales Engineering and Analytics to remove deal blockers, then land and grow the accounts you open
• Test pricing, packaging and commercial models, and bring the results back to the business
• Write the playbook for each sector: ICP, discovery questions, proof points, objection handling and sequences
• Use Pipedrive, Surfe, Apollo and Claude every day for prospecting, enrichment and pipeline management, and keep your records clean and current
Minimum requirements

The role provides strategic tax leadership to support the Group's commercial objectives, growth initiatives, operating model and financing arrangements, while ensuring compliance with global tax regulations and maintaining a robust tax control framework. • Develop capability within the broader finance organisation regarding international tax matters.

Creating the Extraordinary, Together.

Through compelling and irresistible entertainment, we aim to engage, inspire and create meaningful cultural impact.
To achieve this, we bring together talented people from all backgrounds, experiences and perspectives both within our teams and across our productions. We are committed to fostering an inclusive culture and creating opportunities for diverse talent in everything we do.
About the team 
The Digital and Branded team at Fremantle UK are pivotal in steering Fremantle’s evolution as a media business across commercial work and on digital platforms such as YouTube and social media. The team create and deliver brand partnerships with our iconic IP, produce digital marketing content for our shows and work with Fremantle UK’s award-winning labels on all things branded entertainment across linear TV, streamers, YouTube and social media.

Fremantle UK is looking for a Senior Sales Manager, Digital Branded Content to join our Digital & Branded team and help drive the next phase of growth in digital-first branded content.
This is a senior, commercially focused role responsible for generating new business opportunities with brands and agencies, securing briefs and developing partnerships built for YouTube, social and the wider digital content landscape.
You’ll combine proactive business development with a strong understanding of content, creators and platforms – identifying where brands can play authentically in entertainment and translating those opportunities into compelling commercial propositions.
A key part of the role will be unlocking digital-first branded entertainment opportunities outside of our existing IP, positioning Fremantle as a creative, production (working closely with the Head of Digital Production) and distribution partner for brands to build new, ownable IP ecosystems.
You’ll also work closely with the wider Digital & Branded team, including partnering with our other Senior Partnerships Manager to develop and deliver digital growth in commercial partnerships around some of Fremantle’s best-known shows and brands, including Britain’s Got Talent, Grand Designs and more.
This is an opportunity to take real ownership of an important growth area within one of the world’s leading creative businesses.
Here you will get to:
• Drive growth in digital-first branded entertainment, identifying and sourcing new commercial opportunities through proactive outreach to brands, agencies and other potential partners.
• Build and manage a strong new-business pipeline, developing relationships with senior decision-makers and turning conversations into tangible opportunities and briefs.
• Secure briefs for branded entertainment opportunities, establishing Fremantle as a go-to creative partner for brands looking to reach audiences through digital-first entertainment.
• Lead conversations with brands and agencies, confidently representing Fremantle’s creative and commercial capabilities and identifying opportunities where we can add value.
• Develop compelling propositions and pitches, working with creative, production and commercial colleagues to turn opportunities into distinctive, sellable ideas.
• Assess Fremantle’s existing IP catalogue to identify opportunities for digital-first content concepts tailored to brand integration, creator collaboration and platform-specific audiences.
• Build commercial models around opportunities, working at pace to understand budgets, scope partnerships and shape commercially viable propositions.

About the Role:

Grade Level (for internal use):
12The Team: The Data Privacy, Protection and Governance team at S&P Global is dedicated to managing sensitive, personal, and non-personal information. We achieve this through the implementation of comprehensive policies, processes, controls, and metrics that ensure compliance with global regulations.

The Impact: S&P Global is seeking an 
 Director, Information Governance and Records Management to lead, mature, and scale the enterprise-wide information governance and records management program across its global data and analytics business, with supporting responsibility for data governance, privacy by design, and AI governance.

This role owns the strategy, policies, standards, and controls that govern the full lifecycle of S&P Global’s business records and information, from creation and capture through classification, retention, legal hold, and defensible disposition. The Director will ensure that records and information management practices align with S&P Global’s Information Governance Policy framework, Privacy Program, and evolving legal, regulatory, and recordkeeping obligations across jurisdictions.

The position plays a critical leadership role in operationalizing the enterprise records retention schedule, strengthening information classification compliance, and reducing over-retention risk, while supporting a risk-based data management and governance model, privacy by design, and responsible AI practices that underpin S&P Global’s delivery of data-driven products and services, including analytics, ratings, market intelligence, and entity-based data solutions.

S&P Global’s business model—focused on delivering data, analytics, and insight to global markets—requires robust governance over data sourcing, processing, retention, and usage to ensure trust, regulatory compliance, and operational resilience.

What’s in it for you: In this role, you will:
• Collaborate with senior and executive stakeholders globally.
• Act as a senior advisor to stakeholders across Legal, Compliance, Technology, and business divisions.
• Lead cross-functional governance forums to drive alignment and accountability for data governance activities.
• Be an integral part of building and maturing the global Information Governance and Records Management program, working alongside executive leadership to drive our team forward.

Responsibilities: The Associate Director, Information Governance and Records Management will be responsible for:

• Information Governance & Records Management Leadership• Lead the strategy, design, implementation, and continuous improvement of the enterprise Information Governance and Records Management program, covering the full information lifecycle (creation, capture, use, storage, retention, legal hold, and defensible disposition) across paper and electronic records.
• Own and maintain core policies and standards, including:• Information Governance Policy
• Information Classification Standard
• Records Retention Schedule
• Legal Hold and Defensible Disposition procedures

• Ensure alignment with regulatory requirements, internal risk frameworks, and international standards.
• Maintain and periodically refresh the global Records Retention Schedule, conducting legal and regulatory retention research across jurisdictions and securing business sign-off on record classes and retention periods.
• Drive operational adoption of retention requirements across business divisions and enterprise systems, including records inventories, system-level retention configuration, and coordinated defensible disposition of records and data that have met their retention periods.
• Partner with Legal and eDiscovery teams to manage the legal hold process and ensure holds override routine disposition.
• Develop and deliver information governance and records management training, communications, and a network of divisional records coordinators.

• Data Classification & Information Handling• Establish and oversee enterprise-wide data classification frameworks and compliance monitoring.
• Partner with Information Security and technology teams to ensure appropriate controls for data access, storage, and protection.
• Implement and track metrics to measure classification compliance and data handling effectiveness.

• Data Management & Governance• Support the development of a scalable, enterprise data management and governance model that integrates with records and retention requirements, including:• Data inventory and cataloging
• Data ownership and stewardship
• Data flow visibility and control

• Collaborate with business, technology, and risk teams to ensure governance controls are embedded across products, platforms, and operations.

• Risk Management & Regulatory Readiness• Identify, assess, and mitigate risks relating to data governance, retention, classification, and regulatory compliance.
• Support internal audits, regulatory inquiries, and external assessments.
• Maintain audit-ready documentation and evidence of compliance.

• Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance and Oversight• Act as Information Governance and Data Compliance support for the development, implementation, and continuous enhancement of S&P Global’s AI governance framework, ensuring the responsible, ethical, and compliant use of artificial intelligence and automated decision-making technologies across the enterprise, including appropriate classification, retention, and disposition of AI training data, inputs, and outputs.
• Where necessary, establish and oversee policies, standards, controls, and risk assessment processes governing the lifecycle of AI systems, including model development, procurement, deployment, monitoring, and retirement.
• Partner with Legal, Compliance, Information Security, Technology, Risk, and business stakeholders to ensure AI initiatives align with regulatory requirements, corporate policies, data governance standards, and responsible AI principles, while promoting transparency, accountability, and effective risk management.

The Team
We are a high-accountability, globally connected Sales Compensation team that values disciplined execution, a strong sense of urgency, and end-to-end ownership. We expect our people to understand the full lifecycle of their work, anticipate downstream impacts, and communicate outcomes with exceptional clarity, whether supporting our broad population of 1,500+ plan participants or partnering with C-level executives. We value precision, responsiveness, sound judgment, collaboration, and people who take ownership through to resolution.

Responsibilities and Impact
This role sits at the intersection of Finance, Sales Operations, and Technology — and it's central to how S&P Global ensures every sales commission is calculated on a clean, trusted, and fully governed data foundation. As the primary data architect and strategic partner for Sales leadership, you will shape the infrastructure that powers commercial decisions across the division.
• Architect and govern a centralised, SOX-compliant data platform — owning schema design, tool selection, database build-out, and ongoing maintenance — that serves as the single source of truth for all commission calculations and sales performance reporting.

• Lead and develop a team of data and compensation analysts: set goals, allocate resources, and build a culture of technical excellence and continuous improvement.
• Translate complex commercial contracts — including joint/split deals and strategic accounts — into structured, reusable data frameworks that integrate cleanly into operational and reporting workflows.
• Partner with Business Intelligence and Systems Analytics to shape Data Warehouse architecture and ETL workflows, ensuring downstream analytics always run on validated, trusted inputs.
• Communicate and present real-time sales performance analytics and data-quality metrics to senior leadership, while translating complex data architecture into plain English for sales reps and leaders — resolving data-related questions and driving adoption of correct processes across the organisation.

Responsibilities and Impact
If you are at your best when problems are complex, the data is messy, and the stakes are real, this role was built for you. As the operational owner of global SPIFF programs and end-to-end payee lifecycle management at S&P Global Market Intelligence, you will work at the intersection of Commercial Strategy, People Operations, and Sales Finance — ensuring that every compensation event, from a seller's first day to their last commission payment, is calculated precisely, governed rigorously, and resolved with integrity. • Own end-to-end SPIFF operations — translate commercial campaign briefs into precise qualification criteria, crediting logic, and system rate tables; build automated tracking engines using SQL, Python, or Alteryx to monitor real-time attainment and prevent duplicate claims, eligibility mismatches, and off-policy spend; execute all calculations; deliver post-campaign ROI analytics and spend assessments in Power BI; and archive all eligibility criteria, budget sign-offs, and documentation for full audit-readiness.
• Architect and execute active payee lifecycle workflows — manage system setup, prorated quota assignments, draw and guarantee schedules, and ramping accelerators for new hires; model and execute effective-dated target adjustments and split crediting rules for mid-year promotions and role changes; and calculate accurate quota relief, crediting freezes, and temporary account coverage allocations for leaves of absence, in line with regional labour policies and commercial guidelines.
• Own departure and offboarding precision — compute final commission settlements, accelerated vesting, trailing pipeline revenue, and exit reconciliation packages for terminations; manage post-departure claw back reconciliations; and build automated script-based routines linking HRIS platforms, including Workday, with enterprise compensation engines to detect personnel changes, effective-date discrepancies, and reporting line anomalies ahead of payroll processing.

If you thrive in fast-paced, high-growth environments, are motivated by measurable business impact, and enjoy turning ideas into reality, this is your opportunity to make a difference.

In this role you will:

• Own and grow our relationships with insurance carriers, brokers and MGAs in the UK

• You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact - helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

## About the role

We are looking for an experienced, highly creative, and hands-on Art Lead / Art Director to join Secret Level Studios and help define the visual direction of our upcoming titles.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who can combine strong artistic vision with practical game development experience. You will work closely with our Creative Director, designers, and wider development team to establish the look and feel of our games, create production-quality assets that set the visual direction and quality standards for the project, and guide both internal artists and external partners.

We are looking for someone with a strong background in stylised 3D art, particularly character art, who is comfortable taking assets all the way from concept through to implementation in Unity. Professional experience working with Unity is essential, along with strong skills in character modelling, animation, and rigging. Experience creating environments, props, painting, drawing, or concept art would all be highly valuable.

This is an opportunity to help shape the artistic future of a growing independent studio, influencing not only the visual identity of our games but also the art pipelines, quality standards, and creative culture that will support them for years to come.

We're looking for someone who enjoys leading by example; someone who is just as excited about creating outstanding artwork as they are about mentoring others and shaping the studio's artistic vision.

## Responsibilities

### Artistic direction

- Define and maintain the visual identity of our games across all artistic disciplines.
- Establish the artistic direction, visual standards, and style guides that enable both internal teams and external partners to deliver consistent, high-quality work.
- Ensure a consistent visual identity across characters, environments, UI, VFX, and all other artistic disciplines.
- Collaborate closely with studio leadership to define an artistic vision that complements our game design and technical direction.

### Character art and animation

- Design and create 3D stylized characters from concept through to final game implementation.
- Model, texture, rig, skin and animate hero characters and key assets.
- Create, refine, and expand our library of characters and supporting assets.
- Establish efficient workflows and pipelines for integrating assets into Unity.

### Environment and world building

- Create and direct the development of stylised 3D environments, from large outdoor spaces to detailed interior locations, making use of procedural techniques where appropriate.
- Work closely with the Game Director to shape the visual identity of key locations and environments throughout the game.
- Ensure environments are visually compelling while also supporting gameplay, navigation, and technical requirements.
- Guide asset creation from the wider team, ensuring quality across the board.

### Leadership and collaboration

- Provide constructive feedback and mentorship to artists across the team.
- Provide guidance both internally and externally, working closely with publishing partners.
- Collaborate regularly with the Game Director, designers, programmers, and producers to ensure our games are visually compelling, technically achievable, and fun to play.
- Identify artistic and production risks early, and work with the team to develop effective mitigation strategies.
- Support recruitment and onboarding of new artists as the studio grows.

### Unity integration

- Import, configure, and maintain assets for Unity Engine.
- Work with shaders, materials, lighting, animation systems, and scene composition.
- Ensure assets perform well while maintaining visual quality.
- Collaborate with technical teams to improve workflows and art pipelines.

## Requirements

### Essential skills & experience

- Proven professional experience in game art development and shipped titles.
- Strong portfolio demonstrating high-quality stylised 3D character art and game-ready assets.
- Professional experience creating characters, rigs, and animations.
- Experience defining and maintaining an art style across a project or team.
- Strong understanding of composition, colour theory, shape language, and visual storytelling.
- Experience working within Unity.
- Excellent communication and leadership abilities.
- Ability to provide clear, constructive artistic direction and feedback.
- Passion for creating games and memorable player experiences.

### Highly desirable

- Previous experience as an Art Lead, Art Director, Lead Artist, or Senior Artist.
- Familiarity with shaders, VFX, and technical art workflows.
- Experience creating stylised fantasy, life-simulation, RPG, or cosy-game artwork.
- Strong understanding of production constraints and asset optimisation.
- Experience building art pipelines and production workflows.
- Ability to create concept art, sketches, or illustrations that help establish a strong visual identity.

## Important to us at SLS

- Everything we create meets a consistently high standard of artistic quality.
- Artists receive clear direction, constructive feedback, and the support they need to grow and do their best work.
- Art pipelines and workflows enable the team to work efficiently without compromising quality.
- Visual quality supports gameplay, technical requirements, and project schedules.
- New ideas and creative improvements are encouraged while maintaining a cohesive artistic vision.
- Players can immediately recognise and connect with the unique visual identity of our games.

The Senior Protective Intelligence Analyst is a role within the Risk Intelligence Center (RIC). The role is responsible for operating and supporting the delivery of intelligence products and services to Securitas and Securitas’ customers. The role is suited to someone with 3-5 years’ experience in intelligence and / or investigations. Direct experience in an operational role is essential. The ideal candidate would have previous experience in private sector intelligence, however this is not essential for a candidate that can evidence robust understanding of customer requirements.
The primary focus of the Senior Protective Intelligence Analyst is to lead the collection, processing and analysis of data and information to inform the production of intelligence products and services, and disseminate these to customers internally and commercially. The role will take the lead on complex and challenging customer Requests For Intelligence (RFIs).
The role reports directly into the Protective Intelligence Manager, and requires strong intelligence acumen, understanding of customer requirements, relationship building and networking skills, strong research, analytical and report writing skills, in addition to proficiency in IT systems including Microsoft Office and specific intelligence tools.
Working within a dynamic and demanding environment, the role requires flexibility and agility, including mobilising on short notice to meet operational requirements, and some evening and weekend work. The Senior Protective Intelligence Analyst will have an in-depth knowledge of the Protective and Global intelligence functions, providing support and guidance to both services and products. The role is Monday – Friday with a weekend rota. Travel may be required to visit customers on occasion. Responsibilities will evolve over time, with opportunities for ongoing development and progression.
Responsibilities
• Support the management and the Direction of intelligence efforts (reactively and proactively), including proactively identifying, prioritising, and tasking intelligence requirements within the RIC, for both general reporting requirements and client specific requirements.
• Support the management of the Collection of data and information, including use of intelligence tools, and manual processes including research.
• Support the management of the Processing of intelligence into databases, forms, logs, systems, templates etc.
• Support the management of the Analysis of data and information using recognised intelligence techniques and supporting seniors with more complex and / or demanding efforts.
• Support the management of the Production of finished intelligence products autonomously, or with support / supporting seniors, including (but not limited to) alerts, analysis (assessments, reports etc.) and investigations. This includes both written products and verbal presentations.
• Support the management of the Dissemination of intelligence products to stakeholders, including internally within Securitas, and commercially to customers, both in the UK and overseas.
• Support the management and the drive of operational excellence through ongoing Evaluation and Feedback of intelligence services, including maintaining the highest level of consistency and quality. Additionally, managing ongoing service development by maintaining awareness of innovation within intelligence to ensure implementation of latest techniques and tactics, best practice, and information relevant to the RIC.
• Support the identification and development of new sources and methods of research to ensure that intelligence products reflect latest methodologies and best practice.
• Maintaining awareness of innovation within intelligence to develop and implement the latest techniques and tactics, best practice, and information relevant to the RIC and own self development.
• Support management and seniors and provide guidance to junior colleagues in order to maximise their development, efficiency, and morale.
• Provide leadership to the RIC, providing mentoring/coaching, guidance, and support to staff in order to maximise their development, efficiency, and morale, and deliver an effective intelligence service.
• Work collaboratively with the wider Securitas organisation, including client facing staff and global colleagues.
• Work closely in partnership with other internal stakeholders and be willing to challenge the status-quo.
• Liaise and collaborate with colleagues, stakeholders, and agencies (both internally and externally) in the UK and internationally to build an intelligence network.
• Take the lead on complex and challenging customer RFI’s, prioritising the workload as necessary.
• Be able to support the Protective and Global intelligence functions.
• Support senior management with the implementation of new products, ways of working and organisational change.
• Be a role model for all other analysts in the RIC.

About SeeViews

SeeViews is a progressive young company that is pioneering how brands advertise on YouTube.

YouTube is one of the world’s most effective advertising platforms. It provides brands with a huge variety of video content.

TV has always been the gold standard of brand advertising, but as people’s viewing habits change brands are looking for platforms beyond TV to engage their target audience while they are immersed in premium content.

SeeViews has developed technology which connects advertisers with professionally produced, high value YouTube content that has the look, feel and effectiveness of TV. No user generated content, just channels and shows that audiences know, love and trust.

We are a fast moving, fast growing business that has already established a credible position in the industry. We have been appointed by Barb (the industry’s most trusted and respected audience measurement organisation) to assist in developing their YouTube measurement programme. We have been identified by FEBE as one of the top businesses to watch in 2025. We work with some of the world’s largest brands, broadcasters, production houses and media agencies.

We are committed to becoming a guiding light for the advertising industry as the streaming world becomes more complex and intricate.

Our Culture

​

Being part of a start-up takes a special kind of superstar. We are team that is focussed on building a business that will disrupt a tightly controlled industry to ensure advertising can keep pace with the lightening rate of user behaviour change. Here are some of the principles we live by.

We need builders not robots. Our people are curious, agile, creative self-starters. We are doing things that have never been done before, our people work without blueprints, taking responsibility to find the best way forward. We are not afraid to rip it up and start again if the old way is no longer relevant. We are always asking if there could be a better way.

PACE PACE PACE. We are growing fast, we are developing fast and we are working fast. Our customers are independent, forward thinkers who want to be at the cutting edge of what is possible in advertising. We love being able to keep pace with change and responding to the ever evolving habits of consumers.

At SeeViews the best idea wins and we know they rarely come from the board room. Everyone at Seviews has an equal voice. Everyone has psychological safety, anyone can comfortably say when something isn’t working or when something should be changed and everyone is encouraged to bat around any idea…you never know when those small ideas could end up changing everything.

Capability and attitude trumps experience. The right person is more important than the perfect CV.

​

​

As we grow, our clients' experience of SeeViews has to be as brilliant as our product. We are looking for an Account Manager whose mission is simple: to ensure every interaction with SeeViews is a brilliant experience. You will be the trusted day-to-day partner to our clients — making sure campaigns are set up flawlessly, delivered to the highest standard, reported beautifully, and that clients come back to us again and again.

The role has two horizons. In the short term, it is about faultless campaign delivery, reporting and post-campaign analysis. In the longer term, it is about building relationships that drive repeat business and grow our accounts. You will work hand-in-hand with our traders and sales team, and act as the voice of the client inside SeeViews.

• 
Understand each client's ad operations requirements — tagging, tracking, assets and set-up — and work with the trader and sales team to answer client queries and requests quickly and clearly.

• 
Understand the campaign objectives, KPIs, targeting strategy (audience, geography, data, time of day, day of week) and channel strategy, and work with the trader to ensure every campaign is set up correctly.

• 
Ensure campaigns are delivered in a way that maximises the SeeViews value — the best channels, the most relevant moments, the right audience, full delivery and optimised performance.

• 
Work with the trader to identify campaign improvements and feed back client insight, so every delivered campaign exceeds expectations on both performance and environment.

• 
Deliver reports on time and complete — with all relevant data, clear commentary and next steps. These should be the most reassuring, insightful and beautifully presented reports a client receives.

• 
Actively seek feedback and implement improvements, embedding new insights from new data sets into reporting as they become available.

Post-campaign analysis (PCAs)

• 
Deliver a beautiful, timely post-campaign analysis that highlights the campaign's successes, the close management behind it, and the additional insight SeeViews brings through its unique data sets and view of the market.

Client relationships

• 
Manage and grow client relationships to drive repeat business, becoming the trusted partner clients want to work with again and again.

Account management or client services experience, ideally in advertising, media or adtech — agency or media owner side.

A genuine understanding of digital campaign delivery: ad operations, tagging and tracking, targeting and reporting (or the appetite and aptitude to learn it fast).

Exceptional attention to detail — nothing slips through the cracks on your watch.

A natural relationship-builder with excellent communication skills, comfortable being the trusted face of SeeViews to clients.

Strong organisational skills and the ability to juggle multiple campaigns and deadlines at startup pace.

• 
A flair for turning data into clear, engaging, beautifully presented reports and stories.

• 
Commercially minded, with an instinct for spotting opportunities to grow an account.

• 
A curious, proactive self-starter who takes ownership and always looks for a better way — remember, the right person is more important than the perfect CV.

Job Description:
Cloud Security Engineer

POSITION SUMMARY
The Cloud Security Engineer protects Gladstone's cloud platforms and services through secure design, configuration, monitoring, automation and evidence-led remediation. The role works across Azure, Kubernetes, networks, identity, workloads, data and delivery pipelines, and supports the safe adoption of AI-enabled systems and operational tooling.

AI-ENABLED WORKING
AI-enabled working is a core expectation of this role. The role holder will use approved AI tools and automation to improve quality, speed, insight and consistency; validate outputs before acting on them; protect customer, employee and company data; and share effective practices with colleagues. Performance will be assessed through outcomes such as quality, reliability, cycle time, risk control and knowledge transfer - not simply the volume of AI-generated output or frequency of tool use.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Cloud Security Engineering
• Implement and maintain security controls across Azure subscriptions, identities, networks, Kubernetes, containers, servers, data services, endpoints and CI/CD pipelines.
• Review cloud and platform designs, configuration and change proposals, identifying practical improvements before risk reaches production.
• Automate secure configuration, vulnerability detection, policy checks, evidence collection and repeatable remediation where appropriate.
• Support secrets, key, certificate, privileged-access and service-account lifecycle management.
Detection, Response and Vulnerability Management
• Monitor security signals and investigate suspicious activity, vulnerabilities, misconfiguration and control failures.
• Prioritise remediation using exploitability, exposure, business impact and compensating controls rather than severity labels alone.
• Support security incident response, evidence preservation, root-cause analysis and completion of corrective actions.
• Maintain clear security findings, owners, due dates, exceptions and risk acceptance records.
AI and Application Security
• Threat model AI-enabled services and operational agents, including data leakage, prompt injection, over-permission, unsafe actions, supplier risk and inadequate human oversight.
• Use approved AI tools to support security analysis, query development, evidence review and incident investigation while validating outputs and protecting sensitive data.
• Work with R&D and Data teams to embed secure-by-design controls into the AI-DLC, data flows, APIs and deployment patterns.
• Define and test guardrails for AI access to production systems, credentials, logs and customer information.
Compliance and Security Culture
• Provide technical evidence and remediation support for ISO 27001, PCI DSS, Cyber Essentials Plus, GDPR and customer assurance activity.
• Create practical standards, runbooks and guidance and coach engineers on secure cloud and AI-enabled working.
• Report material risks and trends clearly to the Cloud Operations Manager, Compliance Manager and relevant owners.

EXPERIENCE, KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS
Essential
• Hands-on experience securing Azure or another major cloud platform in a production environment.
• Practical knowledge of identity and access management, networking, Kubernetes or containers, operating systems, vulnerability management, logging and incident response.
• Ability to investigate and prioritise technical security findings and implement or coordinate effective remediation.
• Experience with scripting, policy-as-code, infrastructure automation or security automation.
• Understanding of secure development and deployment practices, including secrets and pipeline security.
• Clear documentation and communication of technical risk to different audiences.
Desirable
• Azure security, Kubernetes security or recognised cyber-security certification.
• Experience of ISO 27001, PCI DSS, Cyber Essentials Plus or regulated SaaS environments.
• Experience threat modelling AI-enabled systems, APIs or agentic automation.

PERSONAL ATTRIBUTES
• High ownership, sound judgment and a bias toward solving problems rather than moving them between teams.
• Curious and adaptable, with a practical commitment to continuous learning and responsible AI adoption.
• Systematic, evidence-led problem solving and attention to detail.
• Clear communication with both technical and non-technical colleagues.
• Collaborative working style and willingness to share knowledge, review work and support others.

Gladstone is seeking a Director of Growth to lead the development of a world-class go-to-market capability that supports the company’s next phase of growth across our brands.
Working closely with the Executive Leadership Team, the Director of Growth will connect Product, Technology, Commercial and Customer Success through a common go-to-market operating model. The role will focus on improving customer acquisition, product adoption, retention, expansion and long-term customer value.
This is a strategic and hands-on leadership role, combining commercial thinking, customer insight, data, AI and technology to improve business performance and strengthen Gladstone’s market position.
Mission
To transform customer insight, product innovation and commercial intelligence into predictable, measurable and sustainable business growth across the brands.

Go-to-Market Strategy
The Director of Growth will develop and continually evolve Gladstone’s go-to-market strategy, ensuring the business has clear target markets, customer segments and ideal customer profiles.
The role will create repeatable frameworks for launching new products and services, align Product, Marketing, Sales and Customer Success around shared commercial goals, and identify new routes to market and growth opportunities.
Product Positioning and Commercialisation across our brands
The role will lead the development of clear and compelling product positioning, value propositions and messaging frameworks across Gladstone’s products and services.
The Director of Growth will support product launch planning, market and competitor analysis, pricing and packaging decisions, and commercial proposition development. A key focus will be improving product adoption through stronger market communication and customer understanding.

The Director of Growth will build scalable demand generation programmes that increase Gladstone’s marketing contribution to pipeline and revenue.
This will include improving digital acquisition strategies, strengthening marketing performance across channels, improving customer onboarding and activation, and increasing customer engagement, retention, advocacy and lifetime value.
