The Director of Growth will standardise commercial performance measurement, improve forecasting and attribution, and use AI and automation to improve decision-making, productivity and operational efficiency.
Customer and Market Insight
The Director of Growth will develop a structured customer insight programme, building effective feedback loops between customers, Product and Commercial teams.
The role will analyse market trends, competitor activity and customer data to identify opportunities and support strategic decision-making with evidence-based recommendations.
Leadership and Capability Development
The Director of Growth will build and lead a high-performing Growth function, developing best practice across product marketing, demand generation, customer insight and revenue operations.
They will champion AI, automation and modern go-to-market practices, while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.
Key Performance Indicators
Success in the role will be measured across commercial, operational and strategic outcomes, including:
• Sustainable Annual Recurring Revenue growth
• Increased contribution to pipeline and revenue
• Improved customer acquisition efficiency
• Increased customer retention and expansion revenue
• Growth in customer lifetime value
• Improved return on commercial investment
• Adoption of a consistent go-to-market operating model
• Improved commercial reporting and forecasting accuracy
• Enhanced CRM data quality, governance and automation
• Stronger alignment across Product, Marketing, Sales and Customer Success
• Increased productivity through AI and automation
• Stronger product launch performance
• Improved market positioning and brand consideration
• Faster execution of commercial initiatives
• Greater use of customer insight in strategic decision-making
Experience and Skills
The successful candidate will bring significant leadership experience in Growth, Go-to-Market, Commercial or Marketing leadership within a SaaS or technology business.
They will have a proven track record of scaling recurring revenue businesses and building high-performing demand generation, product marketing and commercial growth functions.
The role requires a strong understanding of subscription and recurring revenue models, customer acquisition and retention, CRM and marketing automation platforms, commercial analytics, Revenue Operations and AI-enabled commercial processes.
Experience partnering with executive leadership teams to shape strategy and deliver measurable business growth will be essential.
Leadership Capabilities
The successful candidate will be commercially driven, strategic and highly operational. They will be confident using data to support decision-making and comfortable leading change across multiple business functions.
They will be an excellent communicator and influencer, able to bring teams together around shared commercial objectives and build trust across Product, Technology, Commercial and Customer Success.
They will also have the ability to build high-performing teams and develop the capability Gladstone needs to scale effectively.

Discovery: decide what’s worth building

• Build the business case for significant investments and present it to senior stakeholders.
• Weigh one customer’s request against what the wider customer base needs, and favour scalable, reusable solutions.

Delivery: get the right thing built well
• Own and prioritise the roadmap and backlog for your product area, balancing customer value, commercial priorities and technical considerations.
• Turn problems into clear, outcome-focused requirements and user stories, and refine them with the squad.
• Work daily with engineering, QA and design: join planning, refinement and reviews, and make scope decisions quickly.
• Champion user experience and self-service, so solutions are simple for operators and their members.
• Spot and manage risks, dependencies and compliance needs, and communicate them early.
• Coordinate with third-party and partner development teams, influencing without direct authority.

Go to market: make sure it lands
• Plan launches with Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, Support and Professional Services, so every team is ready on day one.
• Shape positioning and messaging, and equip Sales with clear value propositions and demos.
• Make sure release notes, Knowledge Base articles and training materials are accurate and ready.

Across all three
• Provide clear updates on progress, priorities and outcomes to the executive team and wider business.
• Use AI responsibly in your own work, and consider where it can improve every feature you own.

Line management
• Line manage one experienced Product Manager, coaching and mentoring them on Gladstone’s products, customers and ways of working.
• Work alongside them as a peer on delivery.
• Align goals, priorities and delivery updates with the CPO and other product leads.

What you’ll need to succeed
• Experience as a Product Manager, Product Owner or in a similar role in B2B software or SaaS.
• A track record of taking products or features from idea to launch, including discovery work, not only delivery.
• Hands-on experience working with agile development teams and owning a backlog.
• Confidence talking to customers and turning what you hear into clear problems and priorities.
• A commercial mindset: you can build a business case and make trade-offs on value, cost and effort.
• Strong written and verbal communication, adjusted for technical and non-technical audiences.
• Experience coaching, mentoring or line managing others.

Why join Gladstone
You’ll join a collaborative Product team shaping leisure management technology used by councils, universities, trusts and leisure operators across the UK, and deliver products that make a real difference to our customers.
As part of the Vesta Software and Constellation Software group, we combine the agility of a specialist software business with the backing of one of the world’s largest software groups.

Seisa holds a firm’s most confidential material: deal memos, data rooms, partner email. What we tell a firm’s security team has to be true and backed by evidence, and this is the role that makes it so. It is the seat we most need to fill.

Cloud Run, Cloud Tasks and Pub/Sub, Vertex AI, Secret Manager and KMS, Cloud Storage and Cloud Build, brought under Terraform.

Neo4j, Postgres on Supabase and Langfuse: backups, restore drills, and isolation between firms.

• Environments
Staging and production fully separate, and promotion from one to the other uneventful.

• Identity and access
Least-privilege IAM, SSO and MFA everywhere, access reviews, secret rotation and offboarding.

• Connectors
Microsoft 365 and the other sources we read handling tokens, scopes and permissions safely.

• Compliance
The controls behind our SOC 2 and ISO 27001 work in Vanta, with the auditor and pen-test firm you choose and manage.

• Security answers
The security pack, the questionnaires firms send, and the calls where their CTO wants to talk to someone technical.

• Observability and incidents
Monitoring and incident response that fit a small team.

• 
You have run production infrastructure on a major cloud, GCP ideally, Azure or AWS welcome, and written the infrastructure as code for it.
• 
You have been the person who got a SOC 2 or ISO 27001 audit through at a startup or scale-up, and can name the controls you owned and the evidence you produced.

You are comfortable in Python and a CI pipeline, and will read and change application code, not only configuration.

You would rather answer “Partial” with a plan than tick “Yes” on something that is not true.

Probably five to twelve years in, though we care about what you have owned more than the number.

Own the evaluation framework that measures agent task completion, failure recovery, output quality, and human override rates, and use it to catch regressions before they reach other teams.

Partner with engineering on the non-functional requirements that make shared services trustworthy at scale: reliability, performance, security, observability, and graceful behaviour under load. Understand what breaks when a service others depend on runs unattended.

This is a quota-carrying sales leadership role and a first-line people leadership role in equal measure. Overview
We are seeking an experienced and driven Full Stack Developer to join our software development team. In this role, you will design, develop, and maintain high-quality web applications using React.js on the frontend and ASP.NET Core (C#) on the backend. • Design, develop, and maintain web applications using React.js and ASP.NET Core (C#).

• Build, integrate, and optimize RESTful APIs to ensure reliable and efficient data communication.

• Develop and maintain SQL Server database objects, including tables, queries, functions, and stored procedures.

• Implement secure authentication and authorization frameworks (e.g., OAuth, JWT).

• Collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams including Client Operations, Management, and DevOps.

• Ensure high code quality through peer reviews, automated testing, and adherence to best practices.

• Monitor, troubleshoot, and optimize application performance, reliability, and scalability.

• Document technical designs, solutions, and processes for internal knowledge sharing.

• Contribute to architectural discussions and provide guidance or mentorship to junior developers as needed.

Requirements
• Proven experience as a Full Stack or Senior Developer using React.js and ASP.NET Core (C#).

• Strong understanding of API design, integration patterns, and lifecycle management.

• Solid hands-on experience with SQL Server, including performance-optimized queries and stored procedures.

• Proficiency in JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, CSS3, and modern React concepts (Hooks, Context API, Redux).

• Experience with Entity Framework Core and LINQ.

• Good understanding of fundamental software engineering principles and version control practices (Git).

• Strong analytical, debugging, and problem-solving skills with excellent communication and collaboration abilities.

Desirable Skills
• Experience with automated testing frameworks (frontend or backend).

• Understanding of Agile/Scrum development methodologies.

• Previous engineering exposure in a medical, industrial, or regulated SCADA environment.

Additional Desirables
Candidates with experience in the following technologies will be given priority due to ongoing parallel IoT/embedded software projects:
• Familiarity with major Cloud IoT platforms (AWS IoT, Azure IoT, Google Cloud IoT).

• Experience with industrial communication protocols (e.g., Modbus) and cloud messaging technologies such as MQTT (QoS 1/2).

• Exposure to multi-language environments, ideally involving embedded C, Python, and Docker for containerized deployments.

• Understanding of diverse storage systems, including both SQL and NoSQL technologies.

What We Offer
• Supportive team and collaborative culture
• Career development and training opportunities
• Competitive salary and benefits
• Hybrid working options (where applicable)
SHJ is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We strive to create an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive, regardless of their background.

**About Singular Photonics**

Singular Photonics develops next generation image sensors based on single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) technology. While most image sensors only measure the intensity of light, SPADs can precisely detect and time individual photons, capturing a wealth of information that conventional cameras simply cannot see. Originating from research at the University of Edinburgh, Singular’s sensors combine highly sensitive photon detection with on-chip processing to enable real-time decision-making at the point of capture, with applications across machine vision, scientific instrumentation, medical imaging and beyond.

**About the Role:**

We are seeking an FPGA Firmware Engineer to join our multidisciplinary R&D team. This is an FPGA role: you will design, implement and verify the Verilog firmware that powers our SPAD sensors, captures photon timing data at high rates and streams it to the host.

Our sensors generate data faster than most imaging systems ever see, so the interesting problems here are real ones: clock domain crossing, timing closure and getting data off the device without losing a photon. You will work alongside our hardware, ASIC and software engineers, from architecture through to system bring-up and customer deployment.

**Key Responsibilities:**

- **Synthesis & Timing:** Own synthesis, constraints, clock domain crossing and timing closure on AMD-Xilinx FPGA family devices in Vivado.
- **High-Speed Interfaces:** Build and integrate the high-speed interfaces that move sensor data: PCIe, USB3, Ethernet, AXI interface, MIPI, LVDS, SLVS, Camera Link.
- **Bring-Up & Debug:** Lead firmware bring-up on new boards and sensors, debugging with oscilloscopes, logic analysers and in-system probes.
- **Source Control & Build:** Keep RTL under version control with a repeatable, automated build, and document designs to the standard our ISO 9001 design control process requires.
- **Reviews & Support:** Contribute to design reviews, and support the software team and customers during field integration.

**Essential:**

- Strong proficiency in Verilog, and a solid grounding in RTL design, synthesis and timing closure.
- Hands-on experience with AMD-Xilinx Vivado and its toolchain.
- Experience writing your own testbenches and verifying a design in simulation before hardware.
- Experience bringing up firmware on real hardware and debugging it in the lab.
- Experience with at least one high-speed interface or bus at RTL level.
- Comfortable in a small company where priorities shift and everyone pitches in.

**Desirable:**

- C, C++ or Python for embedded software integration and test automation.
- Experience with image sensors, time-of-flight, TDCs or single-photon detection.
- Familiarity with PCB design tools such as Altium Designer, and reading schematics during debug.

**Educational Background:**

- Degree in Electronics Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
- 2-5 years’ experience in FPGA and digital design.

**Key Attributes & Behaviours:**

- **Rigour:** Disciplined about verification – you would rather find it in simulation than on the bench.
- **Debugging:** Systematic when the fault could be in the RTL, the board or the sensor, and comfortable with the instruments that tell you which.
- **Clarity:** Writes documentation and code that colleagues can pick up without you in the room.

- **Ownership:** Takes a problem from architecture through to a working system, and sees it through.
- **Adaptability:** Comfortable in a fast-paced, evolving environment where the requirement can move.

**Success Indicators:**

- Design documentation, simulation coverage and design review contributions good enough for another engineer to maintain the work.

Group Accountant

Reporting directly to the Financial Controller, the key responsibilities of the Group Accountant will be the consolidation of key financial reports, including management accounts, budgets and forecasts. The successful candidate will co-ordinate the year end process including our annual external audit as well as managing the business enabling fixed assets and Member Contribution revenue.

Job Location

Cheshire, UK (Head Office)

Area / Department

Business Support

Contract Type

Permanent

Salary

�38,000 - 48,000 Depending on experience plus excellent benefit

Closing Date

16/11/2026

Ref No

The Role

Reporting to the Financial Controller for Construction and Group, the Group Accountant will be responsible for the consolidation of all key financial reports, such as the monthly management accounts and budgets and forecasts. They will be responsible for ensuring that the consolidated monthly management pack has appropriate and sufficient analytical commentary on variances to budget and that accounting treatment is in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) and internal accounting policies. The Group Accountant will also be responsible for the financial management of the Observatory (OBS) ledger which contains the business enabling fixed assets, all Member Contribution revenue and accounts receivable as well as our investment accounts.

The post-holder will be the main co-ordinator of the year end process, ensuring that accurate consolidated financial information and reconciliations are prepared and they will co-ordinate external audit requests for information. 

The Group Accountant will be responsible for the documentation of accounting processes and provide input to accounting and finance policies for the SKAO. They will also help to re-design any weak processes to ensure that the IGO operates in line with best practice and/or regulatory or legal frameworks, and that processes are followed consistently across the global finance teams. The Group Accountant will create and improve training and guidance on finance processes to the wider business.

The role would suit a candidate with experience of working in a small-medium group finance function, who has a willingness and enthusiasm to continuously improve finance processes, is keen to understand and tackle technical accounting questions, and is able to organise decentralised finance teams to report consistently and on time. 

SKAO is committed to fostering an inclusive and flexible working environment that values diversity and collaboration. We welcome applications from under-represented groups, including women and individuals with disabilities, and encourage open dialogue during the recruitment process about any specific requirements.

There may be occasions where this role requires work across different time zones, and in line with SKAO policy, flexible working hours will be supported in agreement with the line manager.

Key Responsibilities, Accountabilities and Duties

The post holder will:

• Be responsible for the preparation and reporting of monthly group management accounts, enhance the monthly reporting to SKAO senior management and prepare related governance papers with supporting commentary for SKAO’s governance bodies

• Manage the non-telescope fixed asset register and perform all related month end routines (capitalisation, depreciation, disposal)

• Responsible for the end-to-end process of revenue recognition of SKAO Member contributions, including maintaining the schedules of indexation of Member contributions, updating and distributing Member Contribution Statements, managing the accounts’ receivable function and performing all related month end postings

• Prepare the group consolidated financial statements, and assist the Financial Controller to ensure that presentation and disclosure is in line with IFRS and SKAO accounting policies

• Co-ordinate and be the main point of contact for the annual external audit and any internal audits of the finance processes in the UK, Australia or South Africa, including scheduling the audit and directing requests for information to the relevant team members, and assist the Financial Controller with preparing audit file notes

• Consolidate the group budgets and forecasts and prepare variance analysis of budget submissions compared to budget baseline figures

• Document finance processes, along with key risks and controls, creating Internal Control Statements (ICS); Perform annual walkthrough tests of finance processes and update ICS as required

• Work alongside the ERP System Manager and Finance Manager to continuously improve the ERP system finance processes and controls

• Support the Financial Controller and Head of Finance by monitoring changes in IFRS accounting standards and planning for any necessary accounting changes

• Prepare the tax and customs claims for non-host Member countries and manage these claims through to conclusion;

• Train finance and non-finance staff as required

• Travel as required, noting that travel is expected to be infrequent (1-2 times per year); and

• Undertake any other reasonable duties, such as assisting with other business systems, as directed by the post holder’s line manager

Mandatory Knowledge, Skills and Experience

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required:

• CCAB accounting qualified or near-qualified (ACCA / ACA / CIPFA preferred) with at least 1 years’ experience in a similar group finance or management accounting role

• Experience of group consolidation of multi-currency core financial reports, such as, monthly management accounts, financial statements and budgets and forecasts

• Experience of participation in external audits and preparation/review of financial statements reported under IFRS;

• Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word and Powerpoint

• Excellent written English 

• Ability to self-manage projects through to completion;

• Problem solver with ability to manage conflicting priorities and work to deadlines

• A self-motivated team player who is flexible and adaptable to change

• Strong attention to detail, both in preparing own work and reviewing work of others to ensure a high standard of accuracy

Desirable Knowledge, Skills and Experience

• Experience of working in a small-medium international group finance function

• Proficient in Unit4 ERP / Unit 4 Business World / Agresso

• Experience within a multi-currency ERP system environment

• Creation or development of finance reports within an ERP system

• Experience of accounting for an IGO

• Experience of working within a large-scale infrastructure project

• Experience co-ordinating remote teams

SRT Marine Systems plc (SRT) is a market leader in the domain of international marine surveillance technology and systems. We are a respected, established, and an ambitious multi-national company headquartered in the UK with a global customer base.

The company has a worldwide impact in the marine sector by leading the next generation of maritime domain awareness technologies “MDA”, products, and systems that significantly enhance security, safety, environmental protection, and sustainability. Our customers are global and range from the largest national coast guards to individual vessel owners.

We are now entering a new and strategically significant phase of growth, characterised by the expansion of our systems to incorporate Land Border Surveillance Systems. Our new Sovereign Territory Surveillance (STS) Systems will play a crucial role in enhancing civil defence security through the deployment of advanced automated security infrastructures. Utilised by nations worldwide, these technologies facilitate the monitoring of sovereign land borders, thereby strengthening border integrity and national security.

 Research Engineer (Planning and Decision-Making)

About the Role

We’re hiring a Research Engineer to work on the planning methods at the core of our software.

Our software turns operational requirements (what needs doing, how often, and constraints like battery, safety and no-go areas) into mission plans that a robot or a fleet executes over hours, days and weeks. Things don’t always go as expected on a real site — tasks fail, areas get blocked, conditions change — so plans have to account for what might go wrong, not just the expected case. The planning methods come from 10+ years of Oxford research on decision-making under uncertainty, and they’re running now with pilot customers on real robots.

The role focuses on designing and implementing planning, scheduling and task allocation methods and adding them to our core solutions. What you build becomes part of a live robot system at customer sites, so code quality, testing and evaluation are a core part of the job too. You’ll work with the rest of the team to integrate your work into the main system and keep it reliable once it’s there. Experience with robots is valued but not required.

Key Responsibilities

• Design, implement and ship planning, scheduling and task allocation methods as production code in our planning core, including routing and scheduling under time and battery constraints, and policy synthesis for MDPs and their extensions

• Contribute to our multi-robot work — task allocation across heterogeneous fleets, sharing chargers and other resources between robots, and reallocating work when a robot fails or new tasks arrive

• Turn customer problems into models the planner can solve, working from a site’s operations, constraints and data, and extend the pipeline that fits model parameters from operational data

• Improve solver performance so we can plan for larger fleets, more tasks and longer horizons

• Get plans running on robots, working with our software and field engineers in simulation and on site, and fix what breaks when deploying in the real world

• Bring new methods into the team from your own area, keep up with the planning, scheduling and decision-making literature, and critically assess their applicability to Stateful’s problems

• Keep software quality high through code review, tests, CI and documentation

• Keep up with how LLMs and agentic tools are being used in and around planning, and bring what’s useful into our work

About You

StoryToys, an independent subsidiary of Team17 Group plc, is a premier, award-winning developer and publisher of interactive educational apps designed to help children learn, play, and grow. About the role
We are seeking a 3D Principal Artist to work with us in high profile games alongside world leading brands. 
You will focus on end-to-end pipeline development to improve the tools, looks and processes used by our 3D art team and will have experience in a similar category of mobile games. You will help artists work more efficiently by identifying recurring production problems and building practical, reliable solutions across Maya, Unity, and the wider workflow. The result is an effective pipeline that can be used as a template for other projects in the future. 
You will take part in the 3D aspect of visual development, collaborating with partners and stakeholders in the presentation and refinement of high-quality and high-preforming graphics representative of the profile of the games that are being produced. Working closely with the 3D Art Lead, Art Manager, Technical Artists and Engineering, you will turn agreed pipeline priorities into tools, automation and production standards that support multiple products. Requirements
Key responsibilities 
Vis/Dev look: Supervise, and when required, directly input in the creation of visual ideation that fulfills the projected scope and look of the game. Pipeline Improvement: Review workflows from source asset creation through export, Unity import and runtime use. Identify bottlenecks and repetitive tasks, and agree priorities with Art leadership, Production and Engineering. 
Tools and Automation: Develop and maintain Maya scripts and Unity editor tools for tasks such as export, import configuration, asset setup, batch processing and validation. Build tools that artists can use confidently in everyday production. 
Asset Standards and Validation: Implement agreed on naming, folder, export and import standards. Create checks that catch common issues with geometry, materials, textures, rigs and animation before they cause downstream rework. 
Troubleshooting: Investigate problems across Maya scenes, exported assets, Unity settings and project systems. Identify root causes, communicate findings, and collaborate with Engineering where fixes involve shared systems. 
Mobile Optimisation: Support profiling and optimisation of art assets, including geometry, textures, materials, animation and memory use. Help artists apply agreed budgets while preserving the intended visual quality. 
Testing and Rollout: Test tools against representative production assets, manage changes through version control and plan adoption with affected teams. Maintain compatibility and provide practical support as workflows evolve. 
Documentation and Training: Write clear setup and usage guidance, demonstrate new tools and gather artist feedback to improve reliability and adoption. 
Agile Collaboration: Estimate and deliver pipeline work within an Agile environment. Communicate dependencies and technical risks, and assess whether changes reduce rework and improve production efficiency. 

Required skills
• Professional experience in technical art or 3D pipeline development for games or real-time interactive media, with examples of tools or workflow improvements used in production. 
• Strong practical knowledge of Maya and Unity, and of the asset workflow connecting them. 
• Proficiency in Python for Maya tooling and C# for Unity editor tools, with the ability to write clear, maintainable code and diagnose failures. 
• Proficiency in modeling, topology, UVs, materials, texturing, rigging, skinning, and animation. 
• Proven capacity to inspect assets, provide effective actionable feedback that improves the quality of the work and troubleshoot pipeline issues alongside it. 
• Experience with Unity asset import workflows, prefabs, materials, animation setup and automated asset validation. 
• Understanding real-time performance constraints and practical experience using profiling or diagnostic tools to investigate art-related issues. 
• Experience supporting external art vendors, licensed IP or children’s content. 
• Experience with version control such as Git, tool testing and documentation, and a considered approach to changing shared production workflows. 
• Strong problem-solving and communication skills, with the ability to understand artists’ needs and discuss technical trade-offs constructively with Engineering. 

Preferred qualifications 
• Experience supporting Unity mobile games or shared pipelines across multiple products. 
• Experience with Substance Painter workflows, rigging or animation tools, or automated content checks within a build pipeline. 
• Experience with Unity rendering, shaders and materials where these affect asset workflows and performance. 
• Experience working in an Agile environment and using Jira for planning and task management. 

Application process
Please submit your CV and a portfolio, showreel or technical breakdown demonstrating relevant pipeline work. Include examples of tools or automation, the production problem each addressed and your contribution. Code samples or recorded demonstrations are welcome where sharing is permitted.

Founding ML Engineer

You turn raw acoustic and time-series signals from the body into things people can read and act on. This is the hard, unsolved centre of the company.

You may own

- The full modelling pipeline: noisy, unstructured real-world sensor data in, actionable insight out.
- Signal processing on continuous data: extracting clean, robust features from continuous time-series and acoustic streams (DSP, filtering, audio embeddings).
- Edge-to-cloud architecture: models that run on-device (resource-constrained audio and sensor processing) and on the backend, plus the judgement of what goes where.
- Agent context and memory: building the harness that feeds our agent the right things at the right time. Good context and memory are most of the product.
- Ground truth validation: how we validate that what we tell people is actually true. Rigour is the product.

You'll fit if

- Minimum MSc (PhD preferred) in Computer Science, EE, Acoustics, ML or a related technical field.
- Strong proficiency in Python and deep learning frameworks (PyTorch or JAX).
- Deep expertise in acoustic signal processing (spectrograms, audio transformers) and time-series analysis (continuous physiological data, sequence modelling).
- Experience deploying ML models on resource-constrained edge devices (C/C++, TinyML, RTOS or mobile neural engines).

Publications at ICASSP, INTERSPEECH, NeurIPS or ICLR
Physiological acoustics (heart or lung sounds) or wearable sensor fusion (IMWUT, UbiComp)

- Meaningful equity. You share directly in what we build.

- 25 days holiday plus bank holidays, and an extra day for your birthday.
- Workplace pension with employer contribution.
- Top-spec kit as standard: new Mac, noise-cancelling headphones, a proper desk setup, whatever you need.
- Cycle-to-work scheme.
- Dinner on us when the work runs late.
- Visa sponsorship and relocation support where needed.

job_title: Senior Global Account Lead, Uber Eats UK
job_description:
About the role and team 
As an Sr Global Account Manager for one of our largest Global partners in the UK, a global QSR brand, you will be the main point of contact for the partner's HQ and play a key role in growing and strengthening the partnership.
Based in London and reporting to a London-based manager, you'll be part of an international organization, working at the intersection of global, regional, and local teams. A key part of your role will be to navigate this environment, align stakeholders across different levels of the organization, and translate broader strategic priorities into impactful local initiatives.
You'll develop a deep understanding of the partner's business, priorities, and challenges to identify growth opportunities, improve performance, and deliver long-term value through Uber Eats.
Working closely with Customer Success Managers (CSMs) and Account Coordinators (ACs), you'll turn data-driven insights into actionable plans and ensure their successful execution.
This role offers a unique opportunity to own a major strategic partnership while gaining exposure to global business initiatives and developing strong cross-functional stakeholder management skills.

What you’ll do 
• Sales Strategy & Execution: Develop and execute joint business plans to drive growth and achieve commercial targets. Identify upsell and cross-sell opportunities, leverage data to uncover growth opportunities, and collaborate with internal specialists to implement initiatives. Support commercial discussions and negotiations with the partner
• Client Success & Retention: Act as the main point of contact for the partner's HQ, building strong relationships with key stakeholders. Lead regular business reviews and Joint Business Planning sessions to align on priorities, track progress, and identify opportunities to strengthen the partnership
• Performance Analysis & Operational Execution: Work closely with CSMs and Account Coordinators to analyze business performance, identify opportunities for improvement, and translate insights into concrete action plans. Coordinate execution, monitor KPIs, and ensure initiatives deliver measurable results
• Partnership Development: Proactively identify opportunities to improve the partner's experience, strengthen engagement with HQ and franchisees, and support the long-term growth of the partnership
• Global, Regional & Local Stakeholder Management: Play a central role in connecting global, regional, and local teams, ensuring alignment between international partnership strategies and local market priorities. Build strong internal relationships, navigate different stakeholder expectations, and coordinate cross-functional initiatives involving Commercial, Operations, Marketing, Ads, and Support teams. Act as a key facilitator to drive decisions, remove roadblocks, and ensure effective execution across the organization

Basic Qualifications 
• 7+ years of experience in account management, business development, consulting, or a similar commercial role, ideally within a tech company or fast-paced environment
• Experience managing client relationships, driving commercial initiatives, and delivering measurable business results
• Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interpret data, identify trends, and translate insights into actionable recommendations
• Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to collaborate across different teams, functions, and organizational levels, ideally in an international environment
• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the confidence to engage with senior business stakeholders
• Collaborative mindset, with the ability to influence without direct authority and coordinate execution across teams
• Proactive, organized, and solution-oriented, with a hands-on approach and a strong sense of ownership

About the Role
This is a new role, creating a new capability for Uber Eats in EMEA.
A single investment vehicle owns a portfolio of QSR and Casual Dining brands operating across multiple EMEA markets. Today, Uber's relationship with that portfolio is managed market by market. This role changes that: it establishes a single, EMEA-wide operational capability that sits above the individual markets and owns the portfolio end to end.
As the Customer Success Manager for EMEA Enterprise Accounts, you will be the connective tissue between the fund's HQ, the leadership of each of its brands, and Uber Eats' commercial teams across EMEA. You'll map to and own the most senior HQ relationships, build the standardised reporting and QBR cadence the portfolio has never had, and - critically - turn Uber's data into decision-grade insight that helps these brands decide which markets to enter next, where to put their next store, which customer segments to target, and which brands to acquire.
You will work alongside a dedicated analyst, so you don't need to build the queries yourself. What you do need is the judgement to know which question is worth asking, the rigour to interrogate what the data actually says, and the presence to land the resulting recommendation with a brand CEO and with a sophisticated finance team at an investment fund.
This is a build role. You will be designing the playbook as you run it, working in close partnership with Account Managers in each market and with the EMEA Enterprise Director. 
What the Candidate Will Do
• Relationship mapping• Build durable relationships with the most senior HQ contacts accountable across all EMEA markets 
• Establish Uber Eats as the default strategic partner at HQ level, not only at market level

• Reporting• Design and run a standardised EMEA-level QBR for the portfolio.
• Build consistent, comparable reporting by brand and by market, giving HQ a single view of performance across the portfolio.
• Own cross-market prospect pipeline management, giving HQ and local teams a shared and accurate view of what's live, what's landing and what's next.

• Insights• Set the analytical agenda for the account and direct the work of a dedicated analyst. Become an extension of the Partner’s strategy team, answering questions such as which market to enter next, where to open the next store, which Customer Segment to target and how to optimise menu pricing strategy
• Interpret complex datasets, draw conclusions and convert them into clear, defensible recommendations that HQ and local teams can act on.
• Present those recommendations credibly to brand C-Suite and to investment-fund finance professionals.

• Coordination• Drive knowledge sharing and best-practice standardisation across markets, so a win in one country becomes the default in the next.
• Coordinate cross-market prospecting and ensure the portfolio experiences one seamless, joined-up Uber.
• Work closely with Account Managers in each market and with the Director across the account, aligning them behind a single portfolio plan.

• Hearts and minds• Win merchant sentiment through elevated, consistent service. Be the partner's advocate inside Uber and Uber's advocate inside the partner.

• EMEA deals• Act as a core member of the deal team on EMEA-level commercial agreements aimed at winning new markets, securing preferential terms and establishing Uber Eats as the preferred partner across the portfolio.
• Build the commercial case, shape the strategy and supply the analysis and partner insight that underpin the negotiation, working with Legal, Finance and local commercial leadership.

• Build the capability• Define the operating model, cadence and playbook for EMEA Enterprise account management — and make it repeatable for the next portfolio after this one.

Basic Qualifications
• 6+ years' experience in account management, customer success, strategic partnerships, commercial strategy, consulting or a comparable client-facing role.
• Demonstrable experience owning senior, multi-stakeholder relationships, including at C-Suite or equivalent level.
• Strong analytical judgement: able to interpret complex data, stress-test the conclusions and turn them into a clear, well-argued recommendation.
• Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the credibility to hold the room with both commercial and finance audiences.
• Experience working across multiple markets or through matrixed, in-market teams.

Preferred Qualifications
• Experience in QSR, Casual Dining, restaurant, retail, FMCG or delivery/marketplace businesses.
• Experience working with private equity or investment funds, or with portfolio-level stakeholders, and fluency with the metrics they care about.
• Experience contributing to complex, multi-market commercial negotiations as part of a deal team.
• Experience directing or partnering with analytical resource to produce client-facing insight.
• Comfort operating with ambiguity and defining structure where none exists.

Additional Information
• Based in London, in line with Uber's hybrid working policy.
• Some travel across EMEA markets will be required, though it is expected to be limited

Senior Commercial Team Manager – UK & Ireland Central Banks and Capital Markets

We are seeking a Senior Commercial Team Manager to lead commercial strategy, client growth, and team performance across a portfolio of Central Banks and Capital Markets clients within the UK & Ireland. This senior-level people manager role is accountable for translating business strategy into commercially focused plans, building trusted relationships with senior client and industry stakeholders, and ensuring the organisation is positioned as the solution of choice in a complex and evolving financial ecosystem.

Role Overview:
• The Senior Commercial Team Manager defines, proposes, and leads commercial plans for assigned areas of responsibility, ensuring alignment with regional and organisational objectives. The role manages the delivery of short- and long-term commercial outcomes, oversees major client relationships and initiatives, and provides leadership to a team of commercial account managers. Working closely with senior management and cross-functional partners, the role contributes to broader commercial strategy, strengthens market presence, and drives sustainable business growth through disciplined execution and client-focused leadership.
Key Responsibilities
• Define, propose, and lead commercial strategy and plans for the UK & Ireland Central Banks and Capital Markets team, industry engagement, regional programmes, and strategic initiatives.

• Own and strengthen long-term relationships with major clients and senior stakeholders, ensuring client needs, strategies, risks, and concerns are understood, anticipated, and addressed.
• Identify market opportunities, client needs, and competitive developments, using insight to influence commercial direction, improve the value proposition, and support business development.
• Lead the implementation of large-scale business plans, client initiatives, Central Bank and market infrastructure engagements, or strategic programmes by coordinating activities across teams, divisions, and regions.
• Act as the senior point of contact for major accounts, clients, market infrastructures, or initiatives, representing the organisation with credibility in client meetings, industry bodies, and external forums.
• Ensure effective liaison with internal divisions and departments to provide coordinated service, integrated solutions, market intelligence, product feedback, and relevant training or information to commercial account management teams.
• Promote the organisation as the solution of choice within the assigned area by strengthening market presence, building advocacy, and ensuring consistent representation of the organisation’s capabilities.
• Hire, coach, reward, motivate, and develop team members, ensuring the department has the capability, engagement, and leadership depth required to deliver against current and future objectives.
• Prepare, propose, substantiate, and manage departmental budgets, including allocation of approved budget, authorisation of expenditures, and assessment of budget performance.
• Model organisational values, promote collaboration across teams and regions, and create an inclusive environment that supports performance, learning, and knowledge sharing.

• Accountability for significant decisions: Makes and takes accountability for operational and tactical decisions with meaningful business impact, including under conditions of pressure, adversity, and uncertainty.

• Client and market influence: Builds trusted relationships with senior clients and industry stakeholders, translates complex needs into practical solutions, and promotes client focus across the team.
• Operational excellence: Sets clear standards for quality, reliability, client satisfaction, and disciplined execution, while encouraging continuous improvement across the department.

You'll own data correctness across Talos. You'll lead the data quality engineering team, run BAU data operations, and own reference and security master data, along with the pipelines and platform that deliver it.

Our goal: the data we return to clients is always correct, and we find defects before a client does.

You'll join a small team with the mandate to work independently from product engineering and challenge it. Engineering teams make assumptions about how their systems behave. Your job is to test those assumptions and prove or disprove them with evidence.

 


RESPONSIBILITIES

Lead AI-first data quality engineering

 - Validate every client-facing endpoint continuously. The focus is our REST and WebSocket APIs. Cloud delivery (S3, Snowflake, Databricks) is also in scope. Assert correctness against independent sources of truth, across every environment and client entitlement.

 - Cover streaming as well as request/response. For WebSocket, that means:
   
   - Sequencing and gap detection
   
   - Snapshot-to-increment consistency
   
   - Reconnect and replay correctness
   
   - Staleness of live subscriptions
   
   - Agreement between the streamed view and the REST view of the same state

 - Use adaptive detection, not static thresholds. Learn baselines per endpoint and per market, and let them adjust as "normal" changes. Hand-set limits get noisy, go stale, and teach people to ignore alerts.

 - Apply LLM and agentic tooling to generate checks from API specs and schemas, keep them current as the product changes, and triage alerts before a human sees them. Know when a deterministic rule, invariant or cross-source reconciliation is the better tool.

 - Test resilience and load. Design load, performance and failure-mode tests.

 - When you find a fault, raise it with the owning team with enough evidence for them to act. Drive it to resolution, then add a check that would have caught it earlier.

 - Measure and publish endpoint and field coverage, time to detect, detected-before-client rate and false-positive rate.

Run data governance

 - Build and maintain a catalog of our data assets and APIs, covering lineage and downstream consumers. Maintain an understanding of assets, how they're used and what breaks when they change.

 - Own data governance tooling such as OpenMetadata.

Own reference and security master data

 - Lead the build-out of the next-generation security master platform, then run it day to day: new listings, symbol mapping across venues, and increment and contract specs.

 - Design processes for safe updates to security entries, with validation and rollback.

Expand coverage across the firm

 - Over time, extend data quality coverage beyond client APIs to:
   
   - Trade signals
   
   - Pre-trade analytics
   
   - Client post-trade analysis
   
   - PMS analytics

 - A deep understanding of streaming and API behaviour: throughput, WebSocket semantics, ordering, recovery and failure modes.

 - Experience inventorying and testing a large API and data surface end to end.

 - Hands-on experience with data governance: cataloging, lineage, ownership.

 - Experience with performance and load testing of distributed systems.

 - A strong engineering background. You design platforms, not scripts on a cron job, and you build on shared infrastructure rather than creating one-off tooling.

 - Practical experience applying LLM and agentic tooling to engineering problems.

 - Our stack: Flink, Doris, Dagster and Spark, plus OpenMetadata (or an equivalent such as Apache Atlas). Experience with comparable tools is just as relevant.

THE ROLE:

We’re hiring a Staff Product Manager to own the portfolio side of Rosso, a hands-on role built around financial outcomes.

Rosso is deeply technical, built on ML-led models and complex engineering covering forecasting, pricing optimisation and portfolio balancing. The portfolio is where the live financial risk sits: fulfilling and balancing a growing two-sided portfolio, managing imbalance, controlling portfolio costs, and finding the revenue and margin in every position we hold. It’s still forming, and it needs someone who wants to own the outcome and win in it.

This is a lead role, but not a head-of-product role. You’ll be building, not running a product practice. You’ll work day to day with engineers and ML specialists to build an automated portfolio management system that handles balancing, forecasting and counterparty placement, and that could be exposed to third parties in future.

You will:

 - Own financial outcomes for the portfolio, including the cost of balancing and managing positions, and be accountable for margin found and risk managed.

 - Work hands-on with engineers and ML/data science to build automated, quantitative systems that run at scale and under live financial risk.

 - Drive open product decisions to a close, with a clear Now, Next and Future for the portfolio area.




🚀 RESPONSIBILITIES:

Own the portfolio outcome

 - Take full ownership of financial outcomes in the portfolio area: balancing, imbalance, forecasting and counterparty placement.

 - Treat hedging, imbalance and trading decisions as product decisions: when to hold a position, when to trade it out, when to reprice to close a gap.

 - Find the most pressing problems worth solving, such as whether to buy or build a new forecasting capability, or how to make Rosso react at scale to any event in the system.

 - Chase the commercial outcome, not just the shipped feature. The measure of this role is margin found and risk managed, at pace.

Turn needs into shipped product

 - Take business and customer needs and turn them into feasible product execution, balancing them against nascent ML and forecasting innovations that push the frontier of what’s possible.

 - Take initiatives from discovery through to regularly released product.

 - Drive open product decisions to a close, yours and the team’s, so work keeps moving.

 - Decide what to formalise, what stays a prototype and what to drop. Be the editor and builder, not just the instigator.

Own the technical-product detail

 - Work embedded in full-stack teams of ML/data science and software engineers, close enough to the systems to make good calls.

 - Set clear success criteria for how well a model or forecast needs to perform for the product to work, and design for the edge cases and operational reality of a system carrying live financial risk.

 - Pull and interrogate your own and others’ data to inform decisions, and reason about model performance and error as business indicators.

 - Get close to the people who use what you build, from internal commercial teams to generators and businesses externally.

Lead by doing

 - Set the pace for the product team and raise the standard of product work around you, through your own work and example rather than by managing a function.

 - Work alongside the other PM on Rosso and the Product Lead, with clear ownership of the portfolio area.




🎯 REQUIREMENTS:

Must haves

 - Senior, hands-on product management experience. You’ve owned a complex, financially significant product area end to end, with a track record of moving real business outcomes, not just shipping features.

 - Domain knowledge in energy trading and markets: positions, hedging, balancing and imbalance, and what it means for a system to carry live financial risk. Strong adjacent experience (financial trading, fintech, battery or EV trading) will be considered, but real depth of understanding is needed.

 - Experience building automated, quantitative systems, or working in pods that do, alongside engineers.

 - Commercial drive. You push decisions to a close and go after revenue and margin. You want to win, and it shows in how you work.

 - Comfortable working with ML specialists. You don’t need hands-on ML experience, but you know how to work with data scientists and can reason about model performance and error as business indicators.

 - Uses data analysis throughout the product process, to validate ideas, progress work and measure success.

 - Built product in a startup, scaleup or other high-growth environment, with high personal ownership.

 - A strong instinct for failure points, edge cases and the operational reality of a live system.

 - AI-native, AI-literate and AI-critical: you know where it helps and where it hurts.

 - A clear, structured communicator, especially in writing.

Bonus points

 - Hands-on energy trading experience: intraday, day-ahead, imbalance or battery optimisation.

 - Experience where forecasting or fulfilling a two-sided marketplace is central to the product.

 - Experience going through a third-party-access and/or international-expansion transition.

 • Use AI tools to speed up tracking, follow-ups, and reporting.

**About CloudBees**

CloudBees helps organizations build, run, and govern software factories, giving enterprises the confidence to ship software better, faster, and safer.

Writing code is no longer the bottleneck. Governing what reaches production and validating its impact is. As enterprises adopt agentic coding, software is created faster than most teams can review, secure, and validate. Without consistent governance, organizations risk shipping code they cannot explain, audit, or trust.

Across every toolchain a customer runs, CloudBees makes each change, human or AI, visible, auditable, and accountable before it reaches production. Founded in 2010, CloudBees is backed by Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Bridgepoint Capital, HSBC, Golub Capital, Delta-v Capital, Matrix Partners, and Lightspeed Venture Partners.

Visit us at www.cloudbees.com.

**The Opportunity**

Germany's flagship enterprises - automotive, manufacturing, financial services, telecoms - run some of the most demanding software delivery operations in Europe. As AI accelerates how much code gets written, the pressure on delivery, governance, and security only grows. CloudBees helps them build better, faster, and safer. We're hiring the seller who will own that story in the German market, based out of London.

This is not a classic AE seat. You'll operate as the franchise owner of the German strategic business: developing our most important existing customers - including DAX 40 and MDAX organizations - while personally opening the strategic accounts we haven't won yet. You'll work from our London hub with regular travel to Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

Requirements

**About the Role: Two Motions, One Owner**

**Protect & grow.** Develop strategic existing German customers, build durable executive relationships from engineering leadership to the C-suite, and identify major expansion opportunities.

**Hunt & create.** Penetrate net-new strategic accounts across the DACH region and personally generate pipeline - with a repeatable prospecting system of your own, not a dependency on inbound.

**What You'll Do**

- Own a territory of strategic German enterprise accounts end to end - strategy, relationships, pipeline, and revenue.
- Run complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles in German across CIOs, CTOs, VPs of Engineering, CISOs, technical teams, works-council-aware procurement, and multi-level buying committees.
- Build Champions, gain access to Economic Buyers, and translate technology into business impact: productivity, cost, risk, governance, and time-to-value.

 - AI platform capabilities. Work with the AI Platforms team to turn engagement patterns into safe, increasingly self-serve company-wide tooling.

 - Deploy ML-built components into production. Serving, integration with the Moneybox platform, and everything surrounding the model, in partnership with Decisioning and Data Science teams (who own what happens inside the model) and our engineering squads.

 - Build reusable capability. Convert engagement learnings into shared tooling, templates, playbooks and self-serve workflows on the AI Platforms stack. Building out platform components including guardrails, sandboxing, workflows, and gateways.

job_description:
Job Summary

The Director, Commercial AI & Automation Product Delivery, EMEA provides dedicated leadership and execution capacity to identify, prioritise, design and deliver high-value AI and automation solutions across the wider Commercial Services organisation.

The role operates at the intersection of Commercial business expertise, process improvement, product delivery and applied technology. It works with Commercial leaders and operational teams to identify the most important business problems, map and simplify the underlying process, determine where AI or automation can add measurable value, and move selected opportunities from concept through prototype, proof of value, deployment and adoption.

This is not a pure strategy, portfolio coordination or software engineering role. The Director is accountable for converting Commercial priorities into practical, adopted solutions and measurable outcomes. The role requires sufficient technical capability to prototype and deliver fit-for-purpose solutions using approved tools, including Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Studio, Power Automate and Power Apps, while recognising when enterprise technology, data, security or specialist development support is required.

The Director serves as the senior Commercial product and delivery owner for this portfolio, making recommendations on where to invest, scale, route, revise or stop work. The role partners with EMEA AI governance and central orchestration, while remaining anchored within Commercial Services where business context, process ownership and accountability for execution sit.

Key Responsibilities

 • Own and actively manage a prioritised portfolio of Commercial AI and automation opportunities aligned with profitable revenue growth, Commercial 30, HOME, and productivity priorities.

 • Evaluate opportunities using business value, user impact, process and data readiness, feasibility, risk, scalability, adoption potential and alignment with enterprise capabilities. Recommend which initiatives should proceed, combine, route, defer or stop.

 • Partner with Commercial discipline leaders, regional teams, subject-matter experts and users to diagnose material business pain points and determine whether the answer is process change, clearer accountability, automation, AI or a combination.

 • Translate ambiguous business needs into clear problem statements, process maps, requirements, test scopes, success measures and proof-of-value plans. Challenge requests constructively where technology would automate the wrong process or create insufficient value.

 • Lead selected use cases from discovery through prototype, testing, governance review, deployment, adoption and benefit measurement, maintaining clear stage gates, owners, decisions and delivery momentum.

 • Act as the senior Commercial product owner, making or facilitating decisions on scope, priorities, user experience, business requirements and release readiness across multiple disciplines and stakeholder groups.

 • Use practical knowledge of Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Studio, Power Automate, Power Apps and related approved tools to explore solutions, build prototypes and deliver appropriate low-code automations.

 • Assess when a solution can be delivered within Commercial and when it requires support from IT, HQ AI Studio, Data & Analytics, Information Security, Privacy, Legal or specialist engineering teams. Ensure solutions use approved pathways and do not create unsupported shadow technology.

 • Build adoption, communication, training, change impact and support requirements into delivery from the outset. Engage users throughout discovery, testing and refinement so solutions fit real workflows and can be sustained.

 • Track usage, user feedback, operational performance and realised benefits after implementation. Establish clear ownership and support arrangements before broader deployment.

 • Capture reusable components, patterns and playbooks so successful solutions can be applied across Commercial teams, markets or hotels where appropriate.

 • Partner with the EMEA AI orchestration team to provide visibility of the Commercial portfolio, identify overlaps and reuse opportunities, and route solutions appropriately without duplicating central orchestration responsibilities.

 • Provide Commercial leadership with concise, evidence-based updates on progress, benefits, risks, resource needs, blockers and decisions required. Surface recurring process, data or capability barriers that limit delivery.

 • Influence senior stakeholders across Commercial, continent and HQ teams, balancing competing priorities while protecting scarce delivery capacity and maintaining a strong bias toward practical execution and measurable outcomes.

Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is a commercially grounded, technology-fluent delivery leader who can move comfortably between senior stakeholder discussions, business processes, user needs and hands-on solution development. They must be credible enough to make continent-wide portfolio and prioritisation recommendations, practical enough to work directly with process owners and users, and technically confident enough to prototype, challenge solution design and make sound delivery decisions.

This role is not intended for a narrow technical specialist whose primary strength is coding, or for a general strategist whose contribution ends with recommendations and roadmaps. It requires a balanced leader who can determine what should be built, shape how it should work, mobilise the right contributors and remain accountable until the solution is operating and delivering value.

 • Significant experience in Commercial e.g. revenue management, sales, marketing, digital, distribution, loyalty, commercial operations, or a closely related field.

 • Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives from ambiguous business need through implementation, adoption and measurable outcome.

 • Strong Commercial acumen and judgement on value, feasibility, operational impact, scalability, adoption risk and return on investment.

 • Practical experience with AI, low-code and workflow automation, particularly Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Studio, Power Automate and Power Apps. Able to build prototypes or fit-for-purpose solutions while recognising when specialist technical development is required.

 • Strong capability in process mapping, requirements gathering, testing, change adoption, benefit tracking and product or programme delivery.

 • High credibility with senior business and technical stakeholders, with the ability to influence across functions and geographies without relying on direct authority.

 • Good understanding of enterprise data, privacy, security, responsible AI and governance considerations.

 • Ability to simplify complex issues, challenge constructively, communicate in clear business language and maintain disciplined follow-through in a matrix organisation.

 • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience. Relevant Microsoft Power Platform, AI, product, agile, process improvement or change qualifications are advantageous but not essential.

Leadership Scope and Role Boundaries

The Director owns Commercial use-case prioritisation, business problem definition, process clarity, product decisions, proof-of-value design, appropriate hands-on prototyping, delivery momentum, adoption planning and benefit realisation. The role carries end-to-end accountability for a cross-discipline EMEA portfolio rather than executing assigned automation requests.

The Director partners on enterprise governance, cross-discipline portfolio visibility, technical architecture, security, data access, complex integrations and scaled production support. The role does not own enterprise AI governance, central EMEA orchestration, general Commercial strategy and planning, technology architecture or specialist software engineering.

Success Measures

 • Measurable business value, productivity or Commercial performance improvement delivered through implemented solutions.

 • A focused, transparent portfolio with clear priorities, ownership, stage gates, risks and evidence-based scale, route or stop decisions.

 • Improved speed from validated business need to usable prototype or solution, without compromising approved governance and technical pathways.

 • Strong adoption, usage, user feedback and sustainable ownership for deployed solutions.

 • Reduction in duplicated, disconnected or low-value experimentation and improved reuse of successful solutions across teams, markets or hotels.

 • Quality of business problem definition, process mapping, requirements, testing and benefit measurement.

 • Effective collaboration with Commercial disciplines, EMEA governance and orchestration, IT, HQ AI Studio, Data & Analytics and other enterprise partners.

 • Clear evidence that Commercial AI and automation work is moving from discussion and experimentation to practical execution and measurable outcomes.

Key Working Relationships

EMEA Commercial Services leadership; Commercial discipline and process owners; regional and field stakeholders; EMEA AI governance and orchestration; EMEA and HQ IT; HQ AI Studio; Data & Analytics; Information Security, Privacy and Legal; HR/L&D and change partners; Digital Operations, low-code builders and approved external partners.

Right to work

At the time of application, applicants must have the legal right to work in the United Kingdom. Unfortunately, this role is not eligible for visa sponsorship or relocation assistance.

Position Summary

The Automation Engineer III identifies, develops, implements, and supports automation solutions that improve manufacturing safety, quality, productivity, capacity, reliability, and cost performance. This role provides technical leadership for automation and equipment projects and serves as a key technical resource for production equipment, robotics, controls, motion systems, and equipment integration -partnering with Manufacturing, Engineering, Operations, Quality, Continous Improvement, Finance, Facilities, and equipment suppliers to translate production needs into reliable, scalable, financially justified solutions. The role requires broad engineering knowledge and the ability to independently manage complex assignments from opportunity identification and business-case development through design, implementation, validation, and benefits realization.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Automation & Equipment Engineering
• Identify, design, and implement automation systems -robotics, motion control, material handling, sensors, machine vision, automated inspection -that improve productivity, quality, capacity, ergonomics, and safety.
• Provide advanced engineering support and structured root-cause troubleshooting for equipment, controls, mechanical, electrical, and process issues.
• Develop corrective actions and improvements that increase equipment reliability, uptime, throughput, and maintainability.
• Monitor equipment/process performance using operational data, alarms, and downtime to identify recurring failure modes and predictive-maintenance opportunities.
• Maintain equipment configurations, specifications, control requirements, and documentation needed to keep equipment in a validated, controlled state.

Process Troubleshooting & Equipment Reliability
• Conduct manufacturing equipment failure investigations and structured troubleshooting of equipment/process failures.
• Study equipment performance and reliability trends; participate in defining preventive-maintenance schedules, procedures, and spare-parts strategies.
• Oversee adherence to maintenance and calibration schedules and ensure activities are properly documented; support complex equipment issues, including off-shift as needed.

Automation Project Leadership
• Lead automation projects end-to-end -from opportunity identification through implementation and sustained operation -working directly with stakeholders to understand process challenges and opportunities.
• Develop technical concepts, feasibility studies, scope, cost estimates, schedules, risk assessments, and business cases; evaluate opportunities by feasibility, value, and risk.
• Support CAPEX planning and technical justification; coordinate cross-functional teams and manage projects to scope, schedule, budget, and expected outcomes.

Installation, Integration & Validation
• Define facility, utility, safety, and production requirements for new automated equipment.
• Coordinate installation, commissioning, FAT/SAT testing, and production handoff; perform or support IQ/OQ/PQ and develop test plans and acceptance criteria.
• Support new product/process introduction and ensure equipment design considers reliability, maintainability, usability, and safety.

Vendor & Technology Management
• Develop technical specifications for suppliers; evaluate vendors, technologies, and system integrators.
• Provide technical direction during design, fabrication, testing, and commissioning; review and approve drawings, specs, and control concepts.
• Manage vendor technical issues through resolution and evaluate alternative equipment and second-source solutions.

Continuous Improvement & Technical Leadership
• Partner with Manufacturing, Operations, PPI, and Finance to establish baselines and quantify benefits (labor savings, cycle time, uptime, scrap, cost avoidance) using PPI/structured problem-solving.
• Maintain a prioritized automation opportunity pipeline; serve as technical subject-matter resource and mentor engineers/technicians.
• Lead cross-functional teams without direct authority; communicate status, risks, and recommendations to leadership.

Supervisory Responsibilities
No direct supervisory responsibility; however, this role is expected to provide technical leadership and direction to project teams, contractors, suppliers, integrators, and technicians to ensure successful delivery of automation initiatives.

Education & Experience
• Bachelor's degree in Automation, Electrical, Mechanical, or Manufacturing Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, Controls Engineering, or related technical discipline; advanced degree a plus.
• Significant relevant experience in manufacturing/factory automation, equipment engineering, controls, or robotics, consistent with an Engineer III level, including independently delivering complex automation projects.
• Experience in regulated, life-sciences, medical-device, semiconductor, or similarly complex manufacturing environments preferred.

Technical Knowledge & Skills

Industrial automation and automated manufacturing equipment; robotics and integration; PLC/industrial control systems; HMI; servo systems and motion control; sensors, actuators, pneumatics, and electromechanical systems; machine vision and automated inspection; material handling and precision positioning; equipment troubleshooting and root-cause analysis; commissioning, qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ), and validation; preventive-maintenance program development and equipment reliability improvement; equipment safety concepts; engineering drawings and specifications; and capital-equipment specification, procurement, and vendor management.

Problem Solving, Communication & Leadership

Demonstrated ability to define complex technical problems, analyze data, determine root causes, and implement sustainable solutions -including in ambiguous situations requiring engineering judgment and innovation. Applies engineering, mathematics, and analysis to balance performance, cost, schedule, safety, and maintainability. Strong written/verbal communication with operators through senior leadership; ability to translate technical topics into business recommendations; ability to influence and lead cross-functional teams without direct authority; and ability to prepare technical reports, business cases, and presentations, and to train and develop others.

Key Competencies

Technical depth and engineering judgment • Factory automation expertise • End-to-end project ownership • Structured problem solving • Innovation and continuous improvement • Business and financial awareness • Project and vendor management • Cross-functional collaboration • Stakeholder management • Proactive communication • Quality and compliance mindset • Influence without authority • Focus on measurable business impact

Success in the Role

Success is demonstrated not only by delivering technically successful automation solutions, but by creating sustainable, measurable improvements to manufacturing operations. The engineer is expected to operate as a technical leader who independently identifies opportunities, drives implementation, and demonstrates operational and financial impact -continuously challenging existing methods and applying automation, robotics, and equipment engineering to make Thermo Fisher Scientific manufacturing safer, more reliable, more productive, and more scalable.

You will enjoy working in an environment where priorities can change quickly and where strong organisation, communication and attention to detail really matter.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills and confidence building relationships with customers and colleagues at different levels.

This role offers the opportunity to build your project management career within a global organisation supporting the delivery of clinical studies.

# Member of _Technical Staff_

Full-time · London · Technical Staff · Open on a rolling basis

This is the role we keep open permanently. The work here is interesting enough that pure mathematics and frontier deep learning sit in the same team, applied to the same problem: measuring what biology is actually doing. It does not divide cleanly into research, infrastructure and product. The person who derives the estimator is usually the person who ships it, and the person who ships it is usually the first to discover where it breaks. Member of Technical Staff is our name for people who move across those boundaries, and for whom the problem matters more than the title.

## What you would do

There is no fixed answer. Depending on who you are, it might mean training world models of human physiology on national-scale compute, making a statistical method rigorous enough to publish and robust enough to run in a hospital, building the data machinery that gets longitudinal clinical records to a GPU without losing what makes them clinical, or proving something about noise that changes what the platform can claim. What stays constant is the object of study: physiological and clinical time series, the mathematics of measurement, and the instruments we build to resolve biological change that coarser methods average away.

## What we're looking for

- **Evidence of exceptional ability** in a quantitative discipline: mathematics, physics, computer science, quantitative finance, computational neuroscience, or a field we have not thought to list. We care about the evidence, not the credential. A proof, a system, a paper, a trading model, a repository.
- **The instinct to build.** Research that ends as an idea is half-finished here. We want people who consider a result unproven until it runs.
- **Taste for the layer beneath the models.** Measurement, inference, estimation, the structure of time.

## How this works

We hire on a rolling basis. There are no application windows and no cycles: we read every application, and when the person is right, we make the role. Tell us what you have built or proven, and why the measurement problem is the one you want to work on.

Bridge the gap between cutting-edge AI research and practical application. You will own the design, training, and fine-tuning of advanced machine learning models to solve complex, domain-specific problems. We value engineering driven by first-principles thinking — someone who genuinely enjoys digging into the math of the latest arXiv papers, exploring novel architectures, and rapidly translating theoretical breakthroughs into functional, high-performance prototypes.

## What you'll do

- **Model architecture & design:** research, design, and prototype deep learning architectures tailored to our data domain — generative models, geometric deep learning, large-scale transformers.
- **Experimental exploration:** own rigorous experimental roadmaps — ablation studies, hyperparameter optimisation, and loss-function engineering.
- **Algorithmic & compute optimisation:** integrate novel optimisations (custom attention, tokenisation, layer normalisation) with an eye on memory efficiency and training stability.
- **Data strategy & feature engineering:** design representation, augmentation, and synthesis strategies for complex, constrained biological datasets.
- **Collaborative hand-off:** partner with MLOps so prototypes are built for stability and transition cleanly into scaled production.

## What we're looking for

- **Advanced ML & deep learning:** deep theoretical and practical grasp of modern frameworks (PyTorch preferred), optimisation, and neural-network primitives.
- **Scientific computing & math:** strong linear algebra, calculus, probability, and statistics; fluency with NumPy, SciPy, and Pandas.
- **Research translation:** read an academic paper, understand its mechanics, and reproduce or adapt it in clean, modular Python.
- **Software fundamentals:** maintainable Python, Git, and rigorous testing with PyTest.
- **Experiment tracking:** Weights & Biases, MLflow, or TensorBoard to document and reproduce dense training runs.

## Nice to have

An advanced degree (MSc/PhD) in a quantitative field; experience with large-scale generative models or spatial, time-series, or geometric data; open-source contributions or publications at NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, or CVPR.
