—Integrate and maintain pricing models used for trading and risk. These aren’t static libraries. They evolve with the market, and they break if you don’t understand them.
—Work across adjacent services within the platform, including order management, trade capture, position keeping, product reference, and market data systems. The system is interconnected whether you like it or not.
—Collaborate closely with pricing quants, quantitative developers, traders, and operations. Ideas don’t live in isolation here. They get tested, challenged, and either deployed or discarded.
—Build primarily in C++ and Python, where performance and control both matter. One gives you speed, the other gives you flexibility. You’re expected to know why and when.
—Engage directly with the trading desk and risk managers. No layers to hide behind. If something breaks or underperforms, you’ll hear about it in real time.

Requirements

—4+ years of experience in a front or middle office environment, where systems are tied directly to trading outcomes. You’ve seen production pressure, not just clean abstractions.
—Deep expertise in low-latency, high-throughput Linux development using advanced C/C++ and STL. You understand where cycles go, and you don’t waste them.
—Strong experience designing and building multithreaded and distributed systems. Concurrency isn’t theoretical to you. You’ve dealt with race conditions, contention, and failure modes in the wild.
—Experience working with pricing models is highly desirable. You don’t need to be a quant, but you should understand what the models are doing and how they fail.
—Solid understanding of asset classes such as Equities, Futures, Options, and Swaps is preferred. Markets have structure, and ignorance of it shows quickly.
—Familiarity with execution and instrument lifecycles, including corporate actions, settlement, bond coupons, and swap resets. The unglamorous plumbing that breaks first if misunderstood.
—Advanced knowledge of distributed network architecture. Latency, reliability, and data flow are not buzzwords, they’re constraints you design around.
—Proficient with Linux and the GCC toolchain, including Red Hat environments. You should be comfortable operating close to the system, not abstracted away from it.
—Experience with GUI frameworks such as Qt, wxWidgets, or MFC is a bonus. Useful, but not where the real game is played.
—Clear communicator and effective collaborator. Not because it sounds nice, but because systems like this fail quickly when people operate in silos.

Role overview

Westren Capital is a London-based proprietary trading firm specialising in digital asset markets. This role sits within our Trading Technology team, building and supporting the systems that connect our trading strategies to venues, exchanges, and liquidity sources across digital asset markets. Where our platform and pricing teams focus on the core trading engine, this role owns the layer around it: exchange connectivity, trade capture, monitoring, and the tools that let traders and engineers see what the system is actually doing at any given moment.

Responsibilities

- Build and maintain exchange connectivity and trade capture systems across a growing number of digital asset venues
- Design and support monitoring and alerting tools that give traders and engineers real-time visibility into system health and trading activity
- Investigate and resolve production issues across the trading systems stack, often under time pressure when a venue or connection misbehaves
- Work across a multi-language stack (Python, C++, and others) depending on what a given system actually needs
- Collaborate closely with traders, quants, and platform engineers to understand how systems are actually used, not just how they were spec'd
- Improve reliability and observability of trading systems on an ongoing basis, not just when something breaks

Requirements

- Solid programming experience in Python and/or C++, with the ability to work across a mixed-language trading systems stack
- Experience with exchange connectivity, trade capture, or order management systems is a strong advantage
- Comfortable debugging live production issues methodically, under pressure, without guessing
- Strong understanding of Linux systems and networking fundamentals
- Prior exposure to crypto or other 24/7 markets is a plus given the operational demands of always-on trading
- Clear communicator, able to work directly with traders and engineers who need fast, accurate answers

We’re looking for a Head of Awareness to own the top of our funnel and get Whering in front of as many future Wherers as possible. From press coverage and creator activations to big brand partnerships and culture-first moments, you’ll make sure the world knows who we are, then hand those new users over to our Head of Engagement to turn them into super users.

- A brand-building expert with experience across PR, partnerships and influencer marketing
- Plugged into fashion, tech and culture, and always first to spot who’s styling who
- A natural relationship builder, comfortable with journalists, industry bodies, partners and talent alike
- Strategic but hands-on, happy to set the plan, own a budget and get stuck into delivery
- Data-minded, tracking reach, engagement and ROI to prove what’s working

- Build and run Whering’s PR strategy, keeping a steady drumbeat of news, features and op-eds
- Secure speaking slots, awards and invites to key fashion and tech events
- Build relationships with industry bodies like the BFC and the Ellen MacArthur Foundation
- Land sponsorships, co-marketing campaigns and product collaborations
- Plan and deliver influencer and creator activations, from scouting to long-term partnerships
- Champion product features that drive top-of-funnel growth

What we offer

- Flexibility: UK-based remote working, plus our 4-day work week (Monday to Thursday)
- Impact: Full ownership of your own strategy and budget, shaping how Whering shows up across media, industry and culture
- Culture: A small and highly collaborative team that cares about quality and purpose

Join us at a pivotal moment to build the scalable backbone of a platform used by millions. You'll design the NestJS services and own the Google Cloud infrastructure that power the Whering experience, while driving the architectural decisions that shape our technical foundation for years to come.

- You're an architect and a builder. You design systems with the long term in mind, then roll up your sleeves to ship them.
- You're an expert problem-solver. Complex issues across distributed systems and microservices don't faze you; you dig in until they're resolved.
- You're a collaborative mentor. You raise the bar for the whole team through thoughtful code reviews and constructive technical guidance.

Summary:
WHG is seeking an experienced and visionary Head of Information Security to lead and evolve our global information security function. Reporting to the executive team and overseeing the Senior Information Security Engineer and wider security function, you will own and drive the company’s security strategy, governance, risk management programme and long-term roadmap. Combining deep technical expertise with executive-level influence, you will lead a team of security professionals and partner closely with engineering, compliance, legal and executive leadership to protect our people, platforms, customers and data across all jurisdictions, with a particular focus on the regulated online gambling and financial services environment.

This role reports to the Head of IT and is fully remote.

Your day to day:
• Defining and executing the company-wide information security strategy, vision, and multi-year roadmap aligned with business objectives and regulatory obligations.
• Leading, mentoring, and growing the security team, including the Senior Information Security Engineer and other security staff, fostering a culture of accountability, learning, and continuous improvement.
• Owning the enterprise risk management programme, including identification, assessment, treatment, and reporting of security and technology risks to the executive team and board.
• Overseeing compliance with all relevant standards and regulations, including PCI DSS, ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR, and jurisdiction-specific gambling regulations across Malta, the UK, US states and other regulated markets.
• Acting as the senior point of contact for external auditors, regulators, partners, and customers on all matters relating to information security, privacy, and assurance.
• Establishing and maintaining security policies, standards, and procedures, ensuring they are embedded across engineering, operations, and business functions.
• Leading the incident response programme, ensuring readiness through tabletop exercises, playbooks, and clear escalation paths, and taking command during major security incidents.
• Driving the vulnerability management, threat intelligence, and penetration testing programmes, ensuring timely identification and remediation of risks across cloud (AWS) and on-premise environments.
• Championing security-by-design across the SDLC, working with engineering and SRE leadership to embed secure development practices, automation, and tooling.
• Defining and managing the security budget, vendor relationships, and tooling investments to ensure cost-effective and scalable security capabilities.
• Building and running a security awareness and training programme that engages all employees and contractors across the organisation.
• Reporting regularly to the executive team and board on the security posture, key risks, programme progress, and emerging threats.
• Staying ahead of the evolving threat landscape, regulatory developments, and industry best practice, particularly within the online gambling and financial services sectors.

What we are looking for:
• Significant experience in senior information security leadership roles, ideally including Head of Security, CISO, or equivalent positions in regulated industries.
• Proven track record of building and leading high-performing security teams across multiple geographies.
• Deep expertise in security governance, risk, and compliance frameworks such as PCI DSS, ISO 27001, SOC 2, NIST CSF, and GDPR.
• Strong technical foundation across cloud security (AWS), application security, network security, identity and access management, and security operations.
• Experience leading incident response and crisis management at an organisational level, including engagement with regulators and law enforcement where required.
• Industry knowledge of online gambling, fintech, or other highly regulated sectors is strongly preferred.
• Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, CRISC, or equivalent are highly desirable.
• Outstanding communication, influencing, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex security topics for executive and board audiences.
• Strategic mindset combined with hands-on pragmatism and the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, scale-up environment.

• Core Values at Heart: We live by Teamwork, Innovation, Trust, and Integrity in everything we do.
• Results-Oriented Focus: We prioritise getting things done while supporting each other to reach both collective and individual goals.
• Open Collaboration: Our open-door policy fosters collaboration across all levels and departments, where ideas flow freely.
• Global Team: We are truly a global team with people from various countries and cultures contributing to our success.

• A remote and flexible working schedule. 
• Generous time off varied based on the country of residence.

• Training and other learning & development opportunities to support you through your career progression.

Summary:
We are looking for a Product Owner with Payments and Risk experience within the Gaming industry. The ideal candidate will help us manage the payment’s roadmap in accordance with business requirements. Must have a strong understanding of an Agile environment and its methodologies and be able to promote them within the development teams.

The role is fully remote, reporting to the Product Manager within our Payments team.

Your day to day:
• Focus on payment integrations - documenting requirements and working with suppliers and development teams to offer new payment methods, solutions, and opportunities.
• Creation and roll-out of operational documentation to support teams relating to new payment methods, features and enhancements.
• Focus on conversion with the registration process (regular and quick registration products) along with the conversion.
• Discovery: prototyping, specifications, user testing.
• Management and guidance of development process (development and QA teams) through to release including demos, user acceptance, and regression testing.
• Responsible for the user experience of the payment’s application.
• Management and control of deposit/cash-out methods offered, limits, currencies, etc via internal reports.
• Communication with payment service providers regarding new and existing products.
• Monitoring and improvement of KPIs relevant to the performance of features and payment methods.
• Coordination with Account Managers for touch points during the release cycle – post and prior to release.

• Proven experience in Payments & Risk Product roles within the iGaming industry.
• Proficiency in creating product requirements and specifications for complex products, features, and tools, utilizing various requirement formats tailored to agile environments.
• Strong understanding of Agile methodologies and experience promoting them within development teams.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including technical writing abilities.
• Demonstrated ability to focus on payment integrations, collaborating with suppliers and development teams to introduce new payment methods, solutions, and enhancements.
• Experience in managing and guiding the development process, including demos, user acceptance, and regression testing, to ensure successful releases.
• Track record of managing user experience for payment applications and coordinating with payment service providers.
• Ability to monitor and improve KPIs relevant to feature and payment method performance.
• Strong organizational skills for coordinating touch points with Account Managers during release cycles.

How we approach things:
• Dynamic Medium-Sized Environment: We have a can-do ethos, where innovation is encouraged, and action is valued.
• Core Values at Heart: We live by Teamwork, Innovation, Trust, and Integrity in everything we do.
• Results-Oriented Focus: We prioritise getting things done while supporting each other to reach both collective and individual goals.
• Open Collaboration: Our open-door policy fosters collaboration across all levels and departments, where ideas flow freely.
• Global Team: We are truly a global team with people from various countries and cultures contributing to our success.

 What we offer:
• A remote and flexible working schedule. 
• Generous time off varied based on the country of residence.
• Discretionary annual performance bonus
• Training and other learning & development opportunities to support you through your career progression.
• Hardware & Software allowance or work equipment is provided to make sure you have all the right tools to get the job done.
• Various well-being programmes and initiatives.

### Who we are

We’re building an analysis engine that helps organisations discover what is happening and why. It makes use of the evidence conventional data systems miss – from large internal text datasets to signals spread across many external sources. Our architecture combines comparative statistical inference and causal frameworks with machine learning and large language models, ensuring stable interpretation and consistent quality at scale. 

We’re backed by a specialist AI venture fund, as well as receiving EU deep-tech funding. Our team’s previous research has been cited over 35,000 times and has previously informed government and industry decision-making. We’re now working with teams across government, pharma, and other large organisations, scaling our first deployments and building the scientific foundation for what comes next. 

For too long, organisations have settled for a shallow, lagged view of the dynamics they care about. We’re changing that, helping teams uncover the drivers that matter and build understanding that improves over time. This is a hard, meaningful problem – come help us solve it. 

### What we’re looking for

We’re hiring an Applied Scientist to invent, validate and implement methods for working out what drives outcomes from unstructured evidence. You’ll explore the frontier between statistical and causal inference and large language models – designing experiments, prototyping pipelines, and collaborating with engineers to bring your best ideas into production quickly. 

You’ll work directly with our CTO – a mathematician with deep experience of turning complex data into real-world impact – and collaborate with enterprise clients to ensure our analysis is rigorous, scalable, and relevant to decision-makers. As one of our early hires, you’ll help shape Wholesum’s methodology, culture, and future. 

### About you

You’re excited by the challenge of understanding cause and effect in messy, real-world data, and have a strong background spanning statistical inference, causal inference and machine learning.

You’re excellent at pushing methodological boundaries and rapidly turning insights into well-designed Python pipelines.

Summary

Wikipedia and its sister projects are among the most popular media properties in the world, visited by over 1 billion people a month across over 300 different languages. The Wikimedia Foundation is looking for a group product manager to guide the development and evolution of our data platforms, the collection of technologies we use to understand how Wikipedia works, improve its experiences, and spread free knowledge.

The group product manager is a leader in the strategic decision-making and tactical execution for the Data Engineering, Experimentation, Search, and Data Platform Site Reliability teams. This role shares leadership responsibility with the Director of Engineering for Data Platform Engineering, and works in collaboration with data analysts, researchers, and product teams building user-facing features for reading and editing Wikipedia on the web and mobile apps. This is a people management role, managing two individually-contributing product managers.

In this role, you and your group of product managers will guide the evolution of our data pipelines, data lake, experiment platform, and analytics tools. This includes ingestion, orchestration, computation, and serving data using a variety of technologies such as Kafka, Flink, Hadoop, Spark, Airflow, Iceberg, Kubernetes, Superset, dbt, and OpenSearch. A strong candidate will have deep experience building a data platform to serve product analytics and production needs, and be technically conversant in the relevant technologies.

This position will report to the Senior Director of Product, Core Experiences.

• Ensuring the accuracy, usefulness, reliability, and accessibility of our data products

• Defining and setting priorities and roadmaps for Data Platform Engineering teams across four domains: data engineering, search, experimentation, and site reliability

• Product lifecycle management of the products, services, and tools of the Data Platform Engineering teams 

• Co-developing product strategy, providing leadership, and making and facilitating sound decisions

• Managing and developing a team of product managers

• Partnering with user-facing product teams to use the data platform to guide product decisions and build derived-data products

• Minimum of 5 years of product management experience with data or infrastructure products

• Experience hiring and managing product managers

• Success delivering data and analytical products and services depended on by multiple product teams

• Expertise in data analytics, A/B testing, search, and data architecture 

• Strong understanding of modern techniques for handling high-scale data

• Knowledge of search technologies

• Experience navigating privacy issues around data collection, retention, and distribution

• Ability to work with multiple stakeholder teams to deliver results through lateral influence and collaboration

You will own the product experience and roadmap across technical integration, catalog onboarding, data structuring, configuration, and activation. Your goal is simple: make it dramatically faster and easier for enterprise customers to get live and see value.

- Time to first value
- Activation and onboarding completion rates
- Catalog integration success
- Drop-off at different onboarding stages
- Data quality and integration reliability
- Support effort required to get customers live

You'll work closely with Engineering, Data, GTM, CSM, TSM and TSE teams, as well as directly with enterprise customers and their technical teams.

You'll also have a significant opportunity to use AI and automation to rethink how enterprise onboarding works—from catalog mapping and configuration to troubleshooting and error resolution.

Banks need flexibility in how they fund international payments, settle with Wise and convert currencies. Our Cash Management team builds the products that give them that control and make Wise work for more partners and their customers.
The problems are concrete. How can a bank lock in an exchange rate today and provide the funds later? How can it send payments first and settle with Wise afterward? We build the capabilities behind those choices, helping partners manage their cash around the needs of their business.
We’re a small, growing team developing new products in a domain with plenty to learn and shape. You’ll work closely with product managers, partner banks and engineers across Wise whose systems handle accounts, incoming payments and liquidity. Together, you’ll understand partner needs, agree how those systems fit together and turn complex requirements into practical products.

Job Description

About the role
We’re looking for a senior engineer who enjoys understanding a customer’s problem, designing a solution and taking responsibility for how it performs in production.
This is a hands-on role with substantial ownership. You’ll have the autonomy to move work forward, alongside colleagues who contribute through shared design, reviews and pairing.
You will:
• Own solutions from problem to production. Work with product managers and engineers to understand partner needs, shape the approach, and design, build, test and operate backend services.

• Make thoughtful technical decisions. Explain tradeoffs clearly and balance delivery time, reliability and maintainability, including when the information available is incomplete.

• Build across system boundaries. Work with other teams to agree clear interfaces and understand how changes affect the wider payment journey.

• Improve the systems you operate. Strengthen testing and observability, diagnose production issues, and use what you learn to make services more dependable.

• Help the team succeed. Contribute across workstreams, share domain knowledge and help other engineers grow through reviews, pairing and mentoring.

Our backend stack includes Java, Spring Boot, Kafka and PostgreSQL. You’ll deepen your understanding of funding, settlement and currency conversion, using that knowledge to make better product and engineering decisions. As the team’s scope grows, there will be opportunities to take on broader technical ownership and influence how we build.
What will you be doing?
• Design, develop, and maintain highly scalable services in Java and Spring Boot within a microservices architecture.

• Apply domain-driven design to build robust, scalable solutions.

• Lead development efforts in event-driven architectures using Kafka or similar messaging systems.

• Architect, design, and optimise relational databases (e.g., PostgreSQL) to ensure performance and scalability.

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to support partner integrations and expand the Wise payment platform globally.

• Participate in code reviews, champion best coding practices and mentor junior engineers.

Qualifications

We’re looking for:
• Hands-on experience building or making substantial contributions to large-scale distributed systems.

• Strong backend engineering experience, including relational databases, event-driven systems and proficiency in an object-oriented language.

• A product mindset: you can explain the customer problems behind your work, why your solution matters and how you assess whether it helps.

• The ability to take ownership with a high degree of autonomy, make progress through ambiguity and involve others when their expertise is needed.

We are the Global KYC and Onboarding squad in the Servicing department and we have a mission: to enable teams at Wise to expand and fine-tune the business in a "config change" manner all across the globe, while remaining compliant and safe for the customers. There are three teams in the squad: Business Onboarding Verification, Personal Onboarding Verification and Wise Platform Verification (our B2B platform).

The scale we operate at: In FY2025, 15.6 million people and businesses used Wise, we onboarded over 5.9 million new customers (~500k/month), and moved £145.2bn across borders (~£400m/day) across 160+ countries and 40+ currencies. Our verification systems aren't supporting tools — they're core production infrastructure that protects customers, enables growth, and must stay reliable under constant change in regulations, policies, and evolving threat patterns.

All of the teams are diverse, cross-functional groups passionate about solving complex problems with elegant solutions. We bring together backend and frontend engineers, mobile developers, designers, data analysts, and product managers who collaborate closely to deliver exceptional customer experiences. Our teams are responsible for the critical verification journeys that business and personal customers complete before using Wise's products. We own the entire verification lifecycle – from document collection flows and automated review systems to agent tooling and compliance monitoring. We operate with high ownership in a bottom-up, transparent culture, make data-driven decisions, and celebrate both technical excellence and customer impact. Right now we're focused on building KYC/FinCrime as a configuration-driven product, refactoring and building new scalable microservice systems, and increasing automation using ML/AI where it genuinely improves decisioning, review quality, and operational efficiency — with safe fallbacks and clear observability. As a team that touches both regulatory requirements and customer experience, we have unique opportunities to innovate in a space traditionally resistant to change.

By joining one of our teams, you'll directly impact these customers by transforming a traditionally frustrating experience into one that's fast, intuitive, and fair. We're not just building verification systems – we're removing barriers that stand between our customers and their financial freedom.

You will own the technical roadmap for your areas of ownership, ensuring they address important technical debt, reliability, scalability, and security concerns.
You will be instrumental in designing and implementing robust backend systems that provide clean APIs and interfaces to hide the internal complexity.
You will drive the integration with various risk and mitigation systems to ensure that Wise is compliant.
You will take initiative to identify and solve impactful problems both within your team and beyond, contributing to high-impact cross-team initiatives.
What we expect from you:
You have 4+ years of experience working with any language, asynchronous message queues (e.g., Kafka, RabbitMQ), and have architected and built highly scalable microservices.
A strong product mindset and a deep passion for both customer experience and regulatory compliance. 
You will prioritize work with a holistic view of the customer and business impact, making data-driven decisions to solve complex, ambiguous problems.
Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex technical and architectural concepts clearly to diverse audiences, including product managers, designers, and other engineering teams.
You demonstrate a commitment to writing clean, testable, maintainable, and highly performant code, and you are a strong advocate for best coding practices and rigorous code reviews.
Proven ability to identify and lead the technical delivery of large-scale, organisationally-complex projects, adept at anticipating and escalating organizational blockers.
Extensive experience working with relational and non-relational databases, including advanced query optimization, schema design, and data lifecycle management for sensitive information.

You’ll have deeply embedded yourself within our mission, owning and delivering quarterly goals for the team, significantly impacting our ability to scale and improve verification processes.
You’ll own the technical roadmap for your areas, ensuring it supports both immediate delivery needs and long-term strategic objectives, including addressing technical debt and improving system health.
You’ll leverage your expertise to identify the right solutions to solve ambiguous, open-ended problems, driving tough prioritization decisions that deliver clear business and customer value.

Wise is a global technology company, building the best way to move and manage the world’s money.
Min fees. Max ease. Full speed.
Whether people and businesses are sending money to another country, spending abroad, or making and receiving international payments, Wise is on a mission to make their lives easier and save them money.
As part of our team, you will be helping us create an entirely new network for the world's money.
For everyone, everywhere.
More about our mission and what we offer.
Job Description
We are the Global KYC and Onboarding squad in the Servicing department and we have a mission: to enable teams at Wise to expand and fine-tune the business in a "config change" manner all across the globe, while remaining compliant and safe for the customers. There are three teams in the squad: Business Onboarding Verification, Personal Onboarding Verification and Wise Platform Verification (our B2B platform).

The scale we operate at: In FY2025, 15.6 million people and businesses used Wise, we onboarded over 5.9 million new customers (~500k/month), and moved £145.2bn across borders (~£400m/day) across 160+ countries and 40+ currencies. Our verification systems aren't supporting tools — they're core production infrastructure that protects customers, enables growth, and must stay reliable under constant change in regulations, policies, and evolving threat patterns.

All of the teams are diverse, cross-functional groups passionate about solving complex problems with elegant solutions. We bring together backend and frontend engineers, mobile developers, designers, data analysts, and product managers who collaborate closely to deliver exceptional customer experiences. Our teams are responsible for the critical verification journeys that business and personal customers complete before using Wise's products. We own the entire verification lifecycle – from document collection flows and automated review systems to agent tooling and compliance monitoring. We operate with high ownership in a bottom-up, transparent culture, make data-driven decisions, and celebrate both technical excellence and customer impact. Right now we're focused on building KYC/FinCrime as a configuration-driven product, refactoring and building new scalable microservice systems, and increasing automation using ML/AI where it genuinely improves decisioning, review quality, and operational efficiency — with safe fallbacks and clear observability. As a team that touches both regulatory requirements and customer experience, we have unique opportunities to innovate in a space traditionally resistant to change.

By joining one of our teams, you'll directly impact these customers by transforming a traditionally frustrating experience into one that's fast, intuitive, and fair. Your code will help individuals and small businesses access global banking faster, enable entrepreneurs to pay international employees on time, and allow people like you and your teammates support their families across borders without friction. We're not just building verification systems – we're removing barriers that stand between our customers and their financial freedom.

We need like-minded engineers in all the teams in the squad, so we'll use the interview process to discover where your unique skills shine brightest. Ultimately, we want to match you with the team that perfectly aligns with your experience and sets you up for success!
As a Senior Software Engineer, you will own large-sized, impactful projects within the domain. Your responsibilities span end-to-end:
You will own the technical roadmap for your areas of ownership, ensuring they address important technical debt, reliability, scalability, and security concerns.
You will be instrumental in designing and implementing robust backend systems that provide clean APIs and interfaces to hide the internal complexity.
You will drive the integration with various risk and mitigation systems to ensure that Wise is compliant.
You will take initiative to identify and solve impactful problems both within your team and beyond, contributing to high-impact cross-team initiatives.
What we expect from you:
You have 4+ years of experience working with any language, asynchronous message queues (e.g., Kafka, RabbitMQ), and have architected and built highly scalable microservices.
A strong product mindset and a deep passion for both customer experience and regulatory compliance. 
You will prioritize work with a holistic view of the customer and business impact, making data-driven decisions to solve complex, ambiguous problems.
Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to articulate complex technical and architectural concepts clearly to diverse audiences, including product managers, designers, and other engineering teams.
You demonstrate a commitment to writing clean, testable, maintainable, and highly performant code, and you are a strong advocate for best coding practices and rigorous code reviews.
Proven ability to identify and lead the technical delivery of large-scale, organisationally-complex projects, adept at anticipating and escalating organizational blockers.
Extensive experience working with relational and non-relational databases, including advanced query optimization, schema design, and data lifecycle management for sensitive information.
What does success look like?
You’ll have deeply embedded yourself within our mission, owning and delivering quarterly goals for the team, significantly impacting our ability to scale and improve verification processes.
You’ll own the technical roadmap for your areas, ensuring it supports both immediate delivery needs and long-term strategic objectives, including addressing technical debt and improving system health.
You’ll leverage your expertise to identify the right solutions to solve ambiguous, open-ended problems, driving tough prioritization decisions that deliver clear business and customer value.
You’ll consistently define and implement technical solutions or efficient operational processes that level up your team and contribute beyond it, mentoring other engineers and sharing best practices.
You’ll inspire a high-performing team environment where ideas are shared, technical excellence is pursued, and continuous learning is embraced.

Job Description

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer II with deep systems thinking, data engineering expertise, and a product-oriented mindset to join our Treasury FX function — spanning both the Market Data and Risk Engineering teams.
Our team builds the real-time infrastructure that powers Wise's FX pricing, risk management, and trade execution. We aggregate market data from Bloomberg and Reuters, compute live exposure and VaR, execute hedges worth tens to hundreds of millions of pounds daily, and protect the business from adverse currency movements. Our systems are tier- 1 and serve 50+ internal consumers with sub-second freshness across 50+ currency pairs.
You will be the technical anchor across both engineering teams, owning the architectural direction of 14+ production services, from rate ingestion and distribution, through real-time risk calculation, to automated hedge execution. The primary mission: build Wise's first semi-automated trade and hedge execution platform in close coordination with FX dealers, quantitative researchers, and treasury controllers.
We operate on a strong belief in automation, programmatic implementation, and reusable design. We're looking for people who can step back and think holistically about the ecosystem, but also follow through and help implement the design; drawing on the resources across the rest of the Finance & Treasury tribe.
Our stack is polyglot and modern: Java 21 + Spring Boot 4.x, Python 3.12, Apache Flink (streaming), Kafka, gRPC + Protobuf, and Bloomberg/Reuters real-time feeds. This isn't typical CRUD — it's real-time financial infrastructure where a 1bps improvement in hedging efficiency saves millions.
We need a seasoned engineer who can architect streaming data pipelines, collaborate with quants on model productionisation, drive reliability across mission-critical systems, and translate complex business requirements from traders and risk managers into elegant technical solutions.
What will you be working on?
You will own the technical direction and architectural evolution of Wise's FX engineering stack, with immediate focus on:
• Architecting a semi-automated hedge execution platform, from exposure decomposition through model-driven hedge proposals to programmatic trade execution on external partners

• Building real-time streaming pipelines with Apache Flink for portfolio-split exposure computation, tenor interpolation, and hedge lifecycle event processing

• Evolving our rate infrastructure for 10x throughput with FX Forwards, new corridors, NDFs and work on cross-provider deviation alerting

• Building production infrastructure for quant models for VaR, beta-adjusted exposure management, dynamic pricing and FRP cancellations.

• Owning Kafka topology design and schema evolution across the full pipeline: rate ingestion → risk calculation → trade execution → analytics

• Driving technical roadmap across both teams, mentoring IC2/IC3 engineers, and leading incident response for Tier-1 critical services

Qualifications

We acknowledge that engineers continuously evolve their skillsets, and we are committed to supporting your growth. However, we are looking for candidates who can bring these core skills to the table:
• 8+ years of professional software engineering experience, ideally in financial systems, trading, or real-time data infrastructure

• Deep expertise in Java (17+) with Spring Boot in high-throughput production environments

• Extensive experience with Apache Kafka, topic design, schema evolution, consumer group management at scale

• Strong data engineering skills, building real-time streaming pipelines with Apache Flink, Kafka Streams, or equivalent

• Proven track record designing and operating distributed systems processing millions of events per day

• Demonstrated ability to own system reliability end-to-end: SLOs, alerting, incident response, disaster recovery

• Experience leading technical design of complex multi-service architectures and influencing without direct authority

• Exceptional product mindset — able to translate business requirements from traders, operations, and quants into technical strategy

• Track record of mentoring senior and junior engineers and raising team-wide engineering standards

The successful candidate will onboard as the technical anchor for both FX engineering teams, bringing architectural leadership and deep systems expertise while contributing to the transformative impact our platform has on Wise's FX operations.

This role works at the intersection of the Risk API platform, Product, and Financial Crime (FinCrime) teams — offering a unique opportunity to build the systems that give Wise confidence in every risk assessment it operates at scale.
You will be the driving force behind the platform's trustworthiness and integrity, focusing on:

• Auditability & Explainability: Implementing end-to-end audit trails, change history tracking, and explainability tooling that enables one-click regulatory evidence generation.

What will you be working on?
You will join the team at a pivotal moment, with your contributions being immediately visible and critical to the success of the entire Risk Assessment platform's governance layer.
The core challenge for the team — and your immediate focus — is to build the assurance and governance foundations that the platform currently lacks, ensuring every control can answer: Was the right trigger used? Was the right data available? Was the right decision made? Is the control still effective?

Your immediate impact will be to:
• Build Data Trust: Implement data quality monitoring, data contracts, and lineage tracking that give the organisation full traceability from risk decisions back to source data.

• Deliver Continuous Assurance: Design and build automated monitoring systems that continuously validate control effectiveness — detecting drift, false positives/negatives, and coverage gaps before they become incidents.

• Enable Auditability: Create audit trail infrastructure and explainability tooling that dramatically reduces the effort required for regulatory reporting and compliance evidence generation.

• Integrate with Risk API: Work closely with the Risk API team to embed governance and assurance capabilities into the core platform, ensuring clean integration points and shared data contracts.

Qualifications
What do you need?
• Strong Backend Engineering: Proven experience building high-throughput, data-intensive systems in any language. Hands-on expertise with Kafka, SQL and NoSQL databases, and designing for scale and reliability.

• Data Engineering Aptitude: Experience with data quality frameworks, pipeline orchestration, or lineage tracking. You understand what it takes to make data trustworthy at scale.

About the role

Wood Mackenzie's trading customers act on our forecasts and analytical models every day, across power, gas and oil markets. We are turning that modelling estate into a portfolio of products in its own right: versioned, documented, commercially packaged, and consumable by machines as readily as by analysts.

The Director of Modelling Products owns that portfolio. You set the strategy for what we model and why, you own the commercial case for investment across commodities, and you lead the product leads who hold each market. You will not build the models yourself and you will not own the engineers who implement them. You decide what the portfolio should contain, hold the standard it is judged against, and make the case for what we invest in next.

What you will own

• The portfolio strategy. Which models we build, rebuild, retire or acquire across power, gas and oils. You own the investment case and the sequencing, and you defend both.
• Productization of analytical assets. Moving models and their underlying features from research outputs into products, with versioning, documented methodology, reproducible outputs and a defined release cycle. This is the central program of the role.
• The modelling product leads. Senior product people holding market specific depth in their commodities. You hire them, develop them, set their objectives, and hold a consistent methodological standard across them.
• Methodology governance. One standard for validation, change control, backtesting and documentation, so that a colleague or a customer can understand what a model does and how much to trust it.
• Commercial packaging and distribution. How modelling assets reach customers: in applications, through APIs and data platforms, and as inputs to our own analysts. You work with commercial teams on pricing and packaging.
• The partnership with central engineering and modelling functions. Development capacity is provided centrally and built to your specification. You set requirements, review implementations and hold the quality bar without managing the developers.

What we are looking for

• A quantitative background you can draw on. A degree in a mathematical, engineering or scientific discipline, and real experience with linear programming, econometric or machine learning modelling. You need to be able to discuss, validate and challenge a methodology on its merits rather than take it on trust.
• Portfolio level product leadership in analytics or data. Ten years or more in product, including ownership of a multi-product portfolio and the investment tradeoffs across it.
• Experience leading product managers, including senior ones. Your leverage in this role comes through other people.
• A track record of productizing analytical or research assets. Taking work built for internal or bespoke use and turning it into something repeatable, documented and commercially viable.
• Machine consumable delivery. APIs, streaming, data platforms and workflow integration. Our customers increasingly want the model and the data rather than the report.
• Commodity or energy market context preferred. Deep subject matter expertise is not a prerequisite, since market specific depth sits with peers or the leads reporting to you. You do need enough market and commercial literacy to prioritize well.
• Comfort operating without direct control. Development, data engineering and market expertise all sit with teams you do not manage. Clear specifications, credibility and influence are how this role works.

What this role is not

• Not a modelling role. You will not be building or running models. You direct, prioritize and hold the standard.
• Not an engineering or data science management role. Those capabilities are provided by central functions.
• Not a research leadership role. Our analyst teams produce market views and commentary. You own the models they and our customers depend on.
• Not a finished portfolio. The scope will expand across commodities as the function develops.

## About the Role

## **Role Purpose**

Own the cosmetic product at Worldover.

## **About Worldover**

Worldover™ is building the AI operating system for substance-based companies. One platform that replaces the tangle of PLM, ERP, regulatory, formulation, and quality tools that chemicals, cosmetics, food, pharma, and supplements companies have stitched together over decades.

Three things make it work. Composable software blocks (CRM, SDS, PLM, ERP, compliance) that get configured to each customer instead of forcing them into a generic mould. A single customer data layer that holds every raw material, formulation, product, and packaging record in one structured home. And Willow, our chemical intelligence engine, sitting underneath every workflow with the domain knowledge to make agentic AI actually safe in regulated environments.

The platform is already live with names like HUDA Beauty, Kayali, The White Company, ICONIC London, Hallstar, and Cosmoproject. We’re backed by Index Ventures, Entrepreneur First, and Chalfen Ventures, and we’re hiring across the company as we go deeper into chemicals and expand across food, pharma, and specialty chemicals.

## **The role**

We’re hiring a Product Manager to own a product vertical at Worldover.

Cosmetics is our deepest vertical and the one we’re building out hardest right now. The platform needs a single owner for what ‘great’ looks like for a customer: which templates ship, which workflows are standard, how raw material and formulation data is structured, what Willow knows about CLP and REACH and GHS, and where the product needs to go next. That’s this job.

You’ll be the first vertical PM at Worldover. Over time we expect a small team of these, one per industry we serve, with cosmetics first and likely food next.

## **What you’ll be doing**

**Own the cosmetics template library.** 

- Build the templates; you’ll prototype / develop and then work with engineering to productionise the templates.

- Every workflow, data model, classification scheme, and document template that ships to a chemicals customer goes through you. You decide what’s in the standard library, what’s configurable per customer, and what we build next.

**Sit at the centre of the cosmetic product.** 

- Work with our product implementation team (who configure the platform for customers), engineering (who build the software blocks), and the Willow team (who own the chemical intelligence layer). Consolidate the feedback. Spot the patterns. Push for the changes that move the needle. Say no to the ones that won’t.

**Talk to customers constantly.** 

- You’ll develop the map of the various personas of the customers within the market - and how we are best able to position the product and ensure we have strong product market fit for each.

**Be the bridge between domain and product.** 

- Translate ‘this is how a senior regulatory lead at a contract manufacturer actually thinks about a new formulation’ into roadmap, specs, and shipped software.

## **Who you are**

**Product** 

- You’ve worked in product, ideally building and selling SaaS. 

**Mid-to-senior.**

- 3-5+ years across chemicals and product combined, though depth matters more than years. No people management experience required.

**Opinionated but not precious.** 

- You’ll have strong views on what cosmetics customers need. You’ll change them when the evidence says you should.

**You want to own something.** 

- This is not a role for someone who wants a defined backlog handed to them. The cosmetic product is yours to shape.

## **Why we think this role is interesting**

You’ll have unusual large leverage; through the power of our WorldMaker platform you are able to directly implement the vast majority of changes / improvements. Unlike in most organisations you are not beholden to the engineering road map - you have real power to make change yourself.

You’ll also work with one of the more interesting AI products in the enterprise space. Willow is not a wrapper around a foundation model. It’s a real chemical intelligence engine with proprietary corpus, evaluation frameworks, and a tight integration to live customer data. 

You’ll have a direct say in what it knows and how it shows up across the platform.

- Complex B2B Enterprise Software
- AI Native - you extensively use AI in your workflows

We sell a combination of database products, traditional software and AI agents to deliver what we call the operating system for chemicals.

**Background**

The software factory for chemicals.

Re-building the entire software stack for 9% of global GDP.

_Us: ‘Why does your existing software stack not work very well for you guys?’_

_Customer: ‘Because we are ingredient based and none of the software we use actually takes this into account.’_

Traditional enterprise software does not work for substance based businesses. Chemicals and ingredient based companies require a unique data model and ontology that accurately reflects how they create their products. Without this, none of their software really works.

The team at Worldover spent years building regulatory products in chemicals and this gave us the insight and capability to create the foundational layer chemicals. Immediately, our customers began asking if we could replace other elements of their software.

We combined this ontological layer with our own coding agent to create a true software factory that re-builds, replaces or implements for the first time a true operating system for substance based businesses.

We were described in our funding round as ‘the most aggressive implementation of a software factory manifesto I’ve ever seen.’ We are pushing agentic coding to the limits and you must be excited about that prospect to want to work here.

This operating system is based on four layers:

1. Correct ontology for chemicals - ingredient and regulatory databases.

2. Customer data layer.

3. Workflow software - think CRM, ERP, MRP, QMS etc all rolled into one.

4. Intelligence and agentic layer on top - insights and automation but only after steps 1-3 have been completed.

Chemicals is massive and it represents almost 9% of global GDP. We are well placed to win this market and build a truly generational company in this space.

We are looking for a hands-on Senior Data Product Manager who can turn ambiguous business problems into viable data-product opportunities. You will combine product judgement, analytical problem-solving, and technical prototyping to test ideas quickly, establish value, and lead selected products through development, launch, and ongoing improvement.

This is an individual-contributor role for someone comfortable moving between business problems, data, technology, and product delivery. You will not simply write requirements for others. You will explore data, build working prototypes, challenge assumptions, and create the evidence needed to determine whether and how a product should be scaled. This is a 12-month FTC opportunity, based in London, with a hybrid working arrangement requiring 2 days in the office per week. The standard working week is 35 hours.

The Role:

Product discovery and problem definition

- Work with business stakeholders and domain specialists to understand decisions, workflows, pain points, and opportunities that could be addressed through data products.
- Convert broad or ambiguous challenges into clear problem statements, target users, desired outcomes, hypotheses, and measurable product objectives.
- Assess product opportunities based on business value, user need, data readiness, technical feasibility, scalability, and alignment with the broader data-product portfolio.
- Identify when a request should become a reusable product and when a simpler analytical or process solution is more appropriate.

Developer Relations Lead

Zenrows is the web data infrastructure for AI. Founded in 2021, we give developers, AI agents and businesses one reliable way to access, extract and structure data from any website, at any scale, however hard the site tries to block them.

 

Whether it’s an agent that needs fresh web context mid-task, an LLM application grounded in live data, or an enterprise pipeline pulling millions of pages a day, Zenrows handles the rendering, the anti-bot defences and the parsing behind a single API, 10B+ requests a month. Teams at more than 10,000 companies, including Microsoft, Amazon, Dell, IBM, Slack, eBay, EY, Nokia and Clay, rely on Zenrows to turn the web into a reliable source of data for their products, workflows and AI-driven applications, across e-commerce, finance, real estate and AI.

As we continue our rapid expansion, we are now looking for our first Developer Relations Engineer to join us on a permanent basis, make an instant impact and build our DevRel function from the ground up.

 

The Role

Nobody has ever done this job at Zenrows and that’s the exciting part! You’ll be our founding DevRel, which means there’s no playbook or legacy processes to inherit, and nobody telling you how it should be done. You get a blank canvas, real ownership and the freedom to build and scale the function from scratch the way you think it should be built.

 

What You’ll do

• Working alongside our GTM team, you’ll combine your technical advocacy and community skills to build credibility and help developers discover, experiment with, and integrate Zenrows. Ultimately adoption is the goal and success will be measured on that. We want Zenrows to be a name everyone recognises.

• As the face of Zenrows, you’ll be out there in the real world. You’ll give talks, run technical workshops, and collaborate with relevant developer communities. You’ll also own our hackathon programme. Which ones we sponsor, where we speak, and being there on the day, talking to the people building cool things with our tools.

• Engaging with the online community is equally as important. When you’re back at your desk, you’ll drive discussions where developers already hang out, such as Reddit, X and Discord. You’ll create videos, demo content, templates and sample apps, plus open-source projects, GitHub contributions, starter kits and developer integrations. You’ll  show developers what’s possible with Zenrows and get them experimenting. 

• This role is as much about listening as it is about telling. Taking what you’ve learned, you’ll also handle the feedback loop between the community and the product and engineering teams.

• Zenrows already integrates with hundreds of tools that developers love. Our goal is simple and ambitious: make Zenrows part of every agentic developer’s stack.

 

What We’re Looking For

Nobody is equally brilliant at everything. We’ll lean into your strengths and grow the function from there.

• You’re technical, first and foremost. You don’t need to be a hard core developer but you can write Python, JavaScript or similar. You’re comfortable with APIs/SDK, AI agents and can build demos, apps and integrations with the product yourself. 

• You’ve got demonstrable technical and community-building experience. You’re confident on camera and the stage, and have a public body of work you’re proud of. We’d love to see your videos, talks, demos, repos or posts.

• You have a track record of running events, talks or community initiatives. We want someone whose passion is clear and is active in AI/agent developer ecosystems such as GitHub, Reddit, Discord, Hacker News, Stack Overflow.

• You’ve built developer ecosystems, open-source initiatives or technical communities from scratch, and you know how to get noticed without a big brand or logo behind you.

• You measure success in impact, not just reach. You’re driven by API integrations, open-source adoption, and community engagement converting into active customers

• Being the only person in the function excites you rather than scares you! In the end, this is yours to own and you’ll need to be comfortable making big decisions and running with them. 

• You’re a skilled technical writer. Documentation is mainly owned by engineering but you’ll also be expected to contribute in time

 

Bonus points if:

• You already have an audience of your own. Perhaps a newsletter, a YouTube channel or a strong following on X.

• You’ve organised a hackathon (or won one!).

 

Why You Will Love Working Here

• We have a CEO who values world class talent over everything else. Trust and respect is earned and with it comes reward and recognition like nowhere else.

Summary

Zeroth Research is a UK-based nonprofit research organisation dedicated to advancing AI safety through mathematical and computational methods. A guardrail that works and a guardrail nobody can lie about are two different things. You would build the second. You will own the engineering that takes Zero-Knowledge Model Checking from a research prototype to usable infrastructure. Our goal is a production-grade, open-source demonstrator by mid-2027.

The Opportunity

Formal verification can establish that a system satisfies a safety specification across all possible scenarios. Conventionally, however, the system must be disclosed to whoever verifies it.

Zero-Knowledge Model Checking (ZKMC) removes that requirement. A system-holder can prove that a secret system satisfies a public temporal specification without revealing the system itself. The result is a portable certificate that anyone can verify in milliseconds, cryptographically bound to the system actually deployed.

Consider a content-moderation pipeline: its operator could prove compliance with public safety rules without disclosing its proprietary filtering logic.

We are now extending this approach to zero-knowledge runtime monitoring and model checking under two-sided secrecy, where even the auditor’s criteria remain confidential.

Developed in close collaboration with the University of Birmingham and international research partners, this work brings together frontier research in cryptography and formal methods with practical systems engineering.

This position is funded by ARIA, the UK’s Advanced Research and Invention Agency, through its Safeguarded AI programme, which aims to build AI systems with verifiable, quantitative safety guarantees. It offers the opportunity to join the programme as a Creator, becoming part of ARIA’s community of researchers and engineers working towards this goal.

The Role

You will own the engineering that takes ZKMC from a research prototype to usable infrastructure, translating advances in cryptography and formal verification into correct, efficient, production-grade software.

This is not a role where you simply implement specifications handed down by researchers. You will make architectural decisions, challenge assumptions, identify what is computationally feasible and contribute to the design and evaluation of new protocols.

We work in the open. Code is published, performance is measured, and benchmarks are released whether or not they flatter us.

We welcome candidates at different levels of seniority. What matters most is what you have built, how you approach difficult engineering problems, and the judgement you bring to them.

Essential Qualifications

- Hands-on experience with zero-knowledge proof systems, such as arkworks, Halo2, Plonky3, or comparable frameworks

- A track record of translating research papers, formal specifications or theoretical protocols into working, tested implementations

Desired Qualifications

- Background in formal methods, particularly temporal logic, automata, model checking or runtime verification
- Experience maintaining open-source projects or building software that other developers depend on

You do not need to meet every desirable qualification. We are particularly interested in people who can move confidently between mathematical ideas and practical systems engineering.

Responsibilities

- Turn ZKMC into infrastructure. Develop a usable API, a specification front end and commitment verification tied to a running system. Build a library that others can use and extend.
- Make proving practical. Improve proving performance through folding and succinctness, balancing efficiency, complexity and security.

- Build the demonstrator end to end. Integrate the proving pipeline, agent harness, runtime monitor, verifier client and audit path into a working system.
- Measure and optimise. Profile the prover, identify bottlenecks and improve performance using reproducible benchmarks.

Summary

Zeroth Research is a UK-based nonprofit research organisation dedicated to advancing AI safety through mathematical and computational methods. We are hiring two Machine Learning Engineers with complementary backgrounds: one to develop training procedures for neural certificates, and one to build LLM-based generation methods for proof search. Our goal is a production-grade, open-source demonstrator by mid-2027.

The Opportunity

For decades, proof search for system verification has relied primarily on symbolic algorithms. Machine learning now opens up new possibilities.

Formally verifying that a system meets its safety and security specifications means producing machine-checkable artefacts that together constitute a formal proof. At Zeroth Research, we have developed specialised proof tactics for verifying a wide range of systems. These tactics reduce proof search to the search for certificates, such as Lyapunov functions, supermartingale certificates and inductive invariants.

Our tactics define the conditions a valid certificate must satisfy. What’s missing is an efficient way to find these certificates at scale. We are exploring two approaches: learning neural certificates directly, in the style of reinforcement learning, and generating certificates as symbolic expressions using large language models.

Both positions are funded by ARIA, the UK’s Advanced Research and Invention Agency, through its Safeguarded AI programme, which aims to build AI systems with verifiable, quantitative safety guarantees. They offer the opportunity to join the programme as a Creator, becoming part of ARIA’s community of researchers and engineers working towards this goal.

The Roles

You will own the machine learning side of certificate synthesis, including loss design, sampling strategies, counterexample-guided search and network architecture.

This is not a role where you simply tune hyperparameters of a fixed method. You will design experiments, propose and test training procedures, challenge existing approaches and develop alternative solutions when necessary.

We work in the open. Code is published, performance is measured, and benchmarks are released whether or not they flatter us.

We welcome candidates at different levels of seniority. What matters most is what you have built, how you approach difficult engineering problems, and the judgement you bring to them.

Neural Certificate Learning

We are especially interested in candidates with one of two backgrounds:

- Reinforcement learning. Supermartingale conditions are Bellman-type inequalities, and learning a controller together with its certificate is constrained policy optimisation. You bring experience in value learning, actor-critic methods, exploration and making unstable training converge.
- Structured learning, such as graph neural networks. Many of our systems have explicit structure, including stochastic Petri nets, networks of interacting components and automata. You bring architectures and training methods that exploit this structure, including message passing, equivariance and generalisation across system sizes.

In this role you will:

- Make training scale. Design loss functions, sampling schemes and network architectures that exploit the structure of the problem.
- Co-train controllers and certificates. Learn policies alongside the certificates that prove them correct, understanding when the two objectives conflict.

In addition to the essential qualifications below, you will have at least one of:

- Hands-on experience with deep reinforcement learning beyond running existing baselines, including policy-gradient, actor-critic or value-based methods.
- Hands-on experience with neural networks that exploit problem structure, such as graph neural networks.

Language-based Certificate Generation

- LLM-based generation. Many certificates, such as Lyapunov functions or inductive invariants, have compact symbolic forms. A language model proposes candidate formulas, a formal verifier checks them, and any counterexamples feed back to the model so it can refine its next attempt. You bring experience building LLM systems beyond prompting, including fine-tuning, search over generations and learning from verifier or execution feedback.
- Syntactic search. Certificates can also be found by searching directly over the space of expressions, using genetic algorithms, evolutionary methods or other program-synthesis techniques, sometimes with an LLM acting as a smart mutation or proposal operator. You bring experience with search methods that generate, combine and refine structured outputs against an external checker.

In this role you will:

- Generate symbolic certificates. Develop methods in which language models propose candidate certificates and refine them using verifier counterexamples.
- Bring agents into proof construction. Enable AI agents to participate efficiently in building formal proofs using Zeroth Research’s verification infrastructure.

In addition to the essential qualifications below, you will have hands-on experience building LLM systems beyond prompting, including fine-tuning, search over generations or learning from verifier or execution feedback.
